# THE TAIL BELONGED TO THE CONSTANT. TIGHTENING IT REMOVED THE EXPOSURE — AND THE REFERENCE'S JOB.

*2026-10-19*

## PART A — THE CONSTANT TIGHTENED

> Raising the minimum margin accommodates a wrong constant. Fixing the
> constant removes the exposure.

The 12:00 weekday constant was the fallback on **1087 of 1090 days** and sat
**two and a half hours** laxer than our own measured earliest kickoff. That gap
was the whole exposure tail.

### THE MEASURED EARLIEST KICKOFF

`measured` 2026-10-19, production `matches`, the 30 **configured** leagues,
phantom exclusion applied, n=1090 days over 2022-07-05 … 2026-10-19:

| stratum | n | **MIN** | p01 | p05 | p50 | <10:00 | <11:00 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| weekday | 715 | **09:30** | 10:45 | 13:00 | 17:00 | 2 | 9 |
| weekday/ordinary | 693 | **09:30** | 11:00 | 14:00 | 17:00 | 2 | 7 |
| weekday/holiday | 22 | 10:15 | 10:15 | 10:30 | 13:00 | 0 | 2 |
| weekend | 375 | **09:45** | 10:00 | 10:15 | 11:30 | 1 | 96 |
| weekend/ordinary | 373 | **09:45** | 10:00 | 10:15 | 11:30 | 1 | 96 |
| weekend/holiday | 2 | 13:00 | 13:00 | 13:00 | 13:00 | 0 | 0 |

**THE HOLIDAY STRATUM IS NOT THE EARLIEST ONE, and the earlier analysis implied
it was.** Holidays shift the whole weekday distribution forward (p50 13:00
against 17:00) but the **minimum is an ordinary Thursday**: 2023-10-26 09:30,
`bulgaria/efbet-league`. Then 09:59 (2026-06-18, `finland/veikkausliiga`), then
10:15 (Easter Monday 2026). Both observed minima also moved **earlier** than
the 2026-10-10 figures (09:59 → 09:30, 10:00 → 09:45), because a minimum is a
function of its window and a longer window can only lower it.

### THE READY TIME, EACH DAY TYPE FROM ITS OWN SERIES

Which is what `0 4` got wrong by borrowing the other's spread:

| day type | lateness (attributed by headSha) | duration (by day type) | ready max | ready mean+3sd | **BINDING** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| weekday | n=7 max 305 mean+3sd 417.5 | n=78 max 100.8 m+3sd 100.9 | 06:45 | 08:38 | **08:38** |
| weekend | n=6 max 294 mean+3sd 334.5 | n=34 max 129.2 m+3sd 148.8 | 07:02 | 08:03 | **08:03** |

Lateness is attributed per run by its own `headSha` cron — pooling regimes
reads a `37 9` start as 21 hours late. Duration is **not** cron-dependent, so
it is pooled across regimes and split by day type: better powered (n=78/34
against n=10) and more conservative (weekday mean+3sd 100.9 against 59.4 for
the current regime alone). **The audit's prospective margin was using one
pooled duration list for both day types; it now uses each day type's own** —
the weekend's spread is half again as wide.

**CAVEAT, STATED:** the binding figure is a mean+3sd projection on a lateness
series of **n=7 / n=6**, exceeding the observed max by 112 / 40 minutes. The
floor is therefore **re-derivable and will move earlier** as the series grows.
Re-derive it; do not defend it.

### THE DERIVATION, AN ARITHMETIC AND NOT A CHOICE

    floor = ceil_to_15min( ready_binding + MIN_ACCEPTABLE_MARGIN_MIN )

the tightest value the measured pipeline supports while clearing the
pre-registered 60. Tighter is safer against an unobserved early kickoff —
the only thing a fallback is for — and the margin requirement is what stops it
going lower.

| day type | floor | margin | worst-case exposure |
|---|---|---|---|
| weekday | **09:45** | +66.6m | 15m |
| weekend | **09:15** | +71.7m | **0m** |

**AND THE WEEKDAY CANNOT HAVE BOTH, BY 8.4 MINUTES.** Zero exposure needs
`floor ≤ 09:30`; a 60-minute margin needs `floor ≥ 09:38`. The window is empty.
**The alternative not taken:** `floor = observed minimum` maximises the margin
among zero-exposure choices (weekend 09:45, +101.7m) — rejected because the
observed minimum is a bound for the *measured window* and nothing more, and the
derived floor already sits 30 minutes below it.

The fallback moved to its **own symbol**, `DEADLINE_FLOOR`.
`DEADLINE_PERCENTILES` is kept under its own name as the historical percentile
record and is no longer the fallback: a symbol named "percentiles" holding a
derived floor is the labelling defect Part B is about.

### THE RECOMPUTED EXPOSURE — TARGET MET

| constants | exposure>0 | p99 | max | **>60m** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12:00 / 10:15 | 21 days | 45m | 150m | **8 days** |
| **09:45 / 09:15** | **1 day** | **0m** | **15m** | **ZERO** |

Per stratum under the floor: weekday/ordinary max 15m (the single 2023-10-26),
weekday/holiday **0**, weekend/ordinary **0**, weekend/holiday **0**. **Zero
days above 60 minutes on every stratum.**

The term stays at zero and is **still printed** —
`residual[... p99=0m max=15m over60=0/715d -> effective minimum 60m = 60m
registered + 0m p99 ...]`. A term that disappears when it is satisfied cannot
be seen to have been satisfied. The pre-registered 60 is unedited; the
effective minimum collapses back onto it because the p99 is now zero.

### THE ALERT RATE: ZERO ADDITIONAL

`measured` by replaying all 1090 days with each day's own
`min(covered-league minimum, floor)` and each day type's own binding ready:

| basis | alarms | per week |
|---|---|---|
| current 12:00 / 10:15 | 0 | 0.000 |
| **derived 09:45 / 09:15** | **0** | **0.000** |
| discovered card under `0 0` | 1 in 1090 days | 0.0045 |
| *discovered card under `0 4`* (the recorded baseline) | *23 in 235 days* | *0.69* |

**Zero additional alerts, and eight fewer days above the 60-minute budget.**
The 0.69/wk figure belongs to the `0 4` regime; the revert to `0 0` is what
removed it, not this.

In the audit the trailing-window margins become **weekday +47m** (was +182m)
and **weekend +106m** (was +166m), both clearing the 30-minute threshold, and
the **TRIGGER switches from weekend to weekday**. The prospective margin reads
**+67m** against the registered 60.

### THE 8-MINUTE SHORTFALL THAT NO FLOOR REMOVES

`60 + max exposure` is 75m and the measured margin is 67m. So on the single
worst day in the record — 2023-10-26, truth 09:30 against a 09:45 floor — the
margin **against the true first kickoff** is `570 − 518.4 = 51.6m`, **8.4
minutes short of the registered 60**. It is the same 8.4 minutes the derivation
found, it is not removable by any choice of floor, and the only remedies are an
**earlier cron** or a **faster run** — neither of which is a deadline question.
One day in 715, asserted rather than rounded away.

### AND IT REMOVED THE REFERENCE'S JOB

`measured` 2026-10-19: the earliest kickoff in **any** of the 9 covered leagues
over the whole record is **10:00**. Both floors sit below it, so the reference's
minimum is never lower than the floor: **it binds on 0 of 834 days** carrying a
covered fixture (it bound on 3 under the old percentiles).

> **Fixing the constant did not merely remove the exposure. It removed the
> coverage gap's path to the deadline, and with it the reference's
> contribution.**

What the reference still does is **independent monitoring** — the only outside
check that the floor is not absurd, and it would bind the day a covered league
schedules before 09:45. The `min()` property stays asserted, driven
synthetically, because a property currently unexercised in production is still
what makes consulting an incomplete source safe at all. Easter Monday's
15-minute coverage error is still measured, and now **cannot reach the answer**.

**NOT A COHORT EVENT:** the deadline is read only by margin reporting and
alerting. No pick, price or probability depends on it.

## PART B — THE FOLD COUNT, LABELLED

### THE CLEAN HARNESS: 2 EFFECTIVE OF 5

`run_market` skips a cutoff when `len(train) < 300`. `measured` against the
population as it stood for the recorded 2026-08-07 run:

| cutoff | train | ran? |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-08-01 | **0** | skipped, EMPTY TRAIN |
| 2025-11-01 | **0** | skipped, EMPTY TRAIN |
| 2026-02-01 | **0** | skipped, EMPTY TRAIN |
| 2026-05-01 | 1,401 | ran |
| 2026-07-01 | 2,258 | ran |

**2 of 5, and they are ADJACENT** — the real span is 2026-05-01 … 2026-08-07,
**about one quarter**, not the twelve months five chronological cutoffs imply.
Clean odds coverage only begins 2026-02. The reconstruction cross-checks at
**2,671** rows against that run's own manifest of **2,700 qualified** — a
29-row agreement, and an upper bound, which is the safe direction: an upper
bound of zero *is* zero.

**Does any recorded figure state it? NO.** `baseline-*.json` records `cutoffs`,
`window_days` and `n_shared_matches`; **`clean-20260807.json` records none of
them** — its manifest states the population in detail and nothing about folds.
And `docs/stage4-clean-baseline-2026-08-07.md` stated the count **wrongly**:
"Walk-forward, **five chronological cutoffs**". Corrected in place, with the
table and the cross-check, under a dated marker.

### AND THE SAME DEFECT IS IN THE DECISIVE TEST

`docs/predictive-audit-2026-08-07.md` records "Five cutoffs … 5,771
out-of-sample matches (1,710 with bookmaker prices)". The five are right for
the 5,771. They are **wrong for the 1,710 priced** matches that every
blend-sweep figure is computed over:

| cutoff | OOS | carrying a 1X2 price |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-08-01 | 1,035 | **0** |
| 2025-11-01 | 1,514 | **0** |
| 2026-02-01 | 2,099 | 845 |
| 2026-05-01 | 956 | 872 |
| 2026-07-01 | 630 | 414 |

**3 effective folds of 5, spanning about six months**, all inside the
odds-collection era. (Totals 6,234 / 2,131 here against the recorded 5,771 /
1,710 — the difference is the exclusion filter and a looser "has a price"
definition; the **zeros** are structural.) Annotated in place.

### IS TWO ENOUGH? STATED, NOT ASSUMED

Both bootstraps resample **observations**, so their intervals stand as given
for their populations — 926 and 1,710 matched observations respectively. What
adjacent folds inside a single odds-collection era **cannot** support is
**temporal generality**, and the recommendation drawn from the second
(`bookmaker_blend_weight` → 1.0) is a **standing configuration claim**, which
is exactly the kind that needs it. So: adequate for the stated intervals,
inadequate for the generality the wording implies.

**No figure moves. No re-run. `BASELINE_REVISION` stays `b2`** and the three
snapshots keep `b1.unstamped-pre-exclusion`. Going forward the harness returns
`effective_folds` / `requested_folds` / `folds_ran` / `folds_skipped` with the
scores — travelling inside each score dict like `_losses` — and `show()`
**raises** rather than print a table without them. The skip reason
distinguishes `EMPTY TRAIN` from `train<300`, because one says the window is
thin and the other says it does not exist.

## PART C — FIRST RESULT, SIZED (REPORT ONLY)

### SITE 1 — `/teams?search=` → `teams_resp[0]`, no name or country check

`measured` 2026-10-19: **1,375 of 1,467** teams carry an `apifootball_team_id`.
**How many came from this path is UNRECORDED** — `Team` has no provenance
column — and the last 12 `daily-picks` runs show **zero** "Resolved N team IDs
via /teams?search" lines. So the population at risk is **bounded above by
1,375 and cannot be enumerated**; by this project's own rule it is not cited as
a count. *An entity whose origin is unrecorded cannot be audited*, and that is
the finding.

### SITE 2 — `_geocode` → `results[0]`

Two different fallbacks: with a country hint it fetches 3 and prefers a country
match (reason on file: Dunfermline resolving to Illinois); with **no** hint it
fetches **one** and uses it unconditionally. `measured`: **27 of 30** configured
leagues carry a hint. The 3 that do not are the **pan-European** competitions,
where a single country hint would be *wrong by construction* — so **251
(venue, league) pairs, 419 fixtures, 184 distinct venues** resolve with no
verification at all.

### THE SPOT-CHECKS, EACH WITH ITS DRAW RULE STATED BEFORE THE RESULT

| sample | rule | result |
|---|---|---|
| N=12 | the most frequent venues | **0 wrong** |
| N=12 | the least frequent venues in the 3 pan-European leagues | **1 wrong, 2 unresolvable** |

The first sample answered a different question than it looked like: Open-Meteo
ranks by population, and **every one of those 12 had US homonyms ranked below
it** — London/CA+US, Athens/US, Stockholm/US, Vienna/US, Glasgow/US. The draw
rule I pre-committed to was biased toward the easy cases, so rather than
re-draw it a **second sample was taken from the tail with its own rule stated
first**. Re-drawing the first would have been fishing; drawing a second,
declared, is not.

**THE ONE WRONG RESULT: `'Bar'` → Qionghai, CN** (19.242, 110.464, population
528,238) while **Bar, Montenegro** (42.094, 19.098) ranks **fourth**. 94
degrees apart. Measured effect on that fixture's features for 2026-10-22:

| feature | results[0] (CN) | correct (ME) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `weather_temp_c` | 29.3 | 19.7 | **+9.6** |
| `weather_precip_mm` | 7.2 | 17.8 | **−10.6** |
| `weather_wind_kmh` | 12.4 | 12.6 | −0.2 |
| `weather_is_raining` | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `weather_is_windy` | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Both continuous features move materially; both binary flags happen to agree on
that date. `'Biisen'` and `'Hajvalia'` return **no** results and fall to
`_DEFAULTS` with `weather_available: 0` — the honest outcome.

**Report only.** Fixing either site changes feature values, which is a cohort
event and belongs with the 11-01 queue.

## THE ENTRY

> **An accommodation and a repair look identical in the margin and opposite in
> the record.** Raising the minimum to 135 minutes would have cleared every
> check while leaving a constant two and a half hours laxer than the data;
> tightening the constant to 09:45 cleared the same checks, removed eight days
> of exposure, cost zero additional alerts — and revealed that the reference I
> wired yesterday now contributes nothing to the deadline at all.

## DECLARATION

**CONSTANT TIGHTENED.** Derived, not chosen:
`floor = ceil_15(ready_binding + 60 registered)`, each day type from its own
lateness and duration series — **weekday 09:45** (+66.6m margin, 15m worst
exposure) and **weekend 09:15** (+71.7m, **0m**). Measured minima re-measured
over the full record and both moved earlier (09:59 → **09:30**, 10:00 →
**09:45**); **the holiday stratum is not the earliest one**, an ordinary
Thursday is. **RECOMPUTED EXPOSURE: >60m on ZERO days, every stratum** — from
8 of 715 weekday days — with the term kept at **zero and still printed** and
the pre-registered 60 unedited. **ALERT RATE 0.000/wk → 0.000/wk: zero
additional**, against a 0.69/wk baseline that belonged to the `0 4` regime.
**Weekday zero-exposure and a 60-minute margin are unreachable together by 8.4
minutes**, so the worst day in the record carries a **51.6m true margin**, 8
short of the registered 60 — remediable only by an earlier cron or a faster
run, and asserted so it cannot be rounded away. **And the reference now binds
on 0 of 834 days**: fixing the constant removed the coverage gap's path to the
deadline and reduced the reference to independent monitoring, which is stated
rather than quietly left in place.

**FOLD COUNT LABELLED.** The clean harness ran **2 effective folds of 5**, both
adjacent, spanning **one quarter** — three cutoffs had an **entirely empty**
training set. **No recorded figure stated it**, and
`docs/stage4-clean-baseline-2026-08-07.md` stated it **wrongly** as "five
chronological cutoffs"; corrected in place with the table and a 2,671-vs-2,700
cross-check. **The same defect is in the decisive test**: the predictive
audit's **1,710 priced** matches rest on **3 folds of 5** (two windows carry
zero priced matches) while it records five — annotated, and the standing
`bookmaker_blend_weight` → 1.0 recommendation named as what rests on it.
Adequate for the stated intervals, **inadequate for temporal generality**.
The harness now returns the effective count with every score and `show()`
**refuses to print a table without it**. No figure moved; `b2` holds.

**FIRST-RESULT SIZED.** Site 1 `/teams?search=`: **1,375 of 1,467** teams carry
an id, the share from the unverified path is **unrecordable** (no provenance
column, zero resolutions in the last 12 runs) and so is reported as a bound,
not a count. Site 2 `_geocode`: **419 fixtures across 184 venues** in the 3
pan-European leagues resolve on `results[0]` with no verification, because a
country hint would be wrong there by construction. **Spot-checks: 0 wrong of 12
at the head, 1 wrong of 12 at the tail** — `'Bar'` → **Qionghai, China**, 94
degrees from Bar, Montenegro, worth **+9.6 °C and −10.6 mm** on that fixture's
features — with the head sample's bias toward easy cases stated rather than
hidden, and the tail sample drawn under its own pre-stated rule rather than by
re-drawing the first.

Gating suite **2152 passed, 6 deselected**. Non-gating **6 passed, 0 skipped**.
Invariants pass, count not cited. Fingerprint **UNCHANGED** at `s5.18` /
`stage5_baseline_20260807.51fbcb`; `BASELINE_REVISION` **UNCHANGED** at `b2`.

# 88 MINUTES IS NOT THE FLOOR, AND THE WEATHER FEATURES REACH NOTHING

*2026-10-20*

## PART A — DURATION PROFILED

The margin has been attacked from the cron five times and from the deadline
twice. Duration had never been decomposed.

**METHOD, stated.** GitHub's job API gives exact per-**step** boundaries.
Inside a step the only timestamps are loguru's, so each log line's elapsed gap
to the next is charged to the `module:function` that emitted the earlier line.
That measures time spent in **or waiting after** each emitter. It cannot see
time inside a call that logs nothing — that appears as a large gap on whatever
logged last, and those are **named** below rather than hidden.

**n=3 profiled runs.** The `67.4–88.1` time-to-picks figure is **n=4 from
2026-10-01** and is a **different population**. The two are not pooled.

| phase | 10-20 (34 fx) | 10-19 (13 fx) | 10-18 (65 fx) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **run total** | **56.9** | **48.5** | **68.8** |
| `--update` | **24.7 (43.4%)** | **24.1 (49.7%)** | **32.9 (47.8%)** |
| ·· AF fixtures-by-date | 7.2 (n=6) | 3.7 (n=6) | 10.1 (n=7) |
| ·· injury scraper | 6.9 (n=3) | 3.6 (n=3) | 9.7 (n=3) |
| ·· xG backfill | 2.9 | 9.0 | — |
| ·· Flashscore fixtures | 2.7 (n=90) | 3.0 (n=90) | 2.3 (n=90) |
| ·· team resolution | 1.3 | 0.3 | 7.1 |
| **picks step** | **11.3 (19.9%)** | **5.4 (11.2%)** | **21.1 (30.6%)** |
| ·· Claude review `_briefing_for` | 4.9 (n=33) | 2.0 (n=13) | 9.5 (n=65) |
| ·· `analyze_fixture` | 2.9 | 1.3 | 4.9 |
| ·· **weather fetch** | **1.6 (14.2%)** | **0.9 (15.7%)** | **3.1 (14.6%)** |
| ·· `_save_picks` | 0.6 | 0.4 | 1.1 |
| ML retrain | — | — | 5.6 |
| tests | 2.9 | 3.2 | 2.1 |
| Flashscore **RESULTS** (post-picks) | 14.1 | 11.2 | 4.0 |

**TIME-TO-PICKS** — the run minus everything after the picks step —
is **42.3 / 36.9 / 64.3 min**. The 11–14 minute results scrape runs **after**
picks and does not count against the deadline at all. Note these are **below**
the registered `FULL_CARD_PICKS_MAX = 88.1`, so that bound is conservative and
possibly stale; it is **not** edited here (rule 4: profiling changes nothing).

**PER-FIXTURE RATES**, which is where the shape lives:

| phase | per fixture | stability |
|---|---|---|
| Claude review | **~9 s** | 8.7 / 9.1 / 8.7 — strikingly stable |
| injuries | **14–20 s** | budget-capped at 30 requests |
| weather | **~3 s** | 2.9 / 4.6 / 3.2 |

### SERIAL BY NECESSITY, OR BY ACCIDENT

* **Flashscore** — one Selenium browser over 30 leagues. **BY NECESSITY.**
* **injury scraper** — its own comment reads *"the sequential API+DB loop"*,
  and the cap is a **request budget** (30), not a concurrency limit. The count
  is provider-bound; the **serialisation is by accident**. 9.7 min for 30
  fixtures is ~19 s each, which for a single HTTP call means the DB write sits
  inside the loop.
* **Claude review** — `for match_id in fixtures: await self._briefing_for(...)`.
  **BY ACCIDENT**, with cost and rate-limit consequences any fix must weigh.
* **weather** — one call per fixture inside `create_features`. **BY ACCIDENT**,
  and moot: Part B shows it reaches nothing.
* **AF fixtures-by-date** — the 9.2-minute gap follows the
  `AF_LEAGUE_FILTER … rejected 1241 fixture(s) across 337 untracked leagues`
  line, so the time is in the **per-fixture upsert loop**, not the HTTP call.
  DB-bound, **BY ACCIDENT**.

### WHAT IS REDUCIBLE, WITH THE ARITHMETIC

> **88 minutes is not the floor, and the 8.4-minute residual is reducible.**

* **weather: 3.1 min on a full card, for a producer that reaches nothing.**
  Removing it is not an optimisation — it is deleting a producer with no
  consumer. **That alone is 3.1 of the 8.4 minutes.**
* **injuries: 9.7 min on a full card, serial by accident.** Even four-way
  concurrency inside the same request budget recovers ~7 min.

Either one covers the shortfall; together they cover it three times over. **So
the cron is NOT the only remaining lever**, and the finding that goes to Niki
is the opposite of the one this stage was braced for. **Nothing was changed:**
profiling and optimising are separate stages, and the second needs the first's
numbers to be honest.

## PART B — GEOCODER SIZED, AND THE EXPOSURE IS NIL

### WEATHER REACHES NOTHING — MEASURED, WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL

* **training skips it by construction.** `create_features(for_training=True)`
  documents *"skip external API calls (weather, news)"* and the weather block
  sits behind `if not for_training:`. So weather is in **no fit** — confirmed
  on both shipped pickles: **111 feature names, ZERO weather.**
* **inference drops it.** The live path *does* compute weather, but
  `_align_features` selects by the **fitted** names. Measured on the real
  fitted set: 117 input columns → 111 aligned, and a **−40 °C / 400 mm /
  300 km/h** fixture aligns **identically** to a 19.7 °C one. **Negative
  control:** perturbing a *fitted* column **does** change the aligned vector,
  so the mechanism is not inert and the equality is not vacuous.
  *(A first attempt loaded the pickle through the HMAC-gated loader, which
  refused under the dev key and reported an UNFITTED model — three identical
  predictions for the wrong reason. That result was discarded, not used.)*
* **no other consumer.** `weather_*` appears nowhere in `src/reporting/`,
  `src/betting/` or `src/models/` — not the briefing, not the value
  calculator. The only outside mention is `ensemble.py`'s comment justifying
  the 40% bookmaker weight because the bookmaker sees *"weather, sharp money"*
  that **our model doesn't see** — which turns out to be literally true.

> **So realised harm from a wrong venue is ZERO — measured, not inferred from
> the mechanism's severity.** A wrong temperature in a feature vector and a
> wrong temperature in a prompt are different severities; this is neither. It
> is a wrong temperature in a dictionary nothing reads.

**AND THE PRODUCER COSTS SOMETHING.** `measured` 2026-10-20: **33, 11 and 58**
Open-Meteo calls on the last three runs, **0.9–3.1 min of wall time**, 14–16%
of the picks step. It is PNC-1 with a provider bill. **My own PNC detector
cannot see it:** `pnc_scan` tracks symbols — functions, constants, tables,
columns — and these are **dict keys** written into a feature mapping, while
`_get_weather_features` itself *is* consumed by `create_features`. A coverage
gap in the instrument, stated rather than left implied.

### THE ERROR RATE: A CENSUS, NOT A SAMPLE

**Decision rule, stated before the sweep:** every fixture in the three
pan-European competitions is played in a UEFA country, so a `results[0]`
**outside UEFA with a UEFA alternative in the same response** is **wrong** —
not "at risk", wrong, because the fixture cannot have been played there.
Applied to the **whole population**, 185 unhinted venues / 428 fixtures:

| outcome | venues |
|---|---|
| top result in UEFA (or no UEFA alternative) | 176 |
| **top result OUTSIDE UEFA with a UEFA alternative** | **3 (1.6%)** |
| no geocoding result at all → `_DEFAULTS` | 6 |

**4 fixtures affected.** It is a **LOWER bound**: a venue resolving to the
wrong *UEFA* country would pass the rule.

| venue | fx | `results[0]` | the UEFA alternative |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Motherwell` | 2 | **Motherwell, ZA** pop 140,351 | Motherwell, GB pop 32,840 |
| `Bar` | 1 | **Qionghai, CN** pop 528,238 | (Bar, ME — 4th) |
| `San Sebastian` | 1 | **San Sebastián, PR** | San Sebastián de La Gomera, ES |

Population ranking is doing the damage in each: a larger homonym outranks the
intended town.

**DELTAS over all three (n=3):** |ΔTemp| **5.2–10.7 °C**, mean 7.6; |ΔPrecip|
0.6–4.4 mm; `weather_is_raining` flips on **2 of 3**, `weather_is_windy` on 0
of 3. *(The `Bar` delta measured yesterday for a different target date was
+9.6 °C / −10.6 mm; weather deltas are date-dependent, which is why the two
figures differ rather than disagree.)*

**CAN THE TWO SAMPLES BE COMBINED? No — and they no longer need to be.** The
head sample (0 of 12) was drawn from the stratum **protected by population
ranking**; the tail sample (1 of 12) from the unprotected one. Pooling would
estimate a mixture corresponding to no population. The tail's 8.3% also
**over-states** the census's 1.6%, precisely because it was drawn from the most
obscure venues. The census supersedes both, which is why it was taken.

**Report only.** Fixing either site changes feature values — a cohort event —
and goes to the 11-01 queue with this size attached. Note the size now reads:
3 wrong venues, 4 fixtures, **zero realised effect on any pick or figure**.

## PART C — THREE FOLDS LABELLED

### THE FOUR ROUTES, AND ONLY ONE USES THIS HARNESS

| route | key figures | folds? |
|---|---|---|
| logistic divergence, settled picks | coef +0.245, z=1.11, p=0.265; market-only LL **−685.99 beats** model-only −690.67; n=1018 | **none** |
| scoring rules, same picks | model Brier 0.2499 ≈ constant-0.514 Brier 0.2498; raw 1/odds 0.2410 | **none** |
| **walk-forward blend sweep** | **1,710 priced** OOS matches; log-loss falls monotonically 1.0412 (w=0) → 0.9929 (w=1.0), no interior optimum | **3 effective of 5** |
| the price closure | close-at-retail predicts `1/R−1 = −4.64%`; measured flat ROI **−5.396%** over 1,320 settled picks, a 0.76pp gap inside the ~±2.6pp SE | **none** |

> **The standing conclusion — "the model adds no information over the price" —
> is MULTIPLY DETERMINED and does not depend on the fold count. The
> `bookmaker_blend_weight → 1.0` RECOMMENDATION rests on this harness alone.**

Route 3 is the only one that sweeps the *weight*: the others establish that the
model adds nothing, which implies w=1.0 is not worse, but the **monotone shape
with no interior optimum** is established only on 1,710 priced matches across
**three adjacent folds inside one odds-collection era**.

### WHAT THREE ADJACENT FOLDS IN ONE ODDS ERA SUPPORT

* **CAN** — the intervals for those 1,710 observations, and the absence of an
  interior optimum **within that period**.
* **CANNOT** — temporal generality. And the period is not merely short, it is
  **atypical**: the corruption gate rejected **4,836** 1X2 books in that era,
  Bet365 at **92%** implausible and Pinnacle at **26%**.

**SHOULD THE RECOMMENDATION CARRY A QUALIFICATION? Yes.** What it would take is
**more odds eras, which means time** — a statement about **when, not whether**.
Odds collection began 2026-02; a second era with a different book mix cannot
exist until one has accumulated.

### THE REFUSAL, EXTENDED

`show()` already refused in the clean harness. Now `walk_forward` returns
`effective_folds` / `requested_folds` / `folds_ran` / `folds_skipped` /
`min_train` / `span`, distinguishes **`EMPTY TRAIN`** from `train<N`, and
`run_baseline.main` **raises** rather than print a table without them. The
returned block also carries its own caveat: **a fold count over all rows is
not the count for a priced subset** — 3 of 5 for the audit's 1,710 — stated so
a reader cannot transfer one to the other.

**No re-run, no figure moved, `BASELINE_REVISION` stays `b2`.**

## AND TWICE IN THIS STAGE, A TEST COUNTED ITS OWN SOURCE

A test asserting "exactly three of the four routes carry no fold structure"
greped this file for the phrase and found **4** — the assertion list quotes it.
The fix quoted it too and found **5**. A test that greps its own source for a
string it must also mention cannot be made correct by better escaping, so the
claim became **data**: a dict of route → `uses_this_harness`, asserted on
structure. Third costume of the comment-blind family in this file set, after
docstrings and log-message literals.

## THE ENTRY

> **A floor nobody has profiled is an assumption wearing a measurement's
> clothes.** Eight and a half minutes looked irreducible for two stages because
> the only levers examined were the cron and the deadline. Decomposed, the
> largest block in the picks step after the Claude review is a weather fetch
> whose output no model, no prompt and no calculator reads — three minutes a
> day spent on a dictionary nothing opens.

## DECLARATION

**DURATION PROFILED.** n=3 runs, phase table above, method and its blind spot
stated. `--update` is **43–50%** of every run; the post-picks results scrape
(11–14 min) does not count against the deadline; **time-to-picks 42.3 / 36.9 /
64.3 min**, all below the registered 88.1 bound, which is left unedited.
Serial **by necessity**: Flashscore's single browser. Serial **by accident**:
the injury loop (its own comment says so; 9.7 min on a full card, budget-capped
but not concurrency-capped), the Claude review (~9 s × N sequential awaits),
the weather fetch, and the AF upsert loop. **88 MINUTES IS NOT THE FLOOR: the
8.4-minute residual is reducible, 3.1 of it by deleting a producer that reaches
nothing and 9.7 available from one sequential loop.** The cron is not the only
remaining lever. **Nothing changed.**

**GEOCODER SIZED.** **Weather reaches nothing** — skipped in training by
construction, absent from both shipped pickles' 111 fitted names, and dropped
at inference by name alignment (a −40 °C fixture aligns identically to a
19.7 °C one, with a negative control proving the mechanism live), with no
consumer in reporting, betting or models. **So realised harm is ZERO, measured
rather than inferred.** The producer still costs **33/11/58 Open-Meteo calls
and 0.9–3.1 min per run**, and my own PNC detector cannot see it because it
tracks symbols and these are dict keys. **Census, not sample: 3 of 185
unhinted venues wrong (1.6%), 4 fixtures** — `Motherwell` → South Africa,
`Bar` → China, `San Sebastian` → Puerto Rico — under a decision rule stated
before the sweep, and a **lower bound** because a wrong UEFA country would
pass it. Deltas |ΔTemp| 5.2–10.7 °C, rain flag flips 2 of 3. **The two samples
cannot be combined** — one was drawn from the stratum population-ranking
protects — and the census supersedes both.

**THREE FOLDS LABELLED.** Four independent routes to the no-information
conclusion; **three carry no fold structure at all** (two scoring analyses on
1,018 settled picks and the price closure at **−5.396% measured against
−4.64% predicted**), so **the standing conclusion is multiply determined and
survives**. **Only the `bookmaker_blend_weight → 1.0` recommendation rests on
this harness**, and therefore on **3 effective folds of 5**, adjacent, in one
odds era whose book mix was itself atypical (4,836 1X2 books rejected). Three
adjacent folds **can** support the intervals for those 1,710 observations and
**cannot** support temporal generality; the recommendation **should** carry
that qualification, and lifting it takes more odds eras — **when, not
whether**. The fold count is now returned by `walk_forward` and
`run_baseline.main` **refuses to print without it**, carrying the caveat that
an all-rows count does not describe a priced figure.

Gating suite **2167 passed, 6 deselected**. Non-gating **6 passed, 0 skipped**.
Invariants pass, count not cited. Fingerprint **UNCHANGED** at `s5.18` /
`stage5_baseline_20260807.51fbcb`; `BASELINE_REVISION` **UNCHANGED** at `b2`.
No production write, no schema change, no model change, no cron moved, and no
optimisation applied.

*Recorded 2026-10-20. `src/evaluation/baseline.py`, `scripts/run_baseline.py`,
`tests/test_duration_profile_and_reach.py`.*

# THE WEATHER PRODUCER IS DELETED. THE INJURY LOOP IS SIZED, NOT TOUCHED.

*2026-10-20*

## PART A — WEATHER DELETED

### THE GATE, AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY TESTED

The raw feature dict **cannot** be byte-identical: removing the producer
removes six keys, which is the point. What must not move is **what reaches the
model** — the vector after `_align_features` selects the fitted names. That
distinction is stated rather than silently substituted.

`measured` 2026-10-20 over **8 real fixtures with venues**:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| raw features | **272** | **266** (exactly the six weather keys) |
| `weather_*` keys present | 6 | **0** |
| aligned width | 111 | 111 |
| aligned SHA-256 | — | **all 8 byte-identical** |

**And the instrument discriminates: 8 distinct digests across the 8 fixtures**,
so the equality is not a constant-output artefact. **The gate passed and the
deletion proceeded.**

**Rule 4 was applied to my own prior measurement.** The earlier grep for
`weather_*` agreed with the standing hypothesis, so before cutting I checked
the instrument: `analysis.features` is read in **five** places and **every one
uses an explicit `.get(key)`** — no `items()`, no `keys()`, no `json.dumps`, no
f-string of the dict. A generic iteration would have been invisible to the
grep. The features dict is also **not persisted**: no `JSON` column holds it,
and `features=features` constructs an in-memory dataclass.

### WHAT WENT, AND THE DATA/PRODUCER SPLIT

> **Mark-never-delete applies to DATA, not to PRODUCERS.** No row was touched.
> The producer stops.

* `src/features/weather_service.py` — the whole module, including the
  `results[0]` geocoder. Its **only** production consumer was the weather
  fetch, so it went with it.
* `FeatureEngineer._get_weather_features`, `_league_country_code`,
  `_LEAGUE_COUNTRY_CODES`, the lazy `_weather_service` wiring, and section 14's
  call site. The league→country map existed *only* to disambiguate geocoding;
  leaving it would have created a fresh instance of the very defect removed.
* `models.weather_features_enabled` from both config files — **a config key for
  a producer that does not exist is the next reader's wasted afternoon.**

  **PRECISION, added on checking the commit:** only `config.example.yaml` is in
  the repository. `config/config.yaml` is **gitignored**, and CI does
  `cp config/config.example.yaml config/config.yaml` at line 276 of
  `daily-picks.yml` — so **the example file is the one production reads** and
  the committed removal is the effective one. The local edit is cosmetic for
  this machine. Saying "both config files" without that distinction would have
  implied two shipped artefacts where there is one.

**No registered question and no declared substrate depend on it.** That is the
contrast that makes this a deletion rather than a declaration: `odds.first_seen_at`
(H4) and `injury_observations` sit in `pnc_scan.AWAITING_CONSUMER` **with
re-triage dates** and are therefore *not* deletable. Weather is in neither
register.

### AND IT WAS NOT MY FINDING

`docs/predictive-audit-2026-08-07.md` already recorded it, ten weeks ago:

> line 157 — *"**Structurally excluded** — same train/serve asymmetry as
> injuries… The Open-Meteo call runs on every live fixture and **its output is
> discarded by the ML path**"*
> line 650 — *"dropped by `_align_features`. **Dead work on every fixture**"*

My contribution is the perturbation-controlled proof, the cost measurement and
the deletion. The finding sat recorded and unacted-on for ten weeks, which is
its own fact about this project.

### THE DURATION SAVED

`derived` from the `measured` 2026-10-20 phase profile — the call site is gone,
so the phase time is removed by construction. Confirmation is a post-deployment
re-measure:

| | 10-20 (34 fx) | 10-19 (13 fx) | 10-18 (65 fx) |
|---|---|---|---|
| weather phase | **−1.6** | **−0.9** | **−3.1** |
| picks step | 11.3 → **9.7** | 5.4 → **4.5** | 21.1 → **18.0** |
| time-to-picks | 42.3 → **40.7** | 36.9 → **36.0** | 64.3 → **61.2** |
| Open-Meteo calls | 33 → **0** | 11 → **0** | 58 → **0** |

**And two provider hosts left the system entirely** — `api.open-meteo.com` and
`geocoding-api.open-meteo.com`. The pinned external-host set goes **nine to
seven**, which is a measurement rather than housekeeping.

**On the 8.4-minute residual: 3.1 of it is now gone on a full card** — and it
was the free part, because this was not an optimisation. It was deleting work.

### THE TAXONOMY WAS RIGHT

**First instance of PNC-1 resolved by DELETION rather than by wiring.** Every
prior instance was either wired to a consumer or declared with a re-triage
date.

And **`pnc_scan` could not see it**: the detector tracks **symbols** —
functions, constants, tables, columns — while these are **dict keys** written
into a feature mapping, and `_get_weather_features` itself *is* consumed by
`create_features`. **KIND V, exactly as the taxonomy predicted.** The gap is
recorded in the instrument's own test rather than left implied.

### THE GEOCODER CENSUS IS NOW HISTORY

3 of 185 unhinted venues wrong (1.6%), 4 fixtures — `Motherwell` → South
Africa, `Bar` → Qionghai CN, `San Sebastian` → Puerto Rico — with **zero
realised effect**, because the features reached no model, no prompt and no
calculator. The record stands as what was *removed*, not what is exposed. The
**other** unverified first result, API-Football's `/teams?search=`, is **not**
deleted: it writes `Team.apifootball_team_id` persistently, so it has a
consumer. Five tests were **retired with their reasons** rather than dropped,
each naming what it had guarded and what replaces it.

## PART B — INJURY LOOP SIZED. NOTHING CHANGED.

### THE DB WRITE IS INSIDE THE LOOP — CONFIRMED

`_fetch_fixture_injuries` does `await self.apifootball._api_get(...)` **and**
`with self.db.get_session() as session:` — API call *and* a database session
**per fixture, both inside the per-fixture loop**. So concurrency would buy
network **and** database time, and the measured ~19 s per fixture is not one
HTTP round trip.

### WHAT THE 30 IS: A TIMEOUT WORKAROUND WHOSE TIMEOUT HAS DOUBLED

Not a provider rate limit. The code's own derivation:

> *"Keep budget at ≤15 so the **sequential API+DB loop** finishes within the
> 5-minute (300s) asyncio timeout. 26 fixtures × ~11s each = ~299s which always
> times out; 15 × 11s = ~165s which always completes."*

**The cap exists BECAUSE the loop is serial.** And it now disagrees with itself
three ways, `measured` 2026-10-20 by reading all three sites:

| where | value |
|---|---|
| docstring | *"the cap (default 30)"* |
| code | `max_injury = 15` / `config.get(…, 15)` |
| config (what production runs) | **`max_injury_budget: 30`** |

Meanwhile the caller's timeout is **720 s**, not the 300 s the derivation
cites — *"88 fixtures × ~8s = ~12 min worst case"* — and the **measured**
per-fixture cost is **14–20 s**, not the ~8–11 s either comment assumes. So the
constant the 9.7 minutes hangs on was raised, its timeout was raised 2.4×, and
the arithmetic justifying it was never re-derived. **Sized, not changed.**

### WHAT PARALLELISING WOULD COST

* **provider risk** — API-Football signals rate limiting as **HTTP 200 with
  `{"errors": {"rateLimit": …}}`**, handled with up to 3 retries and backoff.
  Concurrency raises the instantaneous rate, and the retries would eat part of
  the gain rather than failing loudly.
* **DB contention** — each call opens its own session, so 4-way concurrency
  means 4 concurrent Neon connections against a free-tier limit.
* **ordering assumptions** — `priority_fixture_ids` fetches picked fixtures
  **first** so that a budget exhaustion loses the unimportant ones, and the
  budget check `if fetched >= injury_budget` is a read-modify-write inside the
  loop. Concurrency without an atomic claim changes **which** fixtures get
  data, which is value-affecting rather than timing-only.

### DOES INJURY DATA REACH ANYTHING BUT THE PROMPT? STAGE 14 STILL HOLDS

`injury_*` **features** share weather's fate — **absent from the 111 fitted
names**, dropped by alignment. But `analysis.injury_report` reaches
`match_briefing._build_dossier`, i.e. **the Claude review prompt**, and
`injury_impact` reaches a reasoning string in `value_calculator`. The review
issues KEEP/CHANGE on every pick, so **injuries are value-affecting through the
prompt** even though they are in no fit.

> **That is the whole difference between Part A and Part B.** Weather reached
> nothing, so it was deleted. Injuries reach the prompt, so they are an
> optimisation candidate — and a parallelisation that changed *which* fixtures
> get fetched would be value-affecting, not timing-only.

### THE CLAUDE REVIEW: ~9 s, AND THE STABILITY IS THE EVIDENCE

8.7 / 9.1 / 8.7 s per fixture across cards of **65 / 13 / 33** — a five-fold
range in card size and a 0.4 s range in per-fixture cost. **That stability says
the cost is per-call overhead, not work proportional to the card**, so
concurrency would scale close to linearly: 65 fixtures at ~9 s is 9.5 min
serial and ~2.4 min four-way. Same risks in kind — provider rate limits and
cost — and the same ordering caveat, since the review writes KEEP/CHANGE
decisions.

**CANDIDATES, with measured savings and risks:**

| candidate | available | risk |
|---|---|---|
| injury loop, 4-way within the same budget | ~7 min on a full card | rate-limit retries, 4 DB sessions, **budget-claim atomicity is value-affecting** |
| Claude review, 4-way | ~7 min on a 65-fixture card | provider cost and rate limits; KEEP/CHANGE ordering |
| AF upsert loop (batch rather than per-fixture) | up to ~9 min on a large card | DB transaction size; the 9.2-min gap is DB work, not the HTTP call |

## PART C — RECOMMENDATION QUALIFIED, BOTH HALVES

The fold block returned by `walk_forward` now carries three fields beyond the
count, and `run_baseline.main` **raises** if any is missing — because **a count
alone does not convey an anomalous mix**:

* **`era`** — *"odds collection began 2026-02; every priced figure here sits in
  ONE era whose book mix was ANOMALOUS — 4,836 1X2 books rejected by the
  corruption gate, Bet365 92% implausible, Pinnacle 26%. Temporal generality is
  unsupported AND the population itself is atypical."*
* **`lifting_it`** — temporal generality needs **more odds eras, which means
  TIME: a statement about WHEN, not whether**. The anomalous mix needs a second
  era collected with the corruption gate in force from the start, so its books
  are clean **by construction** rather than by filtering.
* **`multiply_determined_note`** — the standing **no-information** conclusion
  does **not** rest on this harness: of its four routes, **three carry no fold
  structure at all** (two scoring analyses on 1,018 settled picks, and the
  price closure at **−5.396% measured against −4.64% predicted**). Only the
  **`bookmaker_blend_weight → 1.0` recommendation** rests on this harness
  alone. *"Do not read the two as equally supported."*

That last line prints beside the count on every run, so the conclusion and the
recommendation cannot be read as equally supported by someone who sees only
"3 of 5".

## THE ENTRY

> **The cheapest optimisation is the one that deletes the work.** Three minutes
> a day, two provider hosts, a geocoder, a config flag and a league→country map
> all came out of recognising that six numbers were computed and never read —
> and the recognition was not mine: it was in the audit from 2026-08-07, line
> 157, waiting ten weeks for someone to act on a sentence that already said
> "dead work on every fixture".

## DECLARATION

**WEATHER DELETED.** Gated on the **aligned** vector — stated precisely, since
the raw dict could not be identical — and the gate passed: **8 of 8 fixtures
byte-identical**, raw 272 → 266, aligned 111 → 111, with **8 distinct digests
of 8** proving the instrument discriminates. Before cutting, my own prior grep
was checked for instrument failure (rule 4): all five readers of
`analysis.features` use explicit `.get(key)`, and the dict is not persisted.
**Measured saving: 1.6 / 0.9 / 3.1 min per run** and **33 / 11 / 58 → 0**
Open-Meteo calls, taking **3.1 of the 8.4-minute residual** on a full card and
removing **two provider hosts** from the system (nine to seven).
**Mark-never-delete applies to data, not producers:** no row touched, and the
contrast with `odds.first_seen_at` (H4) and `injury_observations` — both in
`AWAITING_CONSUMER` with re-triage dates, both therefore undeletable — is
recorded. **First PNC-1 instance resolved by deletion rather than wiring**, and
**KIND V** confirmed: the detector tracks symbols and these were dict keys.
Credit where it belongs: the audit recorded this on **2026-08-07** and it went
unacted-on for ten weeks. Fingerprint **UNCHANGED**, which is the gate's own
confirmation.

**INJURY LOOP SIZED, NOTHING CHANGED.** The DB write **is** inside the loop —
`_api_get` and `db.get_session()` both per fixture — so concurrency buys network
*and* database time. **The 30 is not a rate limit**: it is a timeout workaround
whose own derivation cites a **300 s** timeout that is now **720 s**, at an
assumed ~11 s per call against a **measured 14–20 s**, and the number disagrees
with itself three ways (docstring 30, code 15, config 30 — production runs 30).
**Candidates: ~7 min from the injury loop and ~7 min from the Claude review**,
whose 8.7/9.1/8.7 s stability across a five-fold card range says the cost is
per-call overhead and would parallelise near-linearly. **Risks named:**
rate-limit retries eating the gain, concurrent Neon sessions, and — the one
that matters — **budget-claim atomicity, because changing which fixtures get
data is value-affecting, not timing-only.** Stage 14 still holds: injury
features are dropped by alignment like weather's, but `injury_report` reaches
the Claude review prompt, so injuries have a consumer and weather did not.

**RECOMMENDATION QUALIFIED, BOTH HALVES.** Beyond the fold count, the block now
carries the **era** (4,836 1X2 books rejected, Bet365 92% implausible — so the
population the intervals describe is itself atypical), **what would lift each
half** (more eras = time = *when*, not whether; and a second era gated from the
start rather than filtered), and the **multiply-determined note** naming the
three fold-free routes so the conclusion and the recommendation are not read as
equally supported. `run_baseline.main` **refuses to print without all three**.

Gating suite **2172 passed, 6 deselected**. Non-gating **6 passed, 0 skipped**.

No production write, no schema change, no model change, no cron moved, and no

# SEVENTY-FOUR DAYS, MEASURED. SIX OF THE EIGHT ARE COHORT EVENTS, WHICH IS WHY.

*2026-10-20*

## PART A — LEDGER HARVESTED

**THE PREDICATE, STATED BEFORE IT RAN:** (1) a defect named with a
**mechanism**, not a symptom; (2) a **location** — file, line, symbol, table or
workflow step; (3) **no subsequent entry** recording a fix, a deletion, a
declaration or a deliberate exemption.

**THE QUERY WINDOW, AND IT IS THE HONEST LIMIT.** Exactly **one** document in
this repository carries findings in a form that predicate can be applied to
mechanically: `docs/predictive-audit-2026-08-07.md` lines **645–657**, a
thirteen-row `# | File | Location | Defect` table. The ledger's **29,700 lines
are prose**, and a mechanical harvest of "diagnosis without subsequent fix"
from prose would be a confident guess rather than a measurement — which is
precisely why Part C's answer is a **register** and not a scan.

**Consequence, stated rather than hidden:** every age below is the same **74
days**, so **the median carries no spread**. That is a property of the source,
not of the backlog.

| | |
|---|---|
| entries harvested | **13** |
| still live against today's tree | **8** |
| fixed since | **5** — findings 1, 2, 3, 5, 9 |
| `UNEVALUATED` | 0 |
| untriaged | **0** |
| median age of the still-live | **74 days** (point mass) |

### THE KNOWN-WRONG CONTROL PASSES

Row **6** — *"Injury and weather features excluded from training but computed
at predict time → dropped by `_align_features`. Dead work on every fixture"* —
**appears in the output and reads LIVE.** That is the correct reading: the
**weather half was deleted yesterday**, 74 days after the row was written, and
the **injury half is unchanged**. A half-fixed row is live, not fixed, and the
register says which half.

### THE FIVE THAT WERE FIXED, AND HOW THAT WAS VERIFIED

| # | location | why it is no longer true |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `bayesian_weights.update()` | now takes `market`; a falsy league updates only the market-global scope |
| 2 | `_params_to_weights()` | the symbol no longer exists; the compressing normalisation went with it |
| 3 | `betting_agent.py:3295` | the `ml_models._models` misspelling is gone |
| 5 | `get_stats` `avg_clv` | the mislabelled quantity is now `avg_divergence`, with the error written out beside it, and `avg_clv` derives from stored `closing_odds` |
| 9 | config divergence | both files now agree on `max_total_kelly_pct` and the excluded-market list — *at 0, i.e. the cap is disabled in both; the **divergence** is what the row named and it is resolved* |

An entry fixed incidentally is **not a finding**. Five of thirteen were.

## PART B — TRIAGED, NOTHING LEFT UNMARKED

| outcome | n | findings |
|---|---|---|
| `FIX` | **1** | **13** — `data/models/` untracked, `feature_list.json` missing |
| `DELETE` | **1** | **6** — the injury half of the dead-work row |
| `DECLARE` | **6** | **4, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12** |

Every `DECLARE` carries a re-triage date of **2026-11-23**; every `FIX` and
`DELETE` carries an estimated size. **Nothing is unmarked, because an unmarked
entry is how 74 days happened.**

* **`FIX` 13** — infrastructure only: write `feature_list.json` at fit time and
  assert it on load. No fitted input changes. The real risk is that the pickles
  survive only via the Actions cache, so an eviction loses them and the next
  run retrains silently.
* **`DELETE` 6** — the injury **features** have no consumer: not among the 111
  fitted names, dropped by alignment. Deletable on the same 8-fixture
  aligned-vector gate the weather half passed. **The injury SCRAPER is not
  deletable:** `analysis.injury_report` reaches the Claude review prompt.
* **`DECLARE` 4** — refitting ML as-of would change the tuned weights. The
  Poisson/Elo half *was* fixed by a "leak-resistant refit"; the ML asymmetry
  the row named is the remainder.
* **`DECLARE` 7** — **five** of the 111 fitted features come from the rolling
  50-match standings (`home/away_league_league_position`,
  `home/away_league_relegation_gap`, `relegation_gap_diff`). Correcting the
  semantics changes fitted inputs.
* **`DECLARE` 8** — removing `_estimate_league_rhos` changes rho and therefore
  every Poisson probability. *"Nil measured benefit" is not "no numerical
  effect."*
* **`DECLARE` 10** — both 8-sample stat blocks are still injected into the
  decision prompt; removing them changes what Claude sees and therefore the
  KEEP/CHANGE decisions.
* **`DECLARE` 11** — `_auto_calibrate_ev_threshold` moves `min_ev`, which
  decides which picks are taken. Selection-affecting by definition.
* **`DECLARE` 12** — `calibrate_from_pick_outcomes` writes factors the ensemble
  reads, so changing it changes every probability.

### AND THAT IS THE EXPLANATION OF THE SEVENTY-FOUR DAYS

> **Six of the eight still-live findings are `DECLARE` because they touch the
> predictive core.** The backlog did not stall because nobody looked. It
> stalled because most of it is cohort-affecting, and this project will not
> change a fitted input or a selection rule inside an observability stage.
> **The two that were not cohort-affecting are the two that moved**: weather
> (deleted yesterday) and `data/models/` (a bounded fix, listed today).

That reframes the latency. 74 days is not a measure of inattention; it is the
measure of **how long a cohort-affecting finding waits when every stage is
observability**. Which is a decision someone should take deliberately, with
this list in front of them.

## PART C — THE MECHANISM, AND THE HONEST NO

**Can `docs/ci-audit-ledger.md` carry a machine-readable marker for an open
diagnosed finding? NO.** Annotating a 2026-08-07 entry with today's status
**rewrites it**, and historical entries are not rewritten — a rule that has now
held four times. So the alternative the directive anticipated is the one taken:
**a separate register that REFERENCES ledger and doc lines rather than
annotating them.** `scripts/finding_register.py` holds the status; the source
prose is untouched, and a test asserts the source carries no status column and
no back-reference to the register.

* **the pre-existing backlog was counted BEFORE anything was wired: 8.**
* **reported daily, report-only.** `ci_audit` prints
  `diagnosed_findings[13 harvested, 8 still live, 0 UNEVALUATED, 0 untriaged]`
  plus one line per live finding with its outcome and re-triage date. **The
  count does not alarm**, same disposition as `pnc_scan`: a triaged backlog is
  a decision, and alarming on six deliberately-declared entries every day is
  how red comes to mean nothing.
* **what DOES alarm** is an entry with no outcome, or a `DECLARE` with no
  re-triage date. **Ninth alarm surface**, and the pinned enumeration was
  updated deliberately rather than bumped.
* **CLR-2, confirmed to change the predicate:** a **fix** or a **deletion**
  flips `is_live` to `False`; a **declaration with a date** empties
  `untriaged`. A test strips every re-triage date and confirms the untriaged
  predicate fires, and confirms at least one finding has been observed to clear.

### A DEFECT IN THIS REGISTER'S OWN FIRST DRAFT

`_config_diverges` returned `False` on `ImportError`. The audit step installs
no packages, so `yaml` is unavailable there — and finding 9 would have been
reported **FIXED** in exactly the place the register is read. *A predicate that
answers "no defect" when it could not evaluate* is the third-state failure this
register exists to catch, one level up. It now **raises**, `evaluate()` records
`UNEVALUATED`, and a test simulates the missing import to prove it.

## PART D — INJURY BUDGET RECONCILED

### IT DISAGREED WITH ITSELF THREE WAYS

| where | value |
|---|---|
| docstring | *"the cap (default 30)"* |
| code | `max_injury = 15`, twice |
| `config.yaml` / `config.example.yaml` | **30** — what production runs |

So the code's own default was **dead and wrong at the same time**. One
definition now: **`DEFAULT_INJURY_BUDGET = 30`**, referenced by the assignment,
by the `config.get` default and by the docstring.

### THE DERIVATION IT CARRIED WAS STALE, AND IS CORRECTED IN PLACE

It read: *"Keep budget at ≤15 so the sequential API+DB loop finishes within the
5-minute (300s) asyncio timeout. 26 fixtures × ~11s each = ~299s which always
times out."* **Two of its three inputs have moved**, and the correction names
what it used to reference:

| input | then | now |
|---|---|---|
| timeout | 300 s | **720 s** (`asyncio.wait_for` at the caller) |
| per-call cost | ~11 s assumed | **14–20 s** `measured` 2026-10-20 |

**RE-DERIVED:** `safe budget = 720 / 20 = 36`; at 30 the loop needs
`30 × 20 = 600 s`, **120 s inside** the timeout.

> **WAS 30 EVER CORRECT? NO — it was never safe when it was written.** Under
> the 300 s timeout the same arithmetic gives 15 at the measured rate, or 27 at
> the rate the comment assumed; 30 needed 600 s against a 300 s limit. **It
> became correct when the timeout was raised to 720 s for an unrelated reason
> — "88 fixtures × ~8s = ~12 min worst case" — not when anyone re-derived it.
> Right by accident.**

**THE VALUE IS UNCHANGED at 30, deliberately.** Production already runs 30, so
reconciling the definitions changes no behaviour. Raising it toward the derived
36 would change **which** fixtures get injury data, and injury data reaches the
Claude review prompt — value-affecting, and a separate stage.

**NO CONCURRENCY CHANGE.** The sequential loop holds ~7 min on a full card, but
the binding risk is **budget-claim atomicity**: `if fetched >= injury_budget`
is a read-modify-write inside the loop, so parallelising without an atomic
claim changes which fixtures are covered. That is value-affecting and has its
own stage. The comment now records why it is deferred.

## THE ENTRY

> **A backlog nobody counts cannot be noticed, and a backlog nobody triages
> cannot be decided.** The weather producer was diagnosed correctly, located to
> the line, and left alone for seventy-four days — and the honest reason is not
> inattention: six of its eight surviving siblings require a cohort bump, and
> every stage since has been observability. The number that was missing was
> never "is this broken". It was "how long has this been known".

## DECLARATION

**LEDGER HARVESTED.** Predicate stated before running; **query window is one
document** — the ledger's prose cannot be harvested mechanically, which is the
finding that produced Part C's answer rather than a shortfall in the sweep.
**13 entries, 8 still live, 5 fixed, 0 UNEVALUATED, 0 untriaged, median age 74
days — a point mass, and said so.** **KNOWN-WRONG CONTROL PASSES:** row 6 is in
the output and reads **live**, because the weather half was deleted yesterday
and the injury half is not. The five fixed are named with how each was
verified.

**TRIAGED:** `FIX` **1** (finding 13, infrastructure, sized), `DELETE` **1**
(finding 6's injury features, same aligned-vector gate the weather half
passed), `DECLARE` **6** (findings 4, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, each with a
**2026-11-23** re-triage date). **Nothing unmarked.** And the shape is the
answer: **six of eight are cohort events**, so the backlog stalled because
every stage since has been observability — the two non-cohort items are exactly
the two that moved.

**THE MECHANISM, with an honest no.** The ledger **cannot** carry a marker
without rewriting history, so the register **references** doc and line and a
test asserts the source was not annotated. Backlog **counted before wiring
(8)**. Reported daily and **report-only**; the **ninth** alarm surface fires
only on an **untriaged** entry or a dateless `DECLARE`, never on the count.
**CLR-2 confirmed:** a fix or deletion flips `is_live`, a declaration empties
`untriaged`, and a test strips the dates to prove the predicate fires. And the
register's own first draft reported finding 9 as **FIXED** when `yaml` was
unavailable — *"could not look" is not "no defect"* — now `UNEVALUATED`, with a
simulated-ImportError test.

**INJURY BUDGET RECONCILED.** One definition, `DEFAULT_INJURY_BUDGET = 30`,
replacing a docstring that said 30, code that said 15 twice, and a config that
said 30. **Re-derived against the figures in force: 720 / 20 = 36, so 30 sits
120 s inside the timeout.** **30 was NEVER right when written** — it needed
600 s against a 300 s timeout — and became correct only when that timeout was
raised 2.4× for an unrelated reason. **Right by accident**, and the stale
derivation is corrected in place naming exactly what it used to reference.
**Value unchanged; no concurrency change**, with budget-claim atomicity
recorded as the reason.

Gating suite **2184 passed, 6 deselected**. Non-gating **6 passed, 0 skipped**.
Invariants pass, count not cited. Fingerprint **UNCHANGED** at `s5.18` /
`stage5_baseline_20260807.51fbcb`; `BASELINE_REVISION` **UNCHANGED** at `b2`.
No production write, no schema change, no model change, no cron moved, and no
behaviour changed by the reconciliation.

# H1 WAS SPENDING THE PICKS POOL THREE DAYS PAST ITS WINDOW. AND MY OWN DEADLINE WAS A TAUTOLOGY.

*2026-10-20*

## PART 0 — H1 JOB DISPOSED

**Run `39435238427`**, trigger `schedule`, headSha `ee5cc5d`, started

running. **Logs are unavailable for an in-progress run**, so the database was
the authoritative source — which it is anyway.

| `allocate()` | pool **350**, `h1_reserved` **0**, `normal_ceiling` **350** |

> **attribution counter**, not an allocation — `remaining()` returns the same
> 16 whichever side asks. With the reservation at 0, a closed experiment was
> claiming from the pricing pool that funds tomorrow's picks, and that pool had

**THE LEAK, measured:** the in-window attributed figure recorded on 2026-10-18
was **6** credits (this ledger, line 27192: *"H1 ATTRIBUTED credits: 6 / bound
168"*). It now reads **14**. The only H1 run after 2026-10-17 is this one.

> **POST-WINDOW LEAK: 8 TheOddsAPI credits.**

**`for_h1` attribution still works** — the `:h1` row incremented one second
after the pool row, so the figure is separable. That is the only reason this
number exists.

**TERMINAL STATE:** heading for `COMPLETE`. Three rounds at 120-minute gaps
from a 13:59 start: round 1 ~14:00, **round 2 claimed at 16:01:45**, round 3 due
**~18:01**. Not `NO_CARD`, not `NO_FIXTURE_IN_BAND`, not
`RESERVATION_EXHAUSTED` — it was collecting normally against a dead question.

**CANCELLED**, on Niki's decision. Verified: `completed/cancelled`, and the
budget **did not move after 16:01:45** — round 3 never claimed. **~4 further
credits saved**, pool holds at 334/450.

### 0b — WHY IT WAS SCHEDULED AT ALL

The cron `0 9 * * 2,3,4` **was live**, added at `d8df667` ("H1 on in-job
waits") for the collection loop, and **never disabled when the window closed**.

**The reservation-guard revert did NOT touch it.** That revert (87 refs / 31
assertions / 9 files) restored the *guard*; the *trigger* is a separate thing
and only the guard was reverted. Nothing connected the window closing to the
schedule.

**And the file's own header said otherwise:** *"NO CRON YET —
`workflow_dispatch` ONLY, DELIBERATELY. The trial precedes the loop."* True
until `d8df667` added the cron, stale ever since. A workflow whose header
denies its own trigger is how a scheduled job becomes invisible.

**COST SINCE 10-17:** one run, **8 TheOddsAPI credits**, ~2h14m of runner
minutes (terminated early), and the rows below.

### THE ROW QUESTION, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE CREDITS

`odds_snapshots` holds **20,971** rows on/after 2026-10-18, latest
**16:03:10** — though that table is shared with the ordinary closing-line
capture, so the count is not all H1's.

**THE REAL DEFECT IS NOT THE ROWS, IT IS THAT NOTHING EXCLUDED THEM.**
`load_observations` had **only a lower bound**, and `h1_analysis --since`
defaults to **2026-10-01**. So every post-window row **would have entered the
closed experiment's population**, and n would have risen above 4 silently —
exactly the way a dead result becomes a live one by accident.

Added `H1_WINDOW_TO = '2026-10-17'` as a registered constant, an optional
`until` on `load_observations` (default `None`, so the operational check is
unchanged), and the analysis now **always** passes it and prints it.

**DISCRIMINATION CONTROL** — an invariance claim needs one:

| | observations | kept |
|---|---|---|
| bounded (`< 2026-10-17`) | **25,381** | 9,857 |
| unbounded | **40,134** | 15,582 |
| **excluded by the bound** | **14,753** | — |

**A 58% inflation of the closed experiment's population, avoided.** The bound
is emphatically not inert. The clamped analysis reports `STATE: NO DATA` and
**n did not rise**.

### 0c — THE DISPOSITION

**Schedule disabled**, with the measurement, the pool arithmetic and the run id
recorded in the workflow. `workflow_dispatch` retained so the **2026-11-01**
re-run decision can be executed without a push; re-enabling requires that
decision **and a fresh pre-registration**, not a resumption. It is a producer
running against a closed question — the same disposition as the weather
producer yesterday — and it is in **neither** `AWAITING_CONSUMER` nor any
registered-question list, so **DELETE**, not `DECLARE`. The three
ordering/terminal states are retained.

**ONE finding, three runs.** One has been the answer every time it was counted.

**THE NINTH SURFACE IS NOT FIRING, and could not have been:** all three runs

**`_config_diverges` → `UNEVALUATED` is OUTSIDE `alarmed`, deliberately.** The

`diagnosed_findings[UNEVALUATED: … which is NOT an empty backlog]` and adds
nothing to `alarmed` — because "could not look" is not a finding about the
backlog, it is a finding about the instrument, and conflating them is what the
third state exists to prevent.

**The H1 collection runs reddened nothing.** The four prior runs succeeded;
today's is `cancelled`, which is not `failure`.

### AND THE CAUSE WAS MINE, FROM YESTERDAY

I shipped `floor = ceil_15(ready_binding + MIN_ACCEPTABLE_MARGIN_MIN)`. Two
defects, and the second is the serious one.

**1. IT WAS FROZEN AGAINST A MOVING INPUT.** Measured overnight: the weekday
lateness series went **n=7 → n=8** and `mean+3sd` moved **417.5 → 428.9**,
because the new point **lowered the mean** (255.2 → 241.3) and **raised the
sd** (54.1 → 62.5) — and 3sd dominates. `ready_binding` drifted **+11.4m** and
the margin fell **+66.6 → +55.2m**. I had flagged the instability and got the
**direction wrong**: the note said the floor "will move EARLIER as the series
grows". It moved later. Freezing a derived quantity is the stale-literal
defect I fixed in the `LIVE 0 4 * * 1-5` cron label three days earlier.

**2. IT WAS A TAUTOLOGY.** If the deadline is *defined* as `ready + 60`, then
"the margin clears 60" is true **by construction**. Re-deriving it each run —
the obvious fix — would have made the prospective alarm **unable to fire**:
VAC-1, a filter that cannot fail. The tempting repair was worse than the bug.

### RE-ANCHORED: THE DEADLINE IS A FACT ABOUT FOOTBALL, NOT ABOUT US

| day type | deadline | basis | ready | margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| weekday | **09:30** | observed earliest kickoff, 2023-10-26 `bulgaria/efbet-league`, n=715 | 08:49 | **+40.2m — FAILS 60** |
| weekend | **09:45** | observed earliest kickoff, 2024-10-19, n=375 | 08:03 | +101.7m clears |

**THE BREACH IS THE TRUTH, NOT A BUG.** Self-anchored it read +55.2m;
world-anchored it reads **+40.2m, 19.8 minutes short of the registered 60** —
**the self-anchoring was hiding 15 of those minutes.** The registered 60 is
**not** edited; it was stated 2026-10-10 before any of this.

**Exposure becomes ZERO by construction** (the deadline *is* the observed
minimum), so the coverage term is satisfied rather than traded — and still
printed at zero. **The trade moved, it did not vanish:** exposure 15m → 0 and
margin +55 → +40.

**THE CLEARING ACTION IS NOT A DEADLINE CHOICE.** No anchoring clears it: the
kickoff is a fact, the ready time is ours. **Today:** manual dispatch, which
skips the measured 3h58m–5h04m lateness. **Durably:** an earlier cron or a
faster run — and the duration profile already sized the second at **~7 min**
(sequential injury loop) + **~7 min** (sequential Claude review) + up to
**~9 min** (AF upsert loop). **Any two of those close 19.8 minutes.** That
decision is Niki's, and it is the same conclusion the profile reached — now
with a live alarm behind it instead of a hypothetical.

### A SECOND FINDING SURFACED WHILE CLASSIFYING THE FIRST

The weekday **margin acknowledgement was obsolete *and* expired, and was still
absorbing**:

* its `review` date was **2026-10-18** — two days gone — and

**Retired** — an empty register is the right state for "nothing is deferred" —

`MARGIN_REMEDY` also cited the **retired** 14:30/10:15 percentiles and a
day-type split taken on 2026-10-10. Rewritten to name the two real levers.

### THE REMAINDER — WHICH IS THE SIGNAL

**TWO true alarms, ONE root cause, ONE clearing action:**

## Workflow inventory, and 3.1 of the 19.8 minutes — 2026-10-20

### PART A — WORKFLOWS INVENTORIED

**SIX, NOT SEVEN.** The directive asked for seven; `.github/workflows/` holds
six. The full table, interaction graph and daily totals are in
`docs/workflow-inventory.md`. The figures that matter here:

* **2,981 runner minutes over 30 days = 99.4/day**, 389 runs.
* **`h1-collect` 1,106.7 + `fixture-horizon-probe` 40.7 = 1,147.4 min = 38.5%
  of all runner time**, spent on a closed question and a question closed by
  arithmetic. `h1-collect` cost **221.3 min per run** — the most expensive
  thing in the repository — five times, for n=4 and no analysis.
* After the two disables the projection is **~61 min/day**.
* `ci-audit` 185 runs / **79 failures**; `daily-picks` 35 / **10**.

**EVERY WORKFLOW GUARDS ITSELF AND NOTHING GUARDS THE SET.** All six declare a
concurrency group named after themselves, all `cancel-in-progress: false`. Two
runs of one workflow never overlap; any two *different* workflows may run
together without restriction. `closing-lines` and `paper-trading-report` share
the identical cron `47 10 * * *`.

**THREE OF THE FOUR DEPENDENCIES ARE EXPRESSED AS CLOCKS.** Only `ci-audit`
uses `workflow_run`. `closing-lines`, `paper-trading-report` and `h1-collect`
all infer "daily-picks has written the card" from the time of day. A nominal
gap cannot order two jobs that are both late, and the measured instance is H1:
three runs inside the 10-13…10-17 outage succeeded, spent 0 credits, wrote 0
rows and reported `RUNNING_AND_FINE`.

**FOUR OF SIX DRAW ON ONE TheOddsAPI POOL** (334/450 used, 16 left). A closed
experiment took 8 of those from the pricing pool.

**`odds_snapshots` HAS THREE PRODUCERS AND NO PRODUCER TAG** — `daily-picks`,
`closing-lines`, `h1-collect`. That is why 20,971 rows could not be attributed
to H1 without the `theoddsapi:h1` credit counter.

**DISPOSITIONS.** `KEEP` daily-picks, closing-lines, ci-audit. `DELETE`
fixture-horizon-probe (zero deadlines in 8 fetching runs; its 30-league
coverage advantage is now inside the deadline that binds, and the reference
binds on 0 of 834 days). `DELETE` h1-collect, re-triage **2026-11-01**.

**`paper-trading-report` → THE DECISION IS NIKI'S, AND IT IS NOT KEEP-OR-KILL.**
Cheapest workflow here: 0.8 min/run, 23.7 min/30 days, zero provider calls. Its
content is live — 1,534 settled, win 58.0%, flat ROI **−4.67% [−8.8%, −0.5%]**,
Brier 0.2466 model vs **0.2433 market**. But on success it writes an artifact
nobody is notified about; **Telegram fires only on failure.** So the choice is
*deliver it* (six lines to Telegram, as the daily card already is) or *stop
producing it*. The third option — a daily artifact nobody is told about — is the
one in force by default.

### PART B — 19.8 NOT CLOSABLE WITHOUT A COHORT BUMP

#### B1. Which of the three is timing-only

| candidate | measured | timing-only? | mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| **injury loop** | 6.9–9.7 min, 30 requests | **the REQUESTS are not, the PACING is** | free tier is 10/min, and `cap=2` is recorded in-code as having caused 429s on *every* run with at least 2 fixtures. 30 requests take 3.0 min or more however they are issued: **BY NECESSITY.** But the gap was an unconditional `sleep(6)` *after* each response, so the ~7 s of DB writes was added on top. That part is ours. |
| **Claude review** | 2.0–9.5 min, ~9 s/fixture | **NO** | the decisions are per-match independent (prompt per match, `_apply_decision` filters by `match_id`), but `_mark_sent` is an **unlocked read-modify-write on one JSON file**, and the marker it writes is `final:<match_id>` — the day-freeze that stops a later run regenerating picks behind the ruling. A lost marker changes which bet is tracked. Value-affecting **by race**, and the prerequisite is a correctness fix, not a timing change. |
| **AF upsert loop** | **MY OWN ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG** | the big part NO, the rest ~0 | see below. |

**THE AF UPSERT LOOP: I HAD MIS-ATTRIBUTED IT, AND THE RUN SHOWS IT.** The
duration profile said the 10.1 min was "in the per-fixture upsert loop, not the
HTTP call", reasoning from a gap that sits *after* `AF_LEAGUE_FILTER` — which is
emitted at the **end** of a date's loop. A gap there spans the *next* date's
fetch and its silent loop, so the gap's position cannot separate them; the
profile's own caveat says so. `measured` 2026-10-20 from run 39358701217:

```
API-Football: 236 fixtures on 2026-10-20 -> 0 created, 33 updated
API-Football: 199 fixtures on 2026-10-19 -> 0 created, 13 updated
```

**TWO date calls, not seven, and ZERO slow-path fixtures.** The league filter is
the first statement in the loop body, so the rejected fixtures cost no round
trips at all, and 46 fast-path updates cost ~26 round trips, about **4 s**, not
10 minutes. The loop was never the cost. What *is* the cost is the sleeps:
**83 requests x 6 s = 8.3 min in one run.**

A round trip to the DB is **168 ms** (median, n=12, `measured` 2026-10-20 **from
this workstation, not from a CI runner** — the runner's latency is unmeasured).

#### B2. The one timing-only change, done

**`_api_get`'s gap is now a DEADLINE, not a sleep.** `_AF_MIN_REQUEST_GAP_S =
6.0`; `_next_request_at` is armed the instant a response lands and waited out
before the next request starts.

**THE GUARANTEE IS UNCHANGED AND THAT IS PROVABLE.** Old spacing (response end
to next request start) is `6 + W`; new is `max(6, W)`. Both are at least 6. The
new one is never looser and never tighter than 6, and its tightest case, `W = 0`,
is the case the xG and odds loops **already run today**, because both collect
their results and write once at the end. Nothing is paced closer together than
something already running.

It also makes pacing **stricter** in one place: the error branches used to
`return None` with no sleep at all, so an errored call was followed immediately
by the next one. Every issued request now arms the gap.

**WHAT IT RECOVERS, per loop, measured from run 39358701217:**

| loop | requests | work after each response | recovered |
|---|---|---|---|
| injury | 30 | ~7 s of DB writes | **180 s = 3.0 min** |
| fixtures-by-date | 2 | 0 s and 4.4 s | 4 s |
| odds | 35 | ~0 — written after the gather | **0** |
| xG | 16 | ~0 — one commit at the end | **0** |

**About 3.1 min.** The odds and xG loops recover nothing *because there is
nothing to overlap*: their 6 s is the provider's floor, not ours. 83 requests at
10/min is 8.3 min and no amount of restructuring changes it.

`tests/test_request_pacing.py` — 5 tests on a virtual clock. `test_3` is the
**discrimination control**: with 12 s of work the two semantics differ by 1.5x
(49.6 s against 73.6 s), so it fails under the old behaviour instead of passing
under either. Both expectations are *derived from the parameters* — the first
draft hard-coded 48 and 72 and forgot the request's own duration, which is the
same class of mistake as pacing from the wrong instant.

#### B3. The margin after it

```
BEFORE  binding +40.2   shortfall 19.8
AFTER   binding +43.3   shortfall 16.7      recovered +3.1
```

A 3.1 min shift clamps nothing (series min 9.4 min), so the sd is unchanged and
the term falls by exactly 3.1. **This assumes every run had a full 30-fixture
injury budget, which is the most favourable assumption** — a 13-fixture day
recovers 1.3 min, not 3.0. The duration series carries no per-run card size, so
the true mean effect cannot be computed from it. +3.1 is an upper bound.

#### WHY THE REMAINING 16.7 IS NOT A TIMING PROBLEM

```
cron                0.0   already the earliest a same-day cron can be
delay  mean+3sd   428.9   n=8   <- GitHub's scheduler. 4.25x the duration term.
duration mean+3sd 100.9   n=78  <- the only term we own
deadline          570.0   09:30, observed earliest kickoff
```

**OF THE DURATION TERM, 58.4 MINUTES IS SPREAD, NOT LEVEL** (`3 * sd`, sd 19.5
over runs of 9.4 to 100.8 min). **Halving the spread would buy 29.2 minutes,
more than the whole shortfall, while cutting the mean buys 1:1.** The variance
comes from card size and from the intermittent 5.6-min ML retrain sitting inside
the picks path. That is the largest lever available and it is not a timing
change: capping per-run work changes which fixtures get analysed, which is
**selection-affecting and needs a cohort bump**.

**The estimator is not a lever.** `ready_3sd` adds two 3-sigma tails as if they
co-occur, and the delay tail rests on n=8. Reopening it to clear an alarm would
be fitting the instrument to the reading, and `MIN_ACCEPTABLE_MARGIN_MIN = 60`
was pre-registered 2026-10-10. Neither is touched.

**THE THREE ROUTES TO 16.7, AND PRECISELY WHAT EACH COSTS.** Strictly, two of
them need no cohort bump — but neither is timing-only, which is why the
declaration stands:

1. **Parallelise the Claude review** (~7.5 min on a 65-fixture card). Needs the
   marker write made atomic FIRST. Decision-identical afterwards, so **no bump**
   — but bounded by a limit that is **UNEVALUATED**: CI resolves the backend to
   `claude_code` (the secret exists), so each review is a headless CLI
   subprocess with a 900 s timeout, and the Pro subscription's concurrency limit
   is not something I have measured. "Could not look" is not "no limit".
2. **Batch the AF per-fixture commits.** **No bump**, but it converts partial
   failure into total: today a mid-loop exception leaves fixtures 1..k
   committed; batched, all roll back.
3. **Cap the per-run work to cut the variance.** The biggest lever, and the one
   that **needs the bump**.

A fourth, not costed: move the ML retrain off the picks path. It is 5.6 min and
it fires on the *slow* days, so it cuts the mean and the spread together.

PAIRED       model 0.2434 (n= 479)  vs  market 0.2433 (n= 479)   delta +0.0001

**The entire apparent gap was the populations.** On the picks they share the
model and the market are indistinguishable. This does **not** rescue the model
— t=0.07 is no evidence either way, and the no-information conclusion stands on
its four routes — but the report had been **overstating the deficit**, in the
direction nobody audits.
