### THE FINDING THE DELIVERY UNCOVERED: THE EXIT CODE WAS BEING SWALLOWED

Running the report locally exited **1** while the inventory had measured this
workflow at **31 runs / 31 ok / 0 fail**. Both are true, and the reconciliation
is the defect:

```
bash -e -c 'python -c "raise SystemExit(1)" | tee /dev/null'   -> exit 0
bash    -c 'set -o pipefail; ...              | tee /dev/null' -> exit 1
```

GitHub runs `run:` under `bash -e` **without `-o pipefail`**, so the pipeline
returned `tee`'s status and the report's exit code was discarded. **The 80%
closing-coverage threshold had therefore never been able to fail this job** —
and coverage is **12.5% (165/1316)**. `31/31 ok` was the swallowing, not health.
A threshold whose breach cannot change any observable is a check that cannot
fail.

Fixed, with the two outcomes kept apart:

* `set -o pipefail`, so the code survives.
* **`HEALTH_ALERT_EXIT = 2`** — "the report ran and a check alarmed". The alert
  now travels in the delivered summary and in a `::warning::` annotation, and
  the job stays **green**.
* Exit 1 keeps its single meaning, "could not run", which is the only case
  where the existing *"the experiment is still collecting, but its instrument
  is blind today"* alert says something true. For a health alert it would have
  been false: the instrument worked, and that is how it found the problem.
* `section_health` returns the alert **texts**, not a count. An integer cannot
  reach a person; its only channel was the code that was being dropped.

Verified: the full report now exits **2** and emits
`::warning::paper-trading-report: 1 health alert(s) — closing capture coverage
12.5% ... below the 80% threshold`.

### TWO MISTAKES OF MINE, FOR THE RECORD

**A literal backspace byte reached a source file.** A heredoc collapsed
`\bin\bash` to a real `\x08`, so `grep` and the terminal rendered
`Gitinash.exe` while Python saw `Git\x08in\x08ash` — which is why an exact-match
replace kept reporting "already fixed" against a line I could see. The
candidate was never reached because `shutil.which` matched first, so the test
passed with a corrupt constant in it. Repaired, and **every file touched in
this stage and the last was scanned for stray control characters: none remain.**

**A skipped control is not a control.** The pipefail control first failed
because `["bash", ...]` resolved to Windows' WSL stub, which exits **1** for
"could not exec" — indistinguishable from a propagated failure. It now probes
the interpreter with `exit 7` and proves it runs before trusting any code from
it, and resolves a real bash rather than skipping.

**UNCHANGED at s5.18 / 51fbcb** — changing what a report counts changed nothing
about what anything predicts. No production write, no schema change, no model
change. One cron moved, deliberately, to end a collision.

**THE THREE OPTIONS, AND THE CHOICE.**

| option | cost |
|---|---|
| keep 80% | **NOT AVAILABLE.** An alarm that always fires carries no information, and this project has paid for that six times. |
| remove it | loses the only signal that capture is *getting worse*, which is the one thing worth catching while coverage is low |
| **ratchet at the measurement** | **chosen** |

```python
CLOSING_COVERAGE_MEASURED = 0.1254     # 165/1316, 2026-10-21, --days 120
CLOSING_COVERAGE_FLOOR    = 0.12       # the measurement FLOORED to 2dp
CLOSING_COVERAGE_RISE_BAND = 0.03
```

The floor is **derived**: a day adds roughly 10–45 resolved picks to a 1316
denominator, so a zero-capture day moves the rolling figure about **−0.4pp**,
and 0.54pp of slack absorbs one such day without tripping.

**AND IT FAILS ON A RISE TOO.** Above `floor + 3pp` the check alarms and says
to **re-record the floor** — otherwise the floor drifts upward silently and the
next fall is measured against a number nobody wrote down. 3pp is about a week
of sustained improvement at the movement rate above.

Guarded by six tests: the fall fires, the unrecorded rise fires, today's
measured value is **inside** the band (so the replacement is not another
always-on alarm), and the floor is asserted to equal
`floor(measured × 100)/100` so it cannot be quietly re-chosen.

**Coverage was NOT raised in this stage.** That is different work and it did
not ride in behind an incident.

**AND THE FAILING CALENDAR ASSERTION WAS MINE AGAIN, FOR THE SAME REASON ONE
LAYER OUT.** Marking `test_the_weekday_cron_CLEARS…` as `live` took it out of
the capture gate — capture then succeeded — but the **non-gating step has no GH

### PART A — ONE PREDICATE

**THE DEFECT CLASS, NAMED PROPERLY: a gating test is a pure function of the
repository at that commit.** Two guards existed — one for calendar-dependent
tests (2026-10-18), one for live readers (mine, 2026-10-21) — and *neither*
covered the 10-21 pair, because each covered part of the class while both
looked covered. `tests/test_no_live_state_in_the_capture_gate.py` is
**deleted**; its rule lives in `scripts/calendar_marker_scan.py` as a third
reason. Two guards for one class is the shape rule 1 forbids.

#### Why the existing scanner missed both, measured

`scan_function` returned **`()`** for both failing tests. Two causes:

1. **Tuple unpacking defeated the taint tracking.** It required
   `len(targets) == 1 and isinstance(targets[0], Name)`, so
   `by_type, _crons = collect_lag_series_by_daytype()` bound **nothing** —
   while `collect_lag_series_by_daytype` was *already* in `LIVE_NAMES`. The
   guard was pointed at the right function and could not see the call.
2. **The taint was not transitive.** `lag = [l for _d, l in by_type…]` derives
   from a tainted name rather than from a live call, so even once `by_type` was
   tainted the assertion was clean. Now it iterates to a fixed point, because
   `ast.walk` does not visit statements in source order.

And `finding_register.evaluate` joined the live set — **not as a network
call**: finding 13's predicate is
`not Path("data/models/feature_list.json").exists()`, a working-tree read that
`actions/cache` restores in CI. "Live" in this scanner means *outside the
commit*, which is the class.

#### THE CENSUS, before and after

| | total findings | unmarked | after exemptions |
|---|---|---|---|
| at HEAD | 4 | 1 | 0 |
| first draft (transitive taint on BOTH sets) | **19** | **14** | — |
| bare name `evaluate` in `LIVE_NAMES` | 8 | 3 | 1 |
| **final** | **8** | **3** | **0** |

The 19 is the measurement that mattered. Propagating the **clock** set as well
took it from 1 to 14, and **11 of the 13 new ones were false** —
`trained_at = utcnow(); assert not stale` is hermetic forever, because the test
controls the clock-derived input and `now` is always now. All three known-wrong
cases are the **live-state** rule, not the clock rule, so transitivity applies
to `live` only and the clock rule keeps its 2026-10-18 binding exactly.

Two further false positives were measured and removed:

* **the bare name `evaluate`** refused
  `test_h1_precondition::test_NO_FIXTURE_IN_BAND_is_SEPARATE_from_NO_CARD`,
  which calls `pre.evaluate(_Sess(68, 68, 9, 0), …)` — a *different* `evaluate`
  driven by a fake session. Now qualified, as `requests.get` already was.
* **walking the target for Names** tainted the *receiver* of an attribute
  assignment: `agent.predictor.ml_models.trained_at = utcnow()` marked `agent`
  clock-derived. One false positive, `test_ml_stale_when_goals_model_missing`.

Two genuinely new findings remain and are **exempted, not marked** — both are
hermetic in fact, and marking them would move real coverage out of the gate to
silence a scan that was over-reaching. The exemption contract now requires each
entry to name one of four **grounds**; "it is fine" is not one, and the list is
pinned at 3.

#### THE THREE KNOWN-WRONG CONTROLS, each refused by name

| control | source | refused by |
|---|---|---|
| the test that cost **six cards** (2026-10-13) | already on file | `DATE LITERAL compared against LIVE STATE` |
| the **`collect_lag_series_by_daytype()` caller** | 269aea9, verbatim | `COUNT compared against LIVE STATE` |
| the **`feature_list.json` working-tree read** | f0ac3bb, verbatim | `COUNT compared against LIVE STATE` |

**POSITIVE CONTROL**: the same planted test, marked `@pytest.mark.live`, is
accepted — and under the gate's own `-m "not calendar and not live"` it is
*deselected*. Without it the three refusals would prove only that *something*
fails, and a guard that refused everything would pass them all.

#### WHAT THE PREDICATE CANNOT DETECT — its coverage statement

Rule 2. Seven kinds, enumerated in code and asserted to be enumerated:
**indirection through an unregistered helper**; **dependence via a fixture**;
**a module-level constant computed at import**; **a pure-clock test with no
fixed side** (the legitimate both-sides-moving form is deliberately not
flagged); **a filesystem read on a computed path**, since only a literal can
be checked against the index; **unseeded randomness, test order and shared
mutable state**; and **the database**, which a different mechanism covers.
Every one of them would have passed the scan on 2026-10-20.

#### AND THE SEQUENCE IS THE FINDING — SECOND CONFIRMATION

The remedy for this exact shape shipped on **2026-10-18 in `7514a50`**. The
warning sits **four lines above the gate's own pytest command**. On 2026-10-20
I added two more, and on 2026-10-21 they cost a card. *A remedy that must be
remembered is not a remedy* — the sentence was already at the top of that test
file, and this is its second confirmation. It has to be a check, which is now
what it is.

### PART B — TWO MARGINS

`min(reference, floor)` always returned the floor, because the floor **is** the
observed earliest kickoff over all 30 configured leagues. So one number carried
two different facts. Measured 2026-10-21: floor **09:30** against the day's
actual earliest kickoff of **15:30** — six hours pessimistic.

```
PROSPECTIVE MARGINS for 2026-10-22 (weekday) - TWO FACTS, NOT ONE
  STRUCTURAL    +37m  deadline 09:30  verdict ALARM  [ALL 30 configured leagues]
             basis: FLOOR observed earliest kickoff - ALL 30 configured leagues
  ACTIONABLE UNEVALUATED  deadline --:--  [9 of 30 configured leagues]
             the reference supplied no value (NO_FIXTURE) ... NOT a clear margin.
  RESIDUAL on the ACTIONABLE margin: it is an UPPER BOUND. p50=75m p99=592m
             max=1185m, > 60m on 312/605 days (51.6%).
  STRUCTURAL is ACKNOWLEDGED since 2026-10-21 at -19.8m against the registered
             60m (NOT edited), review 2026-11-21.
  ALARMS ON: actionable (CLR-2 - the only one a dispatch changes)
```

**The alarm moved to the actionable margin**, because that is the quantity a
manual dispatch changes. The structural margin is **reported and acknowledged**
with a dated review (2026-11-21), the registered 60 **unedited**, and the
exposure still its own term at zero.

#### THE FIRING RATE, measured over the record (n=904 days, from 2024-01-01)

| | fires |
|---|---|
| **structural** (vs the floor) | **629 / 904 = 69.6%** |
| **actionable** (vs the reference) | **4 / 605 = 0.7%** |

The alarm becoming rare is the point, and the structural term stays printed
every run so nothing is hidden by the change. On 299 of 904 days the reference
would see no fixture at all → `UNEVALUATED`, with the structural half still
reported.

#### THE UNSAFE DIRECTION — AND THE DIRECTIVE'S PREMISE WAS WRONG

The directive said the residual was *"already measured at 15 minutes"* and
asked me to confirm the threshold exceeds it. **It does not, and the 15 minutes
was a different quantity.** That figure was the **self-anchored floor's**
exposure, which is now **zero by construction** because the floor *is* the
observed minimum. The **reference's own** residual had never been measured.

`simulated` 2026-10-21 over **n=605** days, comparing the earliest kickoff
among the reference's 9 covered league keys against the earliest over all 30
configured (phantom 00:00 ingestion stamps excluded):

```
p50   75 min      <- today's case exactly: 16:45 reported, 15:30 true
p75  210 min
p90  360 min
p95  480 min
p99  592 min
max 1185 min
residual > 60m on 312 of 605 days (51.6%); == 0 on 212
```

**THE THRESHOLD IS EXCEEDED BY THE RESIDUAL ON 51.6% OF DAYS.** So an
actionable margin clearing 60 is **NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT**, and that
sentence is printed beside the figure every run. Raising the threshold to p99
would make it fire every day, which rule 4 forbids; subtracting the residual
reproduces the floor. Neither is an improvement, so the residual is **reported
beside the margin rather than folded into it** — and this is precisely why the
structural term must keep carrying the safety claim.

#### KNOWN-WRONG CONTROL

`test_KNOWN_WRONG_a_day_whose_EARLIEST_is_an_UNCOVERED_league` replays the
2026-10-21 case: the reference reports 16:45, the truth is 15:30. It asserts
the actionable margin is optimistic by **exactly 75 minutes**, that the
structural margin is **unchanged** by the reference being wrong, and that the
rendered output still contains `STRUCTURAL` and `UPPER BOUND` — so the pair can
never be silently reduced to the optimistic half.

### FOUR PINS RE-POINTED, ONE STRENGTHENED

The rename broke four deliberate pins. Three were re-pointed from
`"prospective margin"` to `"actionable margin"` (plus a new assertion that the
`structural` half is still present). The fourth,
`test_the_exposure_the_VERDICT_uses_is_the_one_PRINTED`, matched
`min_margin=_ahead["exposure"]["effective_min"]` **in the audit's source**; the
invariant it protects is a fact about *numbers*, so it now asserts
`min_margin == EFFECTIVE_MIN_MARGIN[dtype]` for **both** halves on a weekday
and a weekend, which a rename cannot defeat. Same lesson as the comment-blind
text scans.

One pin also had to move its anchor: it sliced 700 characters from the first
occurrence of the phrase, which now lands in a comment, so it measured prose
instead of the message. And `bound_by` was dropped from its required parts
**deliberately** — with the `min()` gone the actionable margin is
reference-derived by definition and there is no side to name; `coverage`,
`reference_state` and the new `residual`/`UPPER` carry what that pin was
protecting.

## One meaning per run; 14.6 of the 16.7 minutes were never real — 2026-10-21

### PART A — ONE MEANING PER RUN

`daily-picks` concluded `failure` while **all five critical steps succeeded**,
because a self-expiring guard reached its date. One conclusion carried two
independent facts — *did capture work* and *is a reminder due* — and a human
reading red cannot separate them. That inability is what cost six cards on
2026-10-13..18, where a red run was triaged as a pipeline failure after
capture had in fact succeeded. The reverse is worse: a red that means "a
decision is due" trains people to ignore red.

Stage 28 moved those tests out of the **gating path**, which stopped them
losing cards. It did not stop them **reddening the run**: the critical-step
alert read `steps.calendar.outcome` and `sys.exit(1)` on it. This moves them
out of the conclusion.

**`.github/workflows/reminders.yml`**, with the properties the directive
required:

* **`workflow_run` on daily-picks `completed`** — by dependency, never by a
  clock. A nominal gap cannot order two jobs that are both late, and that has
  been paid for twice: H1 ran through the 10-13…10-17 outage reporting
  `RUNNING_AND_FINE`, and `closing-lines` captures nothing when picks are
  late. The `0 13` cron exists only as a **declared** backstop.
* **`types: [completed]`, not `[success]`** — a reminder is due on its own date
  whatever the pipeline did, and the day the pipeline breaks is the day a
  pending decision is most likely to matter.
* it **prints** the upstream conclusion and reports `UNEVALUATED` on a
  non-`workflow_run` trigger, because the fixture-horizon probe's whole
  lifetime was lost to a dependency that looked fine.
* **registered in the audit's `WORKFLOWS` in the same commit that created it.**
  `ci-audit.yml` was created 2026-09-25 and registered a month later; eight of
  its red runs survived unrecorded in that gap.

**AND THE CREDENTIALS ARE GIVEN DELIBERATELY.** The 2026-10-21 reminder
reported *"the weekday series shrank to n=0"* from a step with no GH token — a
finding about football from the absence of a credential. The test now reports
`UNEVALUATED` (rule 3), **but a reminder that can only ever say `UNEVALUATED`
is not a reminder**, so `GH_TOKEN`, `FOOTBALL_DATA_ORG_KEY` and `DATABASE_URL`
are supplied rather than left out and worked around. Both halves are asserted:
the credential is present **and** the test still refuses to invent a verdict
without it. Either alone is a defect.

**Two messages that must not look alike.** They arrive in the same chat, so
the reminder names its workflow, says `A DECISION IS DUE`, says `NOT A PIPELINE
FAILURE`, and names where capture lives. Tests assert neither message has
acquired the other's language.

**KNOWN-WRONG CONTROL**, drawn from the morning: the failing reminder, planted
and run under **both** selections. The capture gate **deselects** it
(`daily-picks` green, nothing failed); the reminder selection **collects** it
(that workflow can go red). Asserted by running pytest, because the claim is
about which selection picks it up — a fact about pytest, not the YAML.

**CONSOLIDATION, because I nearly committed the rule-1 violation I had just
been told to avoid.** These assertions first went into a new
`tests/test_one_meaning_per_run.py` while `tests/test_calendar_separation.py`
already owned the "where do calendar assertions live" contract. The new file
is **deleted** and its unique assertions folded into the incumbent.

**ELEVEN PINS, re-pointed rather than loosened.** Six move from step level to
workflow level, which is **strictly stronger**: a separate workflow can neither
gate capture nor redden it, whereas `continue-on-error` only prevented the
first. The positive control **inverted** with the move — it asserted that a
calendar failure with capture green produced an alert and exit 1; now that same
state must produce **nothing** and exit 0, which is the content of the split,
and the reminder's own alert is asserted in its own test.
`test_BOTH_failing_reports_BOTH` lost its premise ("both failing" was a state
of one run) and became "a capture failure is reported on its own terms". The
alert harness now **refuses** a calendar outcome, so no test can exercise a
variable the shipped script no longer reads.

**Two of the eleven were real defects in my new workflow, not stale pins:**
`test_config_identity` requires the config copy to precede the test run and
locates that run by the **first** occurrence of the runner's name — which
appeared in my pip line *and* in a comment of mine; fixed by reordering the
workflow and rewording the comment, not by weakening the guard. And
`test_every_workflow_on_disk_is_AUDITED_or_EXCLUDED` caught `reminders.yml`
outside the audit's scope.

**The comment-blind text scan again, twice, in my own new tests.** One asserted
`"steps.calendar" not in src` and failed on its own comment explaining the
reference had been removed; a `_code_of()` helper now strips comment lines.
Sixth and seventh instances in this project — the first inside tests written to
be careful about it.

### PART B — DURATION: 14.6 OF THE 16.7 MINUTES WERE AN INSTRUMENTATION ERROR

#### The candidates restated, after the corrections

| candidate | measured | class |
|---|---|---|
| AF upsert loop | **~4 seconds**, not 10 minutes — 0 created / 46 updated, and the league filter is the loop's first statement | nothing to take |
| injury **requests** | provider-bound at 10/min; `cap=2` recorded as causing 429s on every run | **BY NECESSITY** |
| injury **pacing** | the unconditional `sleep(6)` → a deadline. **3.1 min, shipped** | timing-only |

#### And then the term itself was wrong

The margin asks whether **the card is saved and sent** before the earliest
kickoff. Its duration term measured **run start to run END**. Everything after
the picks step is yesterday's business — `Save briefings-sent guard`, the
Flashscore results scrape, `Settle late results`, the alerts, the cache saves —
verified against the workflow's own step order.

```
POST-PICKS TAIL  measured 2026-10-21, n=111 scheduled runs
                 mean 12.8 min, sd 8.7, min 1.7, max 49.6

weekday n=79        mean    sd     max   mean+3sd   binding margin
full run            43.0  19.1   100.8     100.2      +38.0
TIME-TO-PICKS       29.7  18.6    76.7      85.6      +52.6
                                         -> +14.6 recovered
                                            LEVEL +13.3, SPREAD +1.3
```

**No step got faster.** The margin stopped charging the card for work done
after it was delivered. The registered 60 is untouched and so is the deadline.
The superseded series is **retained** as
`MARGIN_RUN_DURATIONS_FULL_BY_DAYTYPE`, labelled the wrong quantity for this
use — a correction that deletes what it corrected cannot be checked.

**The structural margin is now +53m, short 7.0**, and the acknowledgement's
figure was re-stated from −19.8 to −7.0 rather than left to drift.

#### VARIANCE BEFORE MEAN, demonstrated rather than asserted

Per-step decomposition of time-to-picks, `measured` 2026-10-21, weekday n=79:

```
deps     mean  0.90  sd 0.10
tests    mean  1.52  sd 0.64
update   mean 13.81  sd 9.37   max 41.72
retrain  mean  2.16  sd 2.42   max  7.53   ran >1min on 37 of 79
picks    mean  8.64  sd 11.37  max 55.05   <- LARGEST SPREAD CONTRIBUTOR
```

Each candidate applied to the real per-run series, n=72 (the runs present in
both datasets):

| candidate | mean | sd | mean+3sd | margin | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (time-to-picks) | 31.6 | 18.4 | 86.8 | **+51.3** | short 8.7 |
| **A** parallelise the Claude review | 23.8 | **10.8** | 56.3 | **+81.9** | **CLEARS** (+30.5) |
| **B** ML retrain off the picks path | 29.7 | 17.9 | 83.4 | +54.8 | short 5.2 (+3.5) |
| **C** request pacing (shipped, not yet in the series) | 28.8 | 18.0 | 82.8 | +55.3 | short 4.7 (+4.0) |
| A+B | 21.9 | 10.1 | 52.3 | +85.8 | CLEARS |
| **B+C** | 26.9 | 17.5 | 79.4 | **+58.7** | **short 1.3** (+7.4) |
| A+B+C | 19.1 | 9.7 | 48.2 | +90.0 | CLEARS |

**Rule 4 is proven here, not assumed.** A reduces the mean by 7.8 minutes and
buys **+30.5** — four times as much — because it cuts the **spread** (sd
18.4 → 10.8) and the bound is `mean+3sd`. B and C reduce mostly level and buy
roughly their own size. **So the order is A, then B, then C** — and A is the
one that scales with card size, which is where the spread comes from.

#### THE ANTHROPIC CONCURRENCY LIMIT — NO LONGER `UNEVALUATED`

It is **not a concurrency limit at all**, on either backend:

* **API backend**: rate limits are RPM/ITPM/OTPM, enforced with a token bucket.
  **1,000 RPM at Start tier** for current models. Our peak is **65 reviews in a
  run**, about 1/min sustained — roughly **15× under** the limit. The docs give
  no concurrency ceiling separate from RPM.
* **CLI backend, which is what CI uses** (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is a repo
  secret and `briefings.backend` defaults to `claude_code`): a **shared usage
  pool** — a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit, shared with all other
  Claude usage on the account. Parallel work "consumes rate limits
  proportionately", i.e. **the same total, faster**. No documented ceiling on
  simultaneous `-p` sessions.

**So the provider is not the gate.** What remains is (i) the `_mark_sent`
marker race, a correctness prerequisite, (ii) the 2-vCPU runner — and a review
is ~9 s of mostly waiting on web search, so it is I/O-bound rather than
CPU-bound, and (iii) partial-failure semantics. `assumed`, not measured: the
CPU claim rests on the 9 s figure, and the only way to measure contention is to
run N concurrent subprocesses in CI.

#### PARTIAL RESULTS, for when A is taken

Rule 6. Parallelising the review must distinguish a partial result from a
complete one, and today's loop cannot: it catches per-match exceptions and
logs them, then the summary says `Claude reviewed N/M`. With N units in flight
the required behaviour is that **a failed unit leaves its pick at the model's
original selection with `review_action` NULL** — which is distinguishable from
`KEEP` — rather than silently inheriting a neighbour's decision, and that the
day-freeze marker is written **only** for units that completed. The marker
file's unlocked read-modify-write is exactly what makes that unsafe today, so
the prerequisite and the failure semantics are the same piece of work.

#### IS 7.0 REACHABLE WITHOUT A BUMP? YES — AND THE ARITHMETIC

**B + C = +7.4, leaving 1.3 short; A alone = +30.5, which clears outright.**
None of A, B or C needs a cohort bump: A is decision-identical once the marker
is atomic, B is decision-identical **provided the retrain is ordered before
picks** (a `workflow_run` dependency, not a clock — otherwise picks run on
yesterday's model, which *is* value-affecting), and C is shipped. **The
variance cap, which would need a bump, is not required.**

**Taken this stage: the instrumentation correction only** — one change,
measured, and it alters no behaviour at all. A and B are named with their
costs and their prerequisites rather than bundled in behind an incident.

### DISCIPLINE

Gating selection **2,240 passed, 7 deselected**; non-gating 6 passed, 1
skipped. Invariants pass, count not cited. Fingerprint **UNCHANGED at
s5.18 / 51fbcb** — correcting what a term measures changed no prediction and no
selection, which is what rule 5 requires of anything claimed timing-only. No
production write, no schema change, no model change; one cron added as a
declared backstop.

|---|---|---|---|

**ONE FINDING, and the set SHRANK across the day as the causes were taken:**
3 findings → 2 → **1**. The `DID_NOT_RUN` went with the dispatch (465146a);
the prospective margin went with the two-margin split (6150053). One has been
the answer every time it was counted this month, and it is again.

Also first exposures, both clean: `paper-trading-report` ran at 15:21 and
printed `closing capture coverage 12.54% … within the ratchet band [12.00%,
15.00%)` with `delivered: True`, concluding **success** — the ratchet, the
`pipefail` fix and the success delivery all working.

#### The three states

```
VERDICT         red WITH the registered marker  -> does NOT alarm
FAILURE         red WITHOUT it                  -> DOES alarm
UNCLASSIFIABLE  cancelled, empty log, or a marker with no exit beside it
```

**The marker had to be created first.** `reminders.yml` reddened by
`sys.exit(1)` and emitted **no annotation at all**, so its red appeared only
as `Process completed with exit code 1` — indistinguishable from a traceback.
It now prints `::error::REMINDER DUE` immediately before that exit.

**Pinned to what the AUDIT OBSERVES**, per rule 3: `DELIBERATE_RED_MARKERS`
holds `##[error]REMINDER DUE`, the **rendered** form. `::error::` survives only
in the `##[group]Run` echo of the step's own source, and pinning the source
literal is exactly what made the annotation matcher count echoed script text
and miss every real annotation — measured on three runs 2026-10-13.

**The co-occurrence precondition is enforced at both ends.** The marker is
registered in `SELF_EMITTED_ANNOTATIONS`, whose subtraction allows one exit per
annotation — and `classify_red` returns `UNCLASSIFIABLE`, not `VERDICT`, when
the marker is present with **no** non-zero exit beside it, because then it
explains nothing and the red is unaccounted for.

**`UNCLASSIFIABLE` alarms.** Stated in code as `UNCLASSIFIABLE_ALARMS = True`:
"the marker could not be read" is not "there was no marker", and a workflow
whose red cannot be classified is the case where silence has cost most here.

**Silencing was not used.** `reminders.yml` is **not** in
`NEVER_ALARM_WORKFLOWS` and **is** in `WORKFLOWS`, both asserted — rule 2, and
that cost has been paid twice.

#### BOTH KNOWN-WRONG CONTROLS

* **red WITH the marker → `VERDICT`, does not alarm.**
* **red WITHOUT it → `FAILURE`, alarms** — parametrised over four real crash
  shapes: a traceback, a failed install, a YAML syntax error, a missing
  credential. One direction is not a control.

Plus the third state three ways in: an empty/short log, a cancelled run, and a
marker with no exit.

### PART B — ACKNOWLEDGEMENT RESTATED

The structural figure moved `−19.8 → −7.0` with the duration correction. The
acknowledgement **had a `review` date that nothing compared** — the exact
defect named: the retired `ACKNOWLEDGED_MARGIN_BREACH` compared only `binding`
and absorbed a breach for days past its own review date.

`structural_breach_is_acknowledged(binding, today)` now compares **both**,
expiry first. Driven:

```
deficit  -7.4  -7.0  -6.9  -6.0   0.0   ->  COVERED
deficit  -7.5  -8.0 -20.0 -100.0  ->  ALARMS   (deterioration is an event)
on 2026-11-21 (the review date)   ->  COVERED
on 2026-11-22                     ->  EXPIRED, alarms
review None / "" / "soon" / "2026-13-45" / "21/11/2026" -> absorbs NOTHING
```

**AND IT CAUGHT MY OWN FIGURE ON ITS FIRST EXPOSURE.** I computed the margin at

so the predicate refused to cover it and alarmed. `60 − 52.6 = 7.4`, rounded
the wrong way — the same shape as the self-anchored floor, a figure I derived
and then transcribed loosely. Corrected to −7.4, and the audit now prints
`ACKNOWLEDGED … It does NOT alarm`.

The registered `MIN_ACCEPTABLE_MARGIN_MIN = 60` is **unedited**,
`EFFECTIVE_MIN_MARGIN` is still `{weekday: 60, weekend: 60}`, and the exposure

a term that disappears when satisfied cannot be seen to have been satisfied.

`MARGIN_REMEDY` was also re-stated: it still cited "~7 min in the injury loop"

## The review is parallel; the detector that reports dead detectors cries wolf — 2026-10-21

### PREREQUISITE MET — shipped separately in `ac2ca74`, before any concurrency

#### A1. The `_mark_sent` race

**What it guards:** two kinds of key in `data/briefings_sent.json`.
`review:<match_id>` makes a re-run skip a match already reviewed today;
**`final:<match_id>` is the day freeze** that stops a later `--picks` run
regenerating picks behind a ruling Claude already made.

**What it wrote:** a read-modify-write of the whole file — load the day's key
list, append in memory, rewrite all of it.

**What two concurrent reviewers did to it:** both read `{today: [a]}`; one
writes `[a, b]`, the other `[a, c]`. **The later write drops the earlier key.**

**Idempotent?** Per key, yes (`if key not in`). That is the wrong axis — the
file was unsafe under concurrency regardless.

**Detectable after the fact? NO, and that is why it mattered.** Nothing
compares the marker set to the database, so a missing key is
indistinguishable from one never written. Both halves are now tests.

**The fix, three ways:** the read and the write are **one step** (re-load
immediately before writing and merge into what is on disk); the write is
**atomic** (temp file + `os.replace`, because a torn file is read by
`_load_sent`'s bare `except` as "nothing sent today", which would **unfreeze
every match** on the next run — the unsafe direction, now its own test); and an
`asyncio.Lock`, taken at both call sites.

**The ordering, stated:** the decision is persisted **first**
(`_apply_decision` commits), then the freeze marker, and only `if bound`. A
crash between them leaves the **decision** in the database and no freeze — so
the exposure is a duplicate review, never a lost decision. That is why the
order is not reversed.

#### A2. Partial failure, and the NULL/KEEP audit

| consumer | treatment of NULL |
|---|---|
| `betting_agent.py:2804` | `review_action == "CHANGE"` — excluded |
| report `_section_by_review_action` | `review_action or "none"` — own bucket |
| report `section_claude` | `if p.review_action` — excluded from "reviewed" |

**No consumer defaults NULL to KEEP** — the shape that has cost this project
most often — and neither `review_action or "KEEP"` spelling appears anywhere.

**A third state was considered and NOT taken.** "Never attempted" and
"attempted and failed" are the same fact for every *measurement* here —
neither is evidence about the review's quality — and they differ only in
whether **the run** completed, which is a run-level fact. So it is reported at
the run level rather than encoded per pick, where a new value would have needed
both report sites changed to avoid being dropped from their fixed bucket lists.

**What changed instead:** failures are tallied and **named**.
`_last_review_failures` is retained and the log says *"N FAILED and carry
review_action=NULL with no freeze marker: [ids]. This is a PARTIAL review —
their picks stand as the model wrote them."*

**KNOWN-WRONG CONTROL:** the middle unit of three forced to raise — the batch
continues, 2 is reported, the failure is tallied as `[2]`, and the failed unit
gets **no freeze marker**. Plus the control in the other direction: the pre-fix
write pattern, reproduced, **must** lose a key, or the fix proves nothing.

### REVIEW PARALLELISED

`REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 4`, with the reason recorded at the constant.

**The bound is not the Anthropic rate limit** — 1,000 RPM at Start tier against
a 65-per-**run** peak, roughly 15× under, with no documented concurrency
ceiling. CI uses the Claude Code CLI on a Pro subscription, whose limit is a
**shared usage pool**; parallelism does not spend *more* of it, it spends the
same total **faster**.

**On a day when the pool is low:** serially, the first unit to hit the limit
sets `_claude_code_exhausted` and every later unit skips straight to the API,
wasting one doomed spawn. With N in flight, up to **N−1** spawns are already
running when the flag is set. So the cost of a low pool is bounded by this
number — which is why it is 4 and not 65.

**Exhaustion is distinguishable from a decline**, which matters more than the
waste: exhaustion is a **non-zero** exit with `session limit`/`usage limit` in
the output, setting the flag and routing to the API; a decline exits **zero**
and returns no parseable decision, leaving the model's pick unchanged.
Different codes, different log lines, different outcomes.

#### The identity proof, and its discrimination control

* **IDENTITY** — the same card under bound 1 and bound 4, same deterministic
  reviewer: identical decision maps. Order-independence is asserted separately
  by reversing completion order and comparing again.
* **DISCRIMINATION CONTROL** — a different card gives a **different** decision
  map, and the same card under a different reviewer also differs. Without
  these, "identical" is indistinguishable from a comparison returning a
  constant.
* **the bound is driven**, not asserted: the peak in-flight count is measured
  at `<= 4` **and `> 1`**, so a bound that silently serialised would fail.
* **partial failure under concurrency**: two units raised inside `gather`; the
  other eleven still got decisions, both failures were tallied, and neither
  reached `_decisions`.

**THE ONE HONEST QUALIFICATION.** `_claude_code_exhausted` is the only state
shared across units. On the normal path it stays `False` for every unit and
the two orderings are identical. On a day the pool runs out mid-batch,
**which** units fall back to the API differs between serial and parallel — both
produce valid decisions, neither is wrong, but they are not bit-identical.
Recorded at the bound, and asserted to be recorded.

#### Measured against the phase table

```
weekday n=72, bound 4                mean    sd   m+3sd    margin
0 serial (as measured, time-to-picks) 31.6  18.4    86.8    +51.3  short 8.7
A review at bound 4                   25.6  11.3    59.5    +78.7  CLEARS
A at bound 4 + pacing already shipped 22.8  10.9    55.3    +82.8  CLEARS
A idealised (the earlier floor model) 23.8  10.8    56.3    +81.9

PICKS STEP  mean 9.27 -> 3.23   sd 11.71 -> 2.37   max 55.05 -> 13.76
```

The real bound-4 implementation lands at **+78.7** against the idealised
**+81.9** — so the earlier estimate was optimistic by 3.2 minutes, and the
change still clears 60 with **18.7 to spare**. The structural deficit goes
from **−8.7 to +18.7**, so the structural acknowledgement becomes unnecessary
once CI runs confirm it.

**FINGERPRINT UNCHANGED at s5.18 / 51fbcb.** Rule 4 would have stopped this.

#### Does the standing finding clear? NOT YET, AND THAT IS NOT A HEDGE

`schedule margin +19m < 30m` is `deadline − (cron + observed lateness +
FULL_CARD_PICKS_MAX)`, and `FULL_CARD_PICKS_MAX = 88.1` is an **independently
measured n=4 constant from 2026-10-01**, pinned by its own test. The review
change cannot move it until fresh full-card runs are measured after this ships.
So the finding clears **when that constant is re-measured**, not today, and
re-deriving it now would be a second change in the same stage.

### THE TWO DEAD ALARMS, AND THE QUIET-STATE RULE

Both `model_integrity_failures` and `model_unsigned_loads` now fire, each with
a positive control **and** a control in the other direction
(`tests/test_silent_surfaces_can_fire.py`).

**Then the general check, because the defect was in the plumbing and not in
either alarm.** A matching line was synthesised for **every** pattern in
`PATTERNS` and pushed through `extract()`:

```
PATTERNS total            35
  produce a usable value  32
  MATCH BUT CANNOT COUNT   1
  no line synthesisable    2   (this script's limit; both hand-verified fine)
```

So **is each surface's health observable while it is quiet?** After the
previous stage, all eleven have a positive control that runs on every CI run,
so each detector can be shown capable of firing **without waiting for its
condition**. The pattern layer beneath them is now 32 of 35 clean, with the
other 2 hand-checked on real log lines (`no fixtures found for …` → 1,
`API-Football fixtures …: 0 created, 33 updated` → 33).

#### THE NEXT INSTANCE OF THIS CLASS — LISTED, NOT FIXED

1. **`src_flashscore_matched` fires the `NOT COUNTED` diagnostic on an
   ordinary line.** `Flashscore: 12 fixtures updated` yields a value of 1
   **and** prints *"pattern matched but produced no number … NOT COUNTED"* —
   because the key is served by the per-source branch while the generic
   fallback also runs. So that message appears on **every daily-picks run that
   scrapes Flashscore**, and *that is the mechanism by which the real
   model-integrity instance of the same message went unread for ten days.* A
   diagnostic that cries wolf is the mirror of one that cannot fire. One-line
   fix (the count-style list, or a capture group); **not done here.**
2. **The fallback diagnostic is still condition-gated.** It prints only when a
   pattern matches, so a newly added pattern with no numeric group stays
   undetectable until its condition occurs — the exact property that let the
   model-integrity alarms sit dead. The remedy is a **self-test over all
   patterns at startup or in the suite**, which is what the script above is;
   **not wired here.**
3. **Two patterns my synthesiser could not build a line for** —
   `no_fixtures_at_all` and `src_apifootball_matched`. Both hand-verified, but
   the automated check has a hole and the hole is stated rather than counted as
   a pass.

> A diagnostic that only prints when the condition fires cannot report that the
> detector is incapable of firing — and one that prints when nothing is wrong
> guarantees nobody reads it when something is.

## The constant cannot be re-derived; the patterns now test themselves — 2026-10-21

### PART A — `CONSTANT NOT RE-DERIVED`. n = 0, AND THE FULL-CARD ROUTE IS INFEASIBLE

**n = 0.** `cccb0e6` shipped at **21:29**; the newest `daily-picks` run is
**08:29** the same day, at `465146a` — thirteen hours earlier. There is no
post-change population to measure, so `FULL_CARD_PICKS_MAX = 88.1` still
describes the **SERIAL** regime and **the standing finding does not clear.**

**AND IT CANNOT BE RE-DERIVED FROM FULL-CARD RUNS ON ANY USEFUL HORIZON.**
`measured` 2026-10-21 over 2026-07-01…2026-10-21:

```
weekday days with a card              73
  of which >= 40 fixtures              6   (8%)
full-card weekdays per week          0.4   median gap 6 days
fixtures/day                      median 13, p75 26, max 120
```

So n=10 full-card runs is **~25 weeks** and n=20 is **~50**. Replacing an n=4
constant with an n=5 one is not progress, and the required minimum is now
**encoded**: `MIN_N_TO_REDERIVE_PICKS_BOUND = 10`, with the measured reason
beside it — the weekday lateness series moved mean+3sd **417.5 → 428.9 on a
single new point** (n=7→8, because that point lowered the mean and raised the
sd, and 3sd dominates) and the margin went **+40 → +37** overnight. A 3sd
bound on single digits is not a bound.

**THE FEASIBLE ROUTE, recorded as `REDERIVE_PICKS_BOUND_PLAN`.** The full-card
restriction exists because a full card was the worst case — and the
parallelisation is precisely what removes most of the card-size dependence
(modelled over n=72, the picks step's sd falls **11.71 → 2.37**). So the
constant should become an **all-card** time-to-picks bound, for which n=79
weekday runs are already measured (max 76.7, mean+3sd 85.6, SERIAL). Ordinary
weekdays arrive at ~5/week rather than 0.4, so **n=10 is about two weeks**.

**REGIMES ARE NOT POOLED.** The post-change series starts empty and is not
seeded with the serial runs — the same rule that keeps the `37 9`, `0 3` and
`0 0` cron series apart.

Both constants are **consumed**, not decorative: the PNC detector caught them
as producers with no consumer (33 → 35) and three tests now enforce the rule —
the constant still reads 88.1/SERIAL, the minimum is ≥ 10 with its instability
figures present, and the plan names the all-card population, forbids pooling,
and requires **both** max and mean+3sd.

### PART B — `MESSAGE DE-SATURATED`, AND THE CLASS IS 12

`src_flashscore_matched` printed *"matched but produced no number … NOT
COUNTED"* on `Flashscore: 12 fixtures updated` — **an ordinary line on every
run that scrapes Flashscore** — because the key is owned by the per-source
block while the generic loop also reached it and `int()` raised on a
whole-match string.

**THE DECISION: SUPPRESS AT THE SOURCE, not give it its own text.** Renaming
would have left a message printing on every run; the generic loop has no
business computing a key another block owns outright. `_OWNED_BY_A_DEDICATED_BRANCH`
lists all six per-source keys and the loop skips them.

**THIS WAS THE THIRD RECURRENCE IN ONE LIST.** `unpriced_check_dead` was added
to the count-style keys after being silently dropped for two days;
`src_apifootball_fixtures` after it *"printed NOT COUNTED exactly when
API-Football WAS creating fixtures"*; and this is the third. Suppressing the
family ends the pattern rather than patching its latest instance.

**CONFIRMED AGAINST A QUIET BACKGROUND, read as a human would.** `extract()`
on a realistic ordinary run now prints **0 messages** (it printed 1 before).
Injecting `MODEL INTEGRITY FAILURE` still prints 0 from `extract()` and sets
`facts[model_integrity_failures] = 1`, which reaches `alarmed` — so the rare
case is visible through the channel that matters, against silence.

**THE SIZE OF THE CLASS: 12.** On a real audit run whose only finding was the
schedule margin, **13** problem-shaped lines printed and exactly **one** was
the finding:

```
2  TRUNCATED LISTING / LOWER BOUND          (a --limit artifact, every run)
5  no ledger history for <workflow>         (every run, five workflows)
1  435 run(s) listed above is a LOWER BOUND
1  1 workflow record(s) ... NOT OWNED
1  UNEVALUATED, 0 untriaged
1  UNEVALUATED  deadline --:--              (correct and informative)
1  could not be cleared by any action here
1  !! SCHEDULE MARGIN +19 min                <- THE ONLY REAL FINDING
```

So the `!!` marker — the thing that reads as "look here" — carries **12
routine uses against 1 finding**. Counted, not fixed: that is a stage of its
own, and the count is what sizes it.

### PART C — `PATTERNS SELF-TESTED`

```
PATTERNS   35
  pass     35
  FAIL      0
  no example 0
```

Every pattern now carries an **example line it must match**, stored beside it
in `PATTERN_EXAMPLES`, and `selftest_patterns()` pushes that line through
`extract()` and requires a usable value. **A pattern that matches but yields
nothing fails on the next CI run, not on the day its condition first occurs.**

**IT RUNS IN `main()`**, before the early return on "no runs to audit" — for
the same reason the workflow-state check is there: a registration defect is
not about any particular run, and placing it after the return would make it
unreachable exactly when the audit has nothing else to do. A failure **alarms**
and names its clearing action (give the pattern a numeric capture group, or add
the key to the count-style list). It is the **twelfth** alarm surface, added to
both the enumeration and the census.

**COMPILATION IS CHECKED FIRST AND SHORT-CIRCUITS.** `extract()` applies every
pattern, so one uncompilable regex makes it raise on *any* input — including on
another key's example. That is why the compile check cannot be folded into the
loop; found by writing the control and watching it raise from inside
`extract()` rather than be caught.

#### BOTH CONTROLS

* **KNOWN-WRONG** — `model_integrity_failures` **as it was on 2026-10-12**: the
  same regex, under a key that is *not* in the count-style list, with
  `PATTERNS` patched so `extract()` really tries it. It **FAILS** with "this is
  the model_integrity shape". Without the patch the key would have failed
  merely for being unknown — a control passing for the wrong reason.
* **POSITIVE** — the same regex under the real key **passes**, and the test
  asserts the pattern itself was not edited, so the control compares two
  *registrations* rather than two regexes. An example that rots (pattern edited,
  example left behind) **fails** with "does NOT match its own example"; an
  uncompilable regex **fails** rather than raising; and a missing example is its
  own third state, neither pass nor fail.

> A diagnostic that only prints when the condition fires cannot report that the
> detector is incapable of firing. The patterns are now checked at
> registration, including the ones not yet written.

## The definition changed; the marker is reserved — 2026-10-21

### PART A — `DEFINITION CHANGED`

**BOTH POPULATIONS NAMED, and the old one keeps its name in the record:**

```
PICKS_BOUND_OLD_POPULATION
  MAX time-to-picks over FULL-CARD (>=40 fixture) weekday runs, SERIAL review
  regime; n=4, measured 2026-10-01, range 67.4-88.1, mean 76.4, sd 10.2

PICKS_BOUND_NEW_POPULATION
  time-to-picks over ALL-CARD weekday runs, PARALLEL review regime
  (REVIEW_CONCURRENCY=4, first in cccb0e6, 2026-10-21 21:29);
  starts at n=0 because regimes are not pooled
```

**RECORDED AS A CHANGE OF DEFINITION, NOT A RE-MEASUREMENT.** Full-card
weekdays arrive at **0.4/week** (6 of 73 days, measured 2026-10-21), so n=10
of them is ~25 weeks; all-card weekdays arrive at **~5/week**, so n=10 is about
two weeks. That trade would be a straight loss of conservatism under the
serial regime — but **the parallelisation is exactly what removes the
card-size dependence the full-card restriction existed to capture**: modelled
over n=72, the picks step's sd falls **11.71 → 2.37** and its max **55.05 →
13.76**. The common population now bounds the rare one far more tightly than
it did, so the restriction has stopped earning its 25 weeks.

**THE NEW SERIES STARTS EMPTY AND MEMBERSHIP IS BY COMMIT.** A run counts only
if its own `headSha` contains `cccb0e6` — resolved by one `git rev-list`, so a
run on a branch that predates the change cannot join on a later timestamp.
The four serial full-card runs do not contribute.

**REPORTED EVERY RUN**, so the clock is visible rather than remembered:

```
picks_bound[REGIME CHANGE IN PROGRESS]
  since          : cccb0e6 (2026-10-21T21:29 UTC)
  new population : n=0 -- the series is EMPTY, which is not a zero. No
                   scheduled weekday run has yet carried cccb0e6
  needed         : n>=10 -> ~2.0 weeks, about 2026-11-04
                   (simulated from ~5 scheduled weekday runs/week)
  margin uses    : the OLD constant, 88.1 min
  so the margin is CONSERVATIVE: that figure is a full-card MAX from the
  SERIAL regime, and the parallel review cut the picks step's sd 11.71 -> 2.37.
  The true margin is very probably BETTER than reported.
```

**AND THE ALERT SAYS IT TOO** (rule 3), so the operator dispatching by hand
knows what he is insuring against: the schedule-margin alarm now carries
`CONSERVATIVE: computed from FULL_CARD_PICKS_MAX=88.1m, a full-card MAX from
the RETIRED SERIAL review regime (n=4, 2026-10-01) … the replacement series is
at n=0/10, ~2.0 weeks to go (about 2026-11-04)`.

`MIN_N_TO_REDERIVE_PICKS_BOUND = 10` stays, with its reason beside it: the
weekday lateness series moved mean+3sd **417.5 → 428.9 on a single new point**
and the margin went **+40 → +37** overnight.

**TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN NEW CODE, both found by tests rather than by reading:**

* **An unreadable `gh` raised instead of reporting.** `json.loads("")` took the
  whole audit down, caught by `test_an_unreadable_gh_is_UNKNOWN_and_says_so`.
  It now returns `state: UNEVALUATED` — and that matters more than usual here,

* **It shelled out per run.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor` inside the loop

|---|---|---|---|
| **before** | **10** | 1 | **10:1** |
| **after** | **1** | 1 | **1:1** |

| line | disposition |
|---|---|
| `TRUNCATED LISTING: …` (two sites, 2 lines) | → `note:` |
| `no ledger history for <wf>` (5 lines) | → `note:` |
| `N run(s) listed above is a LOWER BOUND` | → `note:` |
| `N workflow record(s) GitHub holds that this repo does not own` | → `note:` |
| `N run(s) EXCLUDED because their headSha could not be read` | → `note:` |
| `X is UNEVALUATED, not safe — no run has yet …` | → `note:` |
| `workflow state UNKNOWN: gh workflow list could not be read` | → `note:` |
| `daily-picks carries no single cron — the margin is UNEVALUATED` | → `note:` |
| **pattern self-test failure** | **keeps `!!`** |
| **ACTIONABLE MARGIN** | **keeps `!!`** |
| **STRUCTURAL MARGIN deterioration** | **keeps `!!`** |
| **SCHEDULE MARGIN** | **keeps `!!`** |

Nothing was suppressed — every demoted line still prints, with its words. The
quiet run shows **10 `note:` lines** carrying the information.

#### THE DEMONSTRATION FOUND THE RULE'S OWN FIRST VIOLATION

Driving the zero-finding state on real data (the standing breach acknowledged
through the mechanism that exists for it) printed **1** mark, not 0 — because
the schedule-margin `!!` was emitted **before**
`margin_breach_is_acknowledged` was consulted. **An acknowledged breach, one
that deliberately does not alarm, still wore the finding marker.** Fixed: the
mark is gated on the absence of an acknowledgement, and the acknowledged path
reports as a `note:` rather than going silent. Then: **0 marks, exit 0.**

**AND AN INCIDENTAL CONFIRMATION WORTH KEEPING.** My first demo acknowledgement
was recorded at **19.0** and refused, because the real binding is
**18.89232917906861** and only *displays* as `+19`. A predicate reading the
rounded display would have absorbed a breach it was never shown. Pinned as a
test.

#### THE RESIDUE, NAMED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DEMOTED

**Three of the nine say "UNEVALUATED, not safe" or "UNKNOWN" and alarm on
nothing** — the day-type with no series, an unreadable `gh workflow list`, and
`daily-picks` carrying no single cron. Their words claim more than the alarm
set delivers. Changing what alarms is a different decision from reserving the
marker, so they are notes today and the mismatch is recorded in the source.

#### The ratio belongs beside the firings figure

```
firings per change (surface census, 30 days) : 163 / 5  = 33 : 1
marked lines per finding (output channel)    :  10 / 1  = 10 : 1  -> 1 : 1
```

They measure the same failure in two media — an alarm that repeats without
producing a change, and a marker worn by output that is not a finding. Both
train the reader to skip.

### THREE PNC ENTRIES, RESOLVED THREE DIFFERENT WAYS

The detector caught 33 → 35 and each was resolved on its merits, not in bulk:

* **`_sh_code` DELETED.** I added it for the per-run ancestor check and then
  replaced its only call with `rev-list`, leaving it dead. Mark-never-delete
  applies to DATA, not to producers.
* **`PARALLEL_REVIEW_SINCE_UTC` CONSUMED.** It is genuinely informative in the
  status block, which is where a reader asks "since when?" — so it is printed
  rather than kept as decoration.
* **`MARKER_IS_FOR_FINDINGS_ONLY` DELETED.** A bool whose only purpose is to be
  asserted `True` is near-vacuous; the rule's **text** is what the test should
  pin, and it already does.

## Telegram carries content and actions; the daily red was two lies and a crash — 2026-10-22

### FOUND FIRST, BEFORE ANY OF THE FOUR PARTS: THE AUDIT HAD BEEN DEAD FOR THREE RUNS

Running the audit to measure its Telegram volume crashed it:

```
File "scripts/ci_audit.py", line 1625, in parallel_regime_picks_series
    started = as_datetime(r.get("createdAt"))
NameError: name 'as_datetime' is not defined
```

**`as_datetime` never existed.** It shipped in `c2eef6d` yesterday and every
`ci-audit` run since has exited 2 with `CI AUDIT CRASHED — NOTHING was
audited` (runs `39671834491`, `39696939013`, `39714443682`). The crash banner
was correct and nobody read it.

**Why 2,312 tests passed over it.** `parallel_regime_picks_series` had **no
test at all**. The one test that reached `main()` stubs `_sh` to return `""`,
so the function took its UNEVALUATED early return and the loop below it was
never executed by anything. *A test that drives only the error branch
certifies the error branch.* `tests/test_picks_bound_series.py` now drives the
real path: a scheduled weekday run on the new commit IS counted, and five
shapes are NOT, each for its own stated reason.

**And the new test immediately caught a second defect in the same function.**
The unreadable-`gh` guard did not work:

```python
rows = json.loads(_sh("gh", "run", "list", ...) or "[]")
```

`or "[]"` turns **no output at all** into an empty list, so the `except
json.JSONDecodeError` only ever caught malformed *non-empty* JSON and an
unreadable `gh` reported **n=0** — the exact confusion the guard was added to
prevent, and n=0 is the state this series is legitimately in. Now: no output
and not-JSON are two separate `UNEVALUATED` returns with different reasons.

With the fix the series is live: **n=1, 35.1 minutes**, against the retired
serial constant of 88.1.

**KEPT — action:** the audit's actionable alarms, `reminders` `REMINDER DUE`,
the probe's FINDING/REFUSAL. **Transport:** `ci_alert` / `alert_delivery`.

| removed | what carries it now | fired |

| daily-picks `❌ workflow FAILED` | GitHub's notification; the LOSS report for the consequence; ci-audit | **11** |
| daily-picks critical-step send | the step STAYS and decides the colour; the log line keeps the step names | **9** |
| daily-picks ML-retrain alert | **NOTHING** — see below | 0 |

### PART B — `MARGIN ACKNOWLEDGED`

**THE FIGURE MOVED WHILE THE DIRECTIVE WAS BEING WRITTEN.** It said `+19m`;
the live binding is **`20.665799601890512`**, which displays as `+21`. Stored
at full precision, because on 2026-10-21 an acknowledgement recorded at the
rounded `19.0` correctly **refused** a real binding of `18.89232917906861`.

**THE FLOOR IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN.** The acknowledgement covers down to
`20.666 − 11.32 = +9.35`. 11.32 is the largest **ordinary** single-point move
of the binding, measured by recomputing it over growing prefixes of the
weekday series: `+5.53, +2.79, −11.32, −2.24, +1.77`. An acknowledgement
pinned to the reading itself would re-alarm within a day or two and the daily
red would be back.

**AND THE EXCLUDED MOVE IS THE FINDING OF THE PART.** The sixth move is
**−97.91**, and it is the moment the lateness series became **BIMODAL**:

```
weekday lateness, n=10, measured 2026-10-22
  2026-10-02 .. 10-09   255.9  256.8  304.9  271.7  282.7  285.8
  ── a ten-day gap ──
  2026-10-19 .. 10-22   128.4  144.1  137.7  132.0
```

**The cron did not change** — it is `0 0 * * 1-5` throughout. So `mean+3sd`
over this series is measuring **between-cluster spread, not tail risk**:
adding the first low point moved the binding −97.91 minutes *while the level
improved by 150*. That makes the `+21` reading conservative, and it is **not**
a licence to resegment on n=4 — splitting a series on an eyeballed gap at n=4
is `settled-pick-segments-are-noise`. Both clusters and "same cron" are
written into the acknowledgement so the claim stays checkable.

ready time is ours. **CLEARING ACTION:** manual dispatch today; durably, the
parallel series reaching n=10 and `FULL_CARD_PICKS_MAX` being re-derived.
**REVIEW 2026-11-04**, the projected date of exactly that.

**DRIVEN, not asserted:** it does not alarm at the level or at the floor, it
**does** alarm one hundredth below the floor, it covers improvements, and with
`date.today()` moved to 2026-11-05 it **refuses**. The weekend (+135.7) is

### PART C — `REMINDERS CLASSIFIED`: **FAILURE**, and the marker certified a lie

One run: `39714443709`, 2026-10-22 03:00 UTC, `workflow_run`, `c2eef6d`,
conclusion **failure**, `##[error]REMINDER DUE` **present**, exit annotation
present → `classify_red` returned **VERDICT**, correctly by its own rules.

**NO REMINDER WAS DUE.** Higher in the same log:

```
collected 1613 items / 17 errors / 1607 deselected / 1 skipped / 6 SELECTED
1 skipped, 1607 deselected, 17 errors in 4.16s
```

Seventeen modules could not be **imported** — the job installed a "minimal"
dependency set, and pytest must import every module under `tests/` to find the
marked ones. pytest stops at collection errors, so **six reminders were
selected and none ran**. It exited **2**; `continue-on-error` turned that into
the word `failure`; the classifier read `failure` as "a reminder is due" and
printed the marker itself. The same selection locally: **6 passed, 1 skipped —
nothing due.**

> **VERDICT 0, FAILURE 1.** A registered marker is only as honest as the
> predicate that prints it.

**THREE DEFECTS, THREE FIXES**, because any one alone would have produced the
false verdict:

1. **The classifier read the step OUTCOME.** It now branches on pytest's exit
   code: `0` nothing due, `1` **a decision is due**, `2/3/4/5` **NOT
   EVALUATED** — with a different, deliberately **unregistered** marker, so
   `ci-audit` returns FAILURE for it with no change to the audit.
2. **The install could not collect the suite.** `aiohttp beautifulsoup4 httpx
   pandas` added, with the measurement that justifies them. Not
   `-r requirements.txt`: that pulls transformers, playwright and camoufox for
   a job that trains nothing.
3. **Nothing checked the reminders had RUN.** A reminder that loses its
   `calendar` marker leaves the selection and pytest exits **0** — a clean
   result for a guard sailing past its date. The job now counts the tests that
   ran and compares against a floor of **7**, verified against the registry by
   AST (three other `@pytest.mark.calendar` decorators in the repo sit inside
   **string literals**, and a grep counts those).

**AND THE PLUMBING NEEDED `set +e`, NOT JUST `pipefail`.** Under `bash -e` a
failing pytest terminates the step *at* the pipeline and `rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}`
never runs. Driven both ways:

```
with    set +e   ->  pytest_rc=2 reminders_ran=0   (classifier: NOT EVALUATED)
without set +e   ->  <empty>                        (rc never reaches it)
```

Same family as the `| tee` that swallowed the coverage gate's exit code.

**VERIFIED END TO END** by extracting the shipped step and running it:
`pytest_rc=0, reminders_ran=7, exit 0` → "nothing due".

**WHAT `reminders` WILL REDDEN ON BETWEEN NOW AND 11-01.** Of the seven, the
only one driven by a date that has not passed is **`H1_RESERVATION_ACK_UNTIL =
2026-11-01`** — the H1 reservation acknowledgement, whose clearing action is
the deletion stage plus the re-run decision, already on the books for that
date. The other two calendar guards fired and had their decisions taken
(`EMPTY_CARD_UNTIL` 10-09; the H1 window 10-17, acknowledged 10-18). The
remaining four are `live` and depend on data, not the clock. **So: nothing
until 2026-11-01, then one VERDICT.**

### PART D — the three lines that claimed more than they delivered

Decided on this project's own test for an alarm — rare, actionable, **and
cleared by an action**. The third condition is what separated them:

| line | clears by | decision |
|---|---|---|
| a day type with no lateness series | the next scheduled run — **TIME** | **REWORDED** |
| `gh workflow list` unreadable | restoring GH_TOKEN — an **EDIT** | **ALARMS** |
| no cron for tomorrow's day type | editing the workflow — an **EDIT** | **ALARMS** |

* **REWORDED.** "Not safe" asserts a safety property the line cannot evaluate;
  it is reporting that there is nothing to evaluate. Now "margin NOT COMPUTED
  … neither clear nor breached", and it states *why* it does not alarm, so the
  mismatch is not rediscovered. An alarm here would be cleared by waiting,
  which is what CLR-2 exists to prevent.
* **ALARMS — and it is the one with no alternative carrier.** A disabled
  workflow produces no runs, so nothing else in the audit can detect one. When
  this check cannot look, that detector is **blind, not quiet**. Zero
  occurrences to date, so it costs nothing in volume.
* **ALARMS — read as a condition rather than as a margin.** It says
  `daily-picks` is **not scheduled to run tomorrow**. The uncomputable margin
  is the least of it.

Marked sites: **4 → 6**, and all six alarm.

## DST handled, the trade curve measured, and the retrain gap closed — 2026-10-22

### PART A — `DST HANDLED`

**Europe/Sofia goes UTC+3 → UTC+2 at 01:00 UTC on Sunday 2026-10-25** (the EU
rule: last Sunday of October). Verified from the zone database rather than
assumed, and the abbreviation moves with it: `EEST` → `EET`.

#### Every site that computes, displays or compares a local time

| site | derives or assumes | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `pipeline_loss_alert._in_tz` | **derives**, prints `%Z%z`, returns `(None, reason)` when the zone is unavailable | already correct |
| `fixture_horizon_probe._in_tz` | **derives**, identically | already correct |
| `match_briefing._kyiv` | ZoneInfo, but falling back to `timezone(timedelta(hours=3))  # EEST fallback` | **assumed +3** |
| `match_briefing` prompt header | `f"KICKOFF (Bulgarian time, EEST): ..."` | **literal label** |
| `telegram_bot` picks card | ZoneInfo, falling back to `timezone(timedelta(hours=2))` | **assumed +2** |
| `OBSERVED_EARLIEST_MIN` / `DEADLINE_FLOOR` | UTC minutes, anchored on **summer** kickoffs | see below |
| the crons | UTC, do not move | meaning shifts, nothing to fix |

**TWO FALLBACKS WITH OPPOSITE LITERALS, and nothing compared them.** The
briefing assumed `+3` and the card assumed `+2`; each is correct for roughly
half the year. Driven against `git HEAD`:

```
OLD _kyiv fallback (the literal +3), the same 09:30 UTC instant
  2026-10-24 -> 12:30   (correct, by luck of the season)
  2026-10-26 -> 12:30   <-- WRONG by an hour, and indistinguishable
                            from a real local time
```

**AND THE LABEL WAS UNCONDITIONALLY WRONG FROM 10-25.** `KICKOFF (Bulgarian
time, EEST)` asserts EEST while `_kyiv` prints 11:30, which is EET. That line
goes into the Claude prompt for every briefing.

#### What changed

* `_kyiv` → **`_operator_local(dt, with_zone=False)`** on a named
  `OPERATOR_TZ = "Europe/Sofia"`. The offset is derived; `with_zone=True`
  appends whatever `%Z` resolves to, which is what replaced the literal.
* **THE FALLBACK NO LONGER GUESSES.** With no zone database it returns
  `"09:30 UTC (Europe/Sofia unavailable)"`. *A wrong clock that looks right is
  worse than a right clock that looks foreign.*
* the card derives its offset, spells `Europe/Kyiv` (keeping the deprecated
  `Europe/Kiev` as a fallback) and prints `%H:%M %Z`.
* **NOT UNIFIED, and named instead:** briefings declare `Europe/Sofia`, the
  card declares `Europe/Kyiv`. Both are EET/EEST on the EU date so they have
  never differed by a minute — but they are two stated intents and only one
  can be what Niki means. Picking is a product decision, not a DST fix.

#### The two-sided test

`tests/test_dst_transition.py`, **14 tests, every one driven at 2026-10-24 and
2026-10-26** — a one-sided test cannot tell a derived offset from a literal
that happens to match today. It pins the transition date and direction from
tzdata first, so that if the zone database ever disagrees the expectations are
void rather than quietly wrong.

#### The crons do not move; their meaning does

`0 0 * * 1-5` and `0 0 * * 6,0` are UTC and GitHub does not reinterpret them.
A 00:00 UTC start is **03:00 local on 10-24 and 02:00 local on 10-26**.
Pinned, so the hour is not later mistaken for a scheduler regression.

#### THE FINDING THIS PART TURNED UP: the deadline floors are summer figures

`measured` 2026-10-22 over production `matches`, the 30 configured leagues,
phantoms excluded:

| day type | offset | n | min UTC | **min LOCAL** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| weekday | UTC+3 | 421 | 09:30 | **12:30** |
| weekday | UTC+2 | 297 | **10:30** | **12:30** |
| weekend | UTC+3 | 211 | 09:45 | 12:45 |
| weekend | UTC+2 | 164 | **10:00** | 12:00 |

**The weekday minimum is the same local time on both sides.** The kickoff is
fixed locally and its UTC minute moves with the clocks. Both anchors of
`OBSERVED_EARLIEST_MIN` were set during summer time — weekday 2023-10-26
(three days before that year's transition), weekend 2024-10-19 — so from
2026-10-25 the weekday floor is **60 minutes pessimistic** and the weekend
one 15. Pinned, **not changed**: moving a deadline is a Part C decision.

*(The wider all-non-`world/*` population has far earlier minima — weekday
08:00 UTC, weekend 09:00 — carried by `other/world`, `other/romania`,
`other/andorra`. The configured-league deadline ignores those rows. Stated as
a limitation of the constant, not altered here.)*

### PART B — `TRADE CURVE`

#### The cron is not the start, and the delay series is not one population

```
weekday lag  n=10  mean 220.0  sd 74.1  mean+3sd 442.3  max 304.9
  old cluster     n=6  mean 276.3  sd 17.1  mean+3sd 327.7  max 304.9
  recent cluster  n=4  mean 135.6  sd  5.9  mean+3sd 153.4  max 144.1
weekend lag  n=6   mean 253.2  sd 27.1  mean+3sd 334.5  max 293.7
```

The directive's `~4h36 mean / ~5h32 mean+3sd` are the **old cluster** (276.3 /
327.7). The pooled series gives **220.0 / 442.3**, and the recent four days
average **135.6**.

**THE CRON EACH START NEEDS, and this is the blocker:**

| start UTC | local post-DST | cron @ pooled | cron @ old cluster | cron @ recent cluster |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 07:30 "latest safe" | 09:30 | **00:08** | 02:02 | 04:56 |
| 08:15 intermediate | 10:15 | 01:04 | 02:47 | 05:41 |
| 09:00 (11:00 local) | 11:00 | 01:49 | 03:32 | 06:26 |

**Under the pooled reading the current `0 0` is already within eight minutes
of the latest safe cron. Under the recent cluster there are four and a half
hours of headroom.** Same data, same unchanged cron — the answer to "how late
may it run" differs by 4h48m depending on which cluster is believed. That, not
the fixture cost, is what Part C turns on.

#### Time-to-picks: three bounds, because the regime changed at n=1

```
serial   mean+3sd  85.6 min   `measured` 2026-10-21, weekday n=79
parallel mean+3sd  55.1 min   `simulated` 2026-10-21 over n=72 (sd 18.4 -> 10.8, +30.5m)
parallel           35.1 min   `measured` 2026-10-22, n=1 -- sd UNDEFINED
```

#### THE CURVE — cards partly lost and fixtures lost per year

Configured leagues, phantoms excluded, `ready = start + bound`, annualised
with the ZoneInfo-derived year split (UTC+2 155 days, UTC+3 210).

| start UTC | local | @ parallel 55.1 | @ serial 85.6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **07:30** latest safe | 09:30 | **0.0 cards / 0.0 fixtures** | **0.0 / 0.0** |
| **08:15** intermediate | 10:15 | **0.0 / 0.0** | **0.4 / 0.4** |
| **09:00** Niki's 11:00 | 11:00 | **0.7 / 0.7** | **18.3 / 24.9** |

Baseline `0 0` is 0.0/0.0 on every bound (its pooled mean+3sd start is 07:22).
At the single measured parallel observation (35.1) every candidate is 0.0/0.0.

**THE WHOLE TRADE IS THE PARALLEL REVIEW'S SIMULATED BOUND.** At 55.1 minutes
an 11:00 local start costs **0.7 fixtures a year**. At the measured serial
85.6 it costs **25**, and the weekend carries 24 of them.

**WHICH LEAGUES, measured:**

* at 55.1 — `bulgaria/efbet-league` ×2, and nothing else.
* at 85.6 — `netherlands/eredivisie` ×60, `poland/ekstraklasa` ×12,
  `bulgaria/efbet-league` ×9, `italy/serie-a` ×5,
  `finland/veikkausliiga` ×1. Dutch Saturday 12:30/12:45 local kickoffs are
  the binding population.

**AND THE DST EFFECT IS VISIBLE IN THE COST.** At a 09:00 start on the serial
bound, the weekend loses **54 of 211 summer days (25.6%)** but only **7 of 164
winter days (4.3%)** — the same start, the same leagues, one hour of UTC
shift. An 11:00 local start is materially cheaper in the regime that begins in
three days than in the one it is being measured from.

**No choice is made.** Part C waits on Niki's point.

### ADDENDUM A — the retrain gap, closed on the OUTCOME

**MEASURED 2026-10-22, and the two answers differ, which is the point:**

```
CI (the cache production uses)   trained_at 2026-10-21T09:07  ->    1 day
this working copy                trained_at 2026-03-31T07:35  ->  205 days
```

CI is healthy, so `scripts/model_freshness.py` ships as a **guard, not a
repair** — and the 205-day local copy is what it was driven against.

**IT CHECKS THE ARTEFACT, NOT THE STEP.** Does a model exist, what timestamp
does it carry, and which run first produced that timestamp. `if: always()`
with **no** condition on `steps.retrain_ml`: keying on the step would rebuild
the sender it replaces, and a step that exits zero while writing nothing is
exactly what the old alert could never catch.

**THE THRESHOLD IS DERIVED.** A retrain is attempted on the first run after
the model passes `ml_retrain_days`, so healthy maximum age is that plus one
scheduling gap. `measured` 2026-10-22 over **n=183** gaps between consecutive
scheduled daily-picks runs: p50 0.97, p95 1.04, p99 1.95, **max 9.18** (the
2026-06-01 outage).

```
threshold = ceil(ml_retrain_days + p99 gap) = ceil(3 + 1.95) = 5 days
```

p95 and p99 **both ceil to 5**, so the figure does not turn on the quantile
choice — worth saying, given the addendum's own Part B. The 9.18-day gap is an
outage, not a cadence, and during one `pipeline_loss_alert` already fires.

**IT IS CONTENT, so it goes to Telegram** under the rule set earlier today:
"the model has not been retrained since X" is a fact about the system that no
run's conclusion reports. It carries the **age**, which rises every day it
stays broken, so consecutive messages differ by construction — the defect
`pipeline_loss_alert` exists to prevent.

**BOTH CONTROLS DRIVEN:** a model within the threshold is silent and exits 0
(and at 0.1/1/3/4.9 days); a failed retrain (an old stamp surviving) and a
skipped one (**no artefact at all**) each alarm. `ABSENT` is `UNKNOWN`, not age
zero. A partial write — one artefact fresh, one 90 days old — is caught, and no
step outcome could see it.

**"BY WHICH RUN", without touching the signed pickle.** Adding a key would
change the signed bytes for a reporting nicety, so the run is recorded
*beside* the artefact in `retrain_provenance.json`. The check runs in the same
job as `--train`, so "first observed" is the writing run whenever the stamp
moved — driven: a later run observing an unchanged model does **not** take
credit.

**TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN NEW CODE, both found by its tests:**

* **A default argument cannot be monkeypatched.** `models_dir =
  MODELS_DIR` in the signature binds at *definition* time, so three tests
  pointed `mf.MODELS_DIR` at a temp directory and the function went on reading
  the real one — reporting the 205-day working copy from inside every fixture.
  Resolved at call time. *A default that cannot be substituted makes a
  function untestable, and silently ignores reassignment in production too.*
* **It opened with an emoji** and `print(body)` raised `UnicodeEncodeError` on
  a cp1251 console. *A detector that dies on its own output is worse than no
  detector.* Plain ASCII, as `pipeline_loss_alert` already was.

### ADDENDUM B — `mean+3sd` is conservative BY ACCIDENT; the successor is named

```
weekday n=10   mean 220.0   sd 74.1   mean+3sd 442.3   MAX 304.9
```

**The bound exceeds every observation by 137.5 minutes.** Three sd of a
two-cluster series is mostly the distance *between* the clusters, so the
margin buys over two hours of headroom against an event never seen.
*(Sample sd, which is what `schedule_margin` uses; population sd gives
70.3 / 430.9. One quantity, one quoted figure — the one that binds.)*

**AND THE DIRECTION IS NOT GUARANTEED.** Driven, both ways:

* let the lower cluster dominate and the excess over the max collapses — the
  headroom was a function of the mixture, not of risk;
* let a **rare** extreme appear and `mean+3sd` falls **below** the observed
  maximum, so it understates the tail with nothing in the statistic to say so.
  *(A first attempt got this wrong: three points at ~900 among ten left the
  bound at 1300, still above the max, because a cluster big enough to move the
  max also inflates the sd. The understating case needs the extreme to be
  RARE — and that is the real shape of this project's own gap series: p50 0.97
  days with one at 9.18.)*

**THE SUCCESSOR: the empirical p95.** No segmentation decision, cannot be
dragged by between-cluster distance, never outside the data. Nearest-rank and
**`None` below n = 1/(1−p)** — an interpolated p95 of nine points is a number
with no observation above it, the same extrapolation being retired.

**USABLE AT n ≥ 100**, from `n ≥ 5/(1−p)`: five observations strictly above it,
because one new point moved `mean+3sd` by **11.4 minutes** at n=9→10. p99 needs
n ≥ 500 — ~100 weeks at ~5 scheduled weekday runs a week — so it is named **out
of reach** rather than offered without a date. p95 projects to **2027-03-11**.

**AND IT IS NOT SWITCHED TO, because at n=10 NEITHER statistic is supported:**
`mean+3sd` extrapolates 137.5 minutes past the data and the p95 quantile would
simply be the maximum. Saying so is the honest state. Both print, labelled,
every run:

```
weekday  deadline 09:30  schedule_margin[n=10 … mean+3sd=7h22m …
                           binding=+21m threshold=30m  ** DECISION FIRES **]
            successor[p95 delay=UNDEFINED (n too small for any point to sit
            above it) (not usable until n>=100); mean+3sd BINDS today and is
            ABOVE the observed max 5h04m]
```

A positive control drives n=100 and checks the verdict flips to `(BINDS)` —
while `binding` still comes from `mean+3sd`, so the comparison cannot become a
replacement by accident.

### ADDENDUM C — the normalisation near-miss, recorded as a rule

> **A cosmetic normalisation of text a detector matches is a change to the
> detector.** Pin to what the consumer observes, treat every edit to matched
> text as an edit to the mechanism, and where the text is outside this file's
> control accept both forms.

Recorded at `extract()`, beside the patterns it governs. The regexes now take
either dash, driven on both; the workflow carries a "THE EM DASHES ARE
LOAD-BEARING" comment; and the anchor still rejects the workflow's own echoed
source, which is why it required a letter after the dash in the first place.
