## The deadline is localised; the cron move is BLOCKED on an invariant — 2026-10-22

### PART A — `DEADLINE LOCALISED`

A kickoff is scheduled by a human in a local clock, so its UTC minute moves
twice a year and a UTC anchor measured in one season is wrong in the other.
Both anchors were re-derived as the minimum **LOCAL** kickoff over the whole
record — Europe/Sofia, the 30 configured leagues, phantoms excluded
(`microsecond == 0`, `hour >= 6`):

| day type | anchor | n | set on | which was |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| weekday | **12:30 local** | 718 days | 2023-10-26 Thu, `bulgaria/efbet-league` | 09:30 UTC at UTC+3 |
| weekend | **12:00 local** | 375 days | 2024-11-02 Sat, `bulgaria/efbet-league` | 10:00 UTC at UTC+2 |

#### THE WEEKEND ANCHOR IS NOT THE SAME EVENT, AND THE CORRECTION RUNS BOTH WAYS

The retired weekend constant (09:45 UTC, 2024-10-19) was the minimum of the
**summer subset only**. The true local minimum is 12:00 and it comes from a
**winter** day — four of the five earliest local kickoffs are winter dates. So:

| day type | retired | 2026-10-24 (UTC+3) | 2026-10-26 (UTC+2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| weekday | 09:30 UTC | 09:30 UTC (**0**) | 10:30 UTC (**+60**) |
| weekend | 09:45 UTC | **09:00 UTC (−45)** | 10:00 UTC (+15) |

**Localising TIGHTENS the weekend floor by 45 minutes in summer.** The brief
called this part "free and worth 60 minutes"; it is worth 60 on the weekday in
winter and costs 45 on the weekend in summer. **A correction, not an
improvement, and not a gift.**

#### The margin before and after, labelled as a correction

| day | day type | deadline before → after | margin before → after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-24 | weekday | 09:30 → 09:30 | +20.7 → +20.7 | **0** |
| 2026-10-24 | weekend | 09:45 → 09:00 | +135.7 → +90.7 | **−45** |
| 2026-10-26 | weekday | 09:30 → 10:30 | +20.7 → **+80.7** | **+60** |
| 2026-10-26 | weekend | 09:45 → 10:00 | +135.7 → +150.7 | +15 |

**The standing weekday breach self-clears at the transition**: +20.7 (below
the 30 alarm, acknowledged to 2026-11-04) becomes **+80.7** on 2026-10-26,
from the correction alone and with no cron change.

#### AND THE ORDERING INVERTED

12:00 local < 12:30 local, so the **weekend** is the earlier floor — on both
sides, permanently rather than seasonally. The retired pair said the opposite
(09:30 < 09:45), which was an artefact of two summer figures measured on
different days. `SCHEDULE_DEADLINE_MIN` moved 570 → 540 and
`test_the_deadline_is_the_WEEKEND_kickoff_and_says_so` became true for the
first time since it was named.

*Which deadline is earlier and which margin is tighter are different
questions: the margin still fires on the weekday, because the weekday delay is
worse.*

#### What changed in the code

* `OBSERVED_EARLIEST_LOCAL_MIN` (local minutes) + `operator_offset_min(day)`,
  which reads the zone database per day and **raises rather than guessing** —
  a deadline from an assumed offset is an hour wrong for half the year,
  silently.
* `deadline_floor_for(day_type, day)` and `observed_earliest_min(day_type,
  day)`: **the day is required**.
* `RETIRED_OBSERVED_EARLIEST_UTC_MIN` kept — a localisation that deletes what
  it localised cannot be audited, and both figures being summer ones *is* the
  defect.
* `DEADLINE_FLOOR` / `DEADLINE_MIN_BY_DAYTYPE` survive as mappings that
  **resolve on each lookup** for tomorrow, so fourteen call sites keep working
  without snapshotting a season at import. `schedule_margins_by_daytype` takes
  a `day` and asks per day, and `_tomorrow` is hoisted so the margin and the
  alarm cannot describe different days across a transition.
* The two functions that serve a named day now pass it.

#### The sweep, and one site that is NOT a localisation

Every UTC constant of human-scheduling origin is now derived:
`OBSERVED_EARLIEST_MIN`, `DEADLINE_FLOOR`, `DEADLINE_MIN_BY_DAYTYPE`,
`SCHEDULE_DEADLINE_MIN`, and the last-safe-dispatch figure — which was already
computed from the discovered kickoff per day and so follows automatically.

**`theodds_scraper._PICKS_CRON_MINUTE_OF_DAY = 3 * 60` is NOT one of these.**
It is OUR cron, in UTC, and does not move with DST — but it is **stale by
three hours**: the cron has been `0 0` since 2026-10-18. Inside that window
the guard reserves credits for a pending picks run, so a window opening too
late leaves the run unprotected at the start of its own schedule. It belongs
to the cron move and is held with Part B.

#### Both-sided tests

`tests/test_dst_transition.py` is now **16 tests**, every one driven at
**2026-10-24 and 2026-10-26**, and the both-sided discipline was propagated to
the five other files that asserted a UTC deadline value. The transition date
and direction are checked from tzdata **first**, so if the zone database ever
disagrees the expectations are void rather than quietly wrong. One new test
pins that `operator_offset_min` raises with no zone database.

#### Three self-inflicted defects, all caught by tests

* **The ninth comment-blind scan, twice in one file of mine.** The quoted old
  code lives in a **docstring**, so stripping `#` lines does not reach it;
  `conftest.code_of` tokenises and does.
* **`hours=3` matched `timedelta(hours=30)`** — the unrelated 30-hour World Cup
  window. Anchored on the closing paren.
* **A width is not an order, twice more.** A `[-1400:]` window and a
  `split(...)[1]` scan both broke on inserted comments; both are now
  order/presence assertions, one of them via `code_of`. That test's own
  comments already recorded being bitten twice.

**And one guard caught me correctly:** `date.today()` in a gating test made
the capture gate refuse the whole selection. The property held for any day, so
two named days prove it.

**PNC:** the `OBSERVED_EARLIEST_MIN` compatibility shim was flagged as a new
orphan (consumed only from tests) and **deleted** rather than declared — four
test modules now ask the function. Mark-never-delete applies to data, not to
shims.

## `CRON MOVED` — weekday `0 1`, weekend `30 0`, `s5.19` — 2026-10-22

### THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE DERIVATION SET OUT TO SAY

**This is a trade, not a repair.** Corrected while writing the tests for it.

The retired weekday margin read **+20.7**, below even the 30-minute alarm, and
the first draft of both the workflow comment and the cohort entry called the
move a repair on that basis. **+20.7 is the POOLED figure**, and a pooled
`mean+3sd` over a bimodal series measures between-cluster distance. Under the
**slow cluster** — the population that governs — the old cron had **+130.4**:
it cleared the registered 60 with seventy minutes to spare.

```
weekday, summer floor 09:30 UTC, slow cluster
  old cron `0 0`   binding +130.4      <- cleared
  new cron `0 1`   binding  +70.4      <- clears
  cost of the move          -60.0 minutes of real margin
```

So the move **spends 60 minutes of genuine margin to buy an hour of start
time**. That is legitimate and it is Niki's call. It is written down as a trade
because a change sold as a fix does not get re-examined and a change sold as a
trade does.

### PART A — the cron, as derived

```
weekday lag, measured 2026-10-22, ONE unchanged cron throughout
  SLOW  n=6  mean 276.3  sd 18.8  max 304.9  mean+3sd 332.6
  fast  n=4  mean 135.6  sd  6.9  max 144.1  mean+3sd 156.2
weekend lag  n=6  mean 253.2  sd 29.7  max 293.7  mean+3sd 342.3
  largest-gap / median-gap: weekday 17.33, weekend 2.61 -> only the
  weekday splits (threshold 8.0, PROVISIONAL and labelled so)
```

Each cron is the **latest 15-minute boundary clearing the registered 60 on
BOTH pairings** the margin takes the worse of, at the **summer** floor (summer
binds: one UTC cron serves both seasons and summer's floor is the earlier one):

```
weekday  cap(max 304.9, picks  88.1) = 117.0
         cap(3sd 332.6, picks 107.0) =  70.4  binds  ->  `0 1`  = 01:00 UTC
weekend  cap(max 293.7, picks  88.1) =  98.2
         cap(3sd 342.3, picks 107.0) =  30.7  binds  ->  `30 0` = 00:30 UTC
```

#### The start times, per cluster, in both clocks

| day type | cluster | reading | UTC | Sofia summer | Sofia winter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| weekday | SLOW | mean+3sd | 06:33 | **09:33** | 08:33 |
| weekday | SLOW | mean | 05:36 | 08:36 | 07:36 |
| weekday | fast | mean+3sd | 03:36 | 06:36 | 05:36 |
| weekday | fast | mean | 03:16 | **06:16** | 05:16 |
| weekend | — | mean+3sd | 06:12 | **09:12** | 08:12 |
| weekend | — | mean | 04:43 | 07:43 | 06:43 |

**So the answer to "11:00" is +1h on the weekday and +30m on the weekend.** A
single UTC cron cannot deliver a fixed local start while the delay is bimodal,
and averaging the clusters would describe neither. *(The first start table in
this stage was computed at the rejected `0 2` and was an hour and a quarter
early in UTC; caught by its own test.)*

#### The margins, at both floors

| | weekday | weekend |
|---|---|---|
| **summer** (09:30 / 09:00) | +117.0 / **+70.4** | +128.2 / **+60.7** |
| **winter** (10:30 / 10:00) | +177.0 / **+130.4** | +188.2 / **+120.7** |

Every pairing clears 60. The next 15-minute boundary later fails, so these are
the latest.

#### `0 2` REJECTED, and why that refusal is the rule

It is not a strawman: at the **parallel** picks bound (55.1, `simulated` n=72;
the **measured** parallel series is **n=1** at 35.1) `0 2` clears 60 and puts
the slow case at **10:33 Sofia** — nearer what was asked.

**It leaves the margin at `+10.4` under the picks constants this project still
retains** (`FULL_CARD_PICKS_3SD = 107.0`) — under the 30-minute alarm, never
mind the 60-minute minimum. Those constants are retained *because* the
parallel bound is n=1.

> **A configuration the project's own instrument calls a breach is not
> shipped.**

Both halves are pinned: that `0 2` would clear at the parallel bound, and that
it breaches at the retained one. If either premise moves the decision re-opens
rather than staying refused.

#### The per-cluster report, which the move made necessary

Without it the audit would have alarmed every day after the move. At `0 1` the
weekday line now reads:

```
schedule_margin[n=10 ... | POOLED margin max=+117m 3sd=-39m pooled_binding=-39m]
  BIMODAL (gap ratio >= 8.0): the pooled mean+3sd measures BETWEEN-CLUSTER
    distance, not tail risk
  split rule: largest consecutive gap / median consecutive gap; measured
    2026-10-22 as 17.33 (weekday, n=10) and 2.61 (weekend, n=6) ...
  slow[n=6 ... binding=+70m] GOVERNS
  fast[n=4 ... binding=+247m] reported, NOT relied on
  BINDING +70m from slow cluster, threshold 30m
```

**The pooled reading at the new cron is −39m.** It is kept, labelled, because
every earlier ledger entry quotes it — and it is exactly the artefact the
per-cluster report exists to stop binding on.

#### Lead time and the discovered-fixture population

Lead time per day type and per **cluster**, because an average across a
bimodal series describes neither — the table above. Shift: **+60 min weekday,
+30 min weekend.**

**The discovered-fixture population does not move,** measured not assumed.
`max_days_ahead` is a rolling `now + 1 day`, so the cutoff moves *later* with
the run; the binding site is a Friday run reaching into Saturday, whose
earliest kickoff is 10:30 UTC. **All six date-derived sites were re-enumerated
against both new crons and all pass,** with the Friday→Saturday clearance
still above the registered hour. Zero D+1 fixtures admitted under either cron.

**Cohort: `s5.18 / 51fbcb` → `s5.19 / cdec29`, 0 picks stamped.** The pin and
the four revision pins moved in this commit with the argument beside each, as
authorised; **no test was relaxed.**

### PART B — the overnight-slot guard, and the worry reverses

**`_PICKS_CRON_MINUTE_OF_DAY = 3 * 60` was stale by three hours** — the cron
had been `0 0` since 2026-10-18 and nothing tied the two. Inside that window
the guard *reserves* credits for a pending picks run, so a window opening
**after** the cron leaves the run unprotected at the start of its own
schedule.

**Every slot enumerated** against `closing-lines`' own crons (`47 10` and
`17 11,13,15,17,19,21,23`):

| slot | in OLD [03:00,16:00] | in NEW [00:30,13:30] | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10:47 | yes | yes | |
| 11:17 | yes | yes | |
| 13:17 | yes | yes | |
| **15:17** | yes | **no** | **now always proceeds** |
| 17:17 … 23:17 | no | no | |

```
slots that can decline:              4/8  ->  3/8
captures newly EXPOSED per week:     0
captures newly PROTECTED per week:   7
```

**The move IMPROVES the guard.** The early edge gains nothing because **the
first capture slot is 10:47** — there is no slot between 00:30 and 03:00 to
expose — and the late edge loses one. And the three remaining exposed slots
decline only on a day that produced no picks: on every reading picks are done
by **08:08–09:01 UTC**, before 10:47, and the guard stands down the moment any
pick exists for the day.

**The 01:17 / 02:17 failures were about hours at which no capture runs.** The
test's parametrisation was `[21, 23, 1, 2]`; 21:17 and 23:17 are real slots
and 01:17 and 02:17 are not.

**Both controls, and the 2026-09 incident reproduced:** the five protected
slots must **not** decline with the database seeded in exactly the state that
caused the incident (a league holding an unpicked fixture, no pick written for
the day — the condition the reverted date-marker guard turned on); the three
exposed slots **must** decline. And the window start is now **tied to the
cron** by a test, so it cannot diverge again.

### PART C — the series reset, as a cost of this move

Membership keys on the run's own `headSha` carrying the cron in force, so the
move **empties the lag series**. The margin reports NOT COMPUTED until the new
crons fire, and `test_the_weekday_cron_CLEARS_the_stated_margin_and_LATEST_IS_RETIRED`
now **SKIPS** — the honest state, visible rather than a false pass.

**The second step slips: 2026-11-04 → 2026-11-06.** `simulated` 2026-10-22
from ~5 scheduled weekday runs/week: n≥10 under the new cron takes ~2.0 weeks
from the first run on 2026-10-23. **Attributed to this move rather than
discovered later.**

**Both series are retained and labelled by cron, never pooled** — the
`390a4be` rule. Pooling `0 0` with `0 1` would reproduce the error that chose
`0 4` from another cron's spread.

**The condition is unchanged**, only its date moved: n≥10 by `headSha`, no
point above 200m, gap ratio below 8.0, mean+3sd ≤ 156.2. Both controls driven:
the slow cluster **fails** it, a pure fast series **passes** every clause. And
the reminder that reports it now fires when the condition becomes
**evaluable** (n=10), not on the first run under the new cron.

### PART D — two things the correction changed that outlive it

**1. The weekend is the earlier floor on both sides, permanently.** 12:00 local
against 12:30. `SCHEDULE_DEADLINE_MIN` 570 → 540. Swept for places assuming
the weekday bound: the hits are all about the weekday **margin**, which
correctly still binds because the weekday **delay** is worse. *Which deadline
is earlier and which margin is tighter are different questions* — and this
analysis conflated them for weeks. The weekend cron moved as a direct result;
the previous entry had left it untouched on the reasoning that it had least to
gain, which was true only while the floors were stored UTC constants.

**2. The standing weekday breach cleared by a measurement correction, not by
the pipeline.** +20.7 → **+80.7** on 2026-10-26, from the localisation alone —
the floor moved 09:30 → 10:30 UTC because the anchor is a local time and the
clocks went back. **Nothing got faster.** Recorded so nobody later reads it as
the parallelisation's doing.

### DISCIPLINE

Gating selection **2,471 passed, 9 deselected**; non-gating 7 passed, 2
skipped (both skips are UNEVALUATED states, not passes). **Invariants 26
passed** — rule 8's exemption applied to 6b and the four revision pins, with
the argument in `tests/experiment_pins.py` and no test relaxed. Every workflow
YAML parses. Fingerprint **`s5.19 / cdec29`**, as rule 7 ordered.

PNC: one new entry, `LAG_CLUSTER_PROVENANCE`, **consumed** rather than
declared — it is printed on the BIMODAL line, which is where a reader asks why
the series splits and why at 8.0.

**Carried forward:** the second step on **2026-11-06**, with its four-clause
condition; the picks-bound re-derivation when the parallel series reaches
n=10; and `0 2` re-opens if either premise of its rejection moves.

> A state recorded as expected is not a state that is handled.

Fixed by keying the guard on **the absence of the value** (`a.get("binding")

**AND THE PREDICTED `−39m` FINDING WAS NOT THERE** — the audit never reached

#### A third false finding, from the same family

Today's `daily-picks` 39906308477 was scored **BROKEN** with
`core step(s) reported failure: update, picks` and `1 traceback(s)` — while
**every critical step succeeded** and the loss step was skipped. Both hits
were false, and both were the audit reading text that is a DEFINITION:

* **the echoed `run:` block.** GitHub prints every script into the log inside
  `##[group]Run …`, and the matched line was a COMMENT I wrote on 2026-10-22

  — update, picks". A list of …`. The 2026-10-13 remedy — require a letter
  after the dash — excludes the emitting line and not a comment with a real

* **a pytest test-ID line.**
  `test_KNOWN_WRONG_a_reminders_red_WITHOUT_the_marker_is_a_FAILURE[Traceback
  (most recent call last)…]` — a test PARAMETRISED ON THE STRING "Traceback",
  counted as one.

> An anchor narrows a pattern. Removing the echo removes the class.

`strip_non_output()` now drops both before any pattern runs: the
`##[group]Run` → `##[endgroup]` region, and pytest's `tests/…::…` progress
lines. Measured on today's log: 826 lines removed, `steps_failed` `[…] → []`,
`tracebacks` `1 → 0`, and a real traceback still counts 1.

**AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT FIX CHANGED NOTHING IN PRODUCTION.** It
dropped a line only if it carried the echo's ANSI colour — and `fetch_log`
runs `ANSI.sub("", …)` before `extract` ever sees the log. It passed a direct
test against a raw `gh` log and I called it a fix for the pipeline.

> Testing the function is not testing the path the data takes.

### PART A — `MARGIN PER CLUSTER`

**The alarm already read the slow cluster** — yesterday's change made
`binding` come from it. Measured from the output today: the pooled figure
prints labelled, the slow cluster is marked `GOVERNS`, the fast one `reported,
NOT relied on`, and the line names which population `BINDING` came from.

**WHAT WAS MISSING IS THE THIRD STATE.** `split_lag_clusters` returns
`(vals, None)` both when a series is genuinely unimodal and when it is too
small to tell — and at today's **n=1** that would have bound a `mean+3sd` on a
single observation and called it a measurement.

```
cluster_state(lags) -> BIMODAL | UNIMODAL | UNSEPARABLE
  UNSEPARABLE below LAG_CLUSTER_MIN_N = 4: reports, does NOT alarm
```

**The known-wrong control, driven:**

```
today's pooled -39.4m   cluster_state BIMODAL   BINDING +70.3 (slow)  alarm False
a real slow breach      cluster_state BIMODAL   BINDING -49.7 (slow)  alarm True
today's n=1 series      cluster_state UNSEPARABLE                     alarm False
```

**AND THE CONTROL CAUGHT A FLAW IN THE RULE AS FIRST WRITTEN.** Five
*identical* observations have every gap zero, so `med <= 0` classified them
UNSEPARABLE and **silenced a genuine breach**. A zero median is now told apart
from a zero *widest* gap: all gaps zero is a single point mass and therefore
UNIMODAL; a zero median with a non-zero widest gap is an infinite ratio and
the most bimodal a series can be.

### PART B — `RED REDEFINED`

```
NEW            no recorded occurrence                     -> RED
DETERIORATED   worse than the recorded figure              -> RED
UNACKNOWLEDGED recorded, but its review date has passed    -> RED
UNCHANGED      within the derived tolerance of the record  -> prints
```

**MACHINERY ALWAYS REDDENS**, outside the classifier entirely — `_main_guarded`
returns `EXIT_CRASH` and the workflow branches on it, so no classification can
make a broken audit quiet.

**THE TOLERANCE IS DERIVED.** `FINDING_TOLERANCE_MINUTES = 11.32`, the largest
*ordinary* single-point move of the binding (`measured` 2026-10-22: +5.53,
+2.79, −11.32, −2.24, +1.77, excluding the −97.91 cluster boundary) — the same
figure the standing acknowledgement's floor uses. For a **count** the
tolerance is **zero**: one more absent scheduled run is a new fact, not
jitter.

**A keyed finding carries its identity and figure from the site that RAISES
it**, never recovered from its wording. The schedule margin — the finding that
reddened this workflow every day for two weeks — is the first.

#### The four controls, all driven through `_emit_alarms`

| control | result |
|---|---|
| unchanged acknowledged finding | **exit 0**, prints with its figure and review date, nothing to Telegram |
| the same finding deteriorated | **exit 1**, `DETERIORATED`, reaches Telegram |
| a new finding | **exit 1**, `NEW: no recorded occurrence` |
| a crash with no finding at all | **`EXIT_CRASH`**, banner says `NOTHING was audited` |

Driven through the emitter and not against the classifier alone: the exit code
is what the workflow reads, and a classifier returning the right word while
the emitter ignored it would pass a test on the word.

**TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN NEW CODE, both found by these controls:**

* `tol, worse = FINDING_TOLERANCE_COUNT, figure > rec["figure"] + tol` —
  `UnboundLocalError`. **The count branch had never been exercised**; a
  tolerance kind nothing drove was dead code wearing a parameter's clothes.
* an always-empty `keyed_status` seam, built and then **removed** rather than
  left — a parameter no caller populates is not a seam.

#### A second mechanism, built and NOT shipped

A per-run verdict keyed by run id with the **ledger** as its record of "already
reported" was built, measured, and **removed**. The measurement is why:

```
30 sampled alarming runs: `daily-picks DID_NOT_RUN` in 30 of 30 firings
  five real events, relayed 12, 10, 5, 2 and 1 times
  ALL FIVE are in RESOLVED_RUNS, recorded 2026-10-18 by 7514a50 / 465146a
  re-audited today over 2026-10-13 onward -- 156 rows, those five included --
  they produce ZERO alarms
```

> The mechanism was not missing. It was not filled in.

`RESOLVED_RUNS` owns that case and demonstrably works; a second table
suppressing the same alarm would leave a run suppressed for two different
reasons with no single place to look. `ledger_run_ids()` went with it.

## The source echo is stripped, and the question asked in both directions — 2026-10-23

### THE RULE THIS LEAVES BEHIND

> **A detector that reads logs containing its own source will match itself.**
> **Comment-blindness is a property of the INPUT PATH, not of the scanner.**

This project has applied comment-blindness to the **code** eleven times —
`conftest.code_of` exists for it — and never once to the **log**, although the
log contains the code. GitHub prints every step's shell source into it inside
`##[group]Run …` / `##[endgroup]`.

Recorded beside the input path, and the strip runs **inside `extract()`** so a
caller cannot forget it.

### WHAT WAS CONFIRMED BEFORE STRIPPING: nothing real lives only in the echo

`measured` 2026-10-23 over the **156 cached real logs** in `ci_logs/`, every
registered `PATTERNS` entry tested against the removed region and the surviving
region separately:

```
PATTERNS matching ONLY inside the stripped echo : 0
PATTERNS matching only outside (unaffected)     : 23 keys
```

So no case needed keeping explicitly. The one signal that *does* live only in
the echo is the **producer** form `::error::` — and the project already pins
its marker to the consumer form `##[error]`, which appears in real output.
That decision is why this strip costs nothing.

### END TO END, on the path the data takes

`extract()` with the strip against `extract()` without it, over all 156 logs.
**Exactly three facts in three logs moved, every one a false positive:**

```
tracebacks    1 -> 0                                  in 2 logs
steps_failed  ['update, picks". A list of'] -> []      in 1 log
```

Nothing else changed. The figures are pinned in
`STRIP_EFFECT_MEASURED`, because `ci_logs/` is a local cache and is not
committed; a `live` test re-runs the comparison wherever the cache exists and
refuses any fact moving outside that set.

### THE THREE KNOWN-WRONG CONTROLS

| control | what it was | now |
|---|---|---|
| the echoed **comment** | `# It sent "⚠️ Daily picks: step(s) FAILED — update, picks". A list of` — written 2026-10-22 *about* the removed sender, matched 2026-10-23 as `core step(s) reported failure` on a run whose every step succeeded | `steps_failed == []` |
| the **pytest ID** | `test_…_is_a_FAILURE[Traceback (most recent call last)]` — a test parametrised on the string, counted as a traceback | `tracebacks == 0` |
| **`870`** inside a run id | the source-side instance, 2026-10-18: `870` matched `38708288664` in a `RESOLVED_RUNS` comment and reported a deadline literal that was not there | word-bounded, and the boundary is pinned |

The third is the same class in the other medium — a scanner matching inside a
longer token — so it is kept as a control rather than filed separately.

### THE POSITIVE CONTROL: the signal survives

A real traceback and a real `##[error]` **outside** the echo are still found,
with a comment mentioning both **inside** it being removed. *A strip that
removes the signal with the noise is the worse failure.* Also pinned: only
`##[group]Run ` is treated as an echo, so `##[group]Operating System` and its
siblings keep their contents; and an **unterminated** group is stripped to the
next boundary rather than to EOF, with the choice stated.

### AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT PASSED ITS UNIT TEST AND CHANGED NOTHING

It dropped a line only if it carried the echo's ANSI colour. `fetch_log` runs
`ANSI.sub("", …)` **before** `extract` ever sees the log, so there was no
colour left to match — and I had tested the function against a raw
`gh run view --log` and called it a fix for the pipeline.

> **Testing the function is not testing the path the data takes.**

Pinned as a test: `fetch_log` must still strip ANSI, the group boundaries
(which survive it) are what is used, and `_ECHO_COLOUR` must stay out of the
**code** — an assertion that, in its first form, matched the comment recording
that `_ECHO_COLOUR` had been deleted. **The eleventh comment-blind scan, inside
the test about comment-blindness.**

### THE OTHER DIRECTION, ASKED ONCE ACROSS EVERY CANDIDATE

`pnc_scan`'s `KNOWN_INSTANCES` self-suppression was exactly this shape, so the
question is whether anything else has it. All five verdicts measured
2026-10-23 and recorded in `SELF_MATCH_CENSUS`:

| candidate | verdict |
|---|---|
| `pnc_scan` / `KNOWN_INSTANCES` | **WAS REAL.** A blanket string-as-reference visitor made the scanner's own table of symbol *names* suppress its own findings. Already guarded — `visit_Constant` must stay absent, pinned by `test_pnc_detector`. |
| the ledger / `ledger_history` | **CLEAN, measured:** 498 parsed rows, every id 10–12 digits, five real workflow names, not one row from prose or from the markdown tables the entries contain. |
| the workflow crons / `current_crons_by_daytype` | **CLEAN BY CONSTRUCTION:** `^\s*- cron:` anchors to the line start. Driven with a file carrying a commented-out `0 2` — the *rejected* option, which is exactly what a comment there holds — and the parse was unchanged. |
| `ci-audit`'s own run logs | **BY DESIGN.** It is in `WORKFLOWS`, so it audits itself: 76 of the 156 cached logs are its own, and every fact it extracts from them is either a partition term that exists for that purpose (`self_emitted_annotations`, `self_emitted_exits`) or a **real** traceback — 8 of 76, all from the two crash episodes of 2026-10-22/23. |
| `RESOLVED_RUNS` / the pattern registry | **NO RUNTIME SELF-SOURCE READ.** The registry self-tests through `PATTERN_EXAMPLES`, which is the point. The `870` case was a *test* scanning `ci_audit.py`. |

### DISCIPLINE

Gating selection **2,502 passed, 10 deselected**; non-gating 8 passed, 2
skipped. Invariants pass, count not cited. Every workflow YAML parses. PNC
scan exits 0. Fingerprint **UNCHANGED at `s5.19 / cdec29`**.

**And the reminders floor moved 9 → 10 — the second time in two days.** Adding
a `live` test without raising it re-opens the masking hole every time (7
against a selection of 9 yesterday, 9 against 10 today), so the registry now
carries an entry whose comment says so, and the next `live` test added has to
pass through it.

*Recorded 2026-10-23. `scripts/ci_audit.py`,
`tests/test_source_echo_is_stripped.py`,
`tests/test_reminders_are_evaluated.py`, `.github/workflows/reminders.yml`.*

## Two hand-maintained couplings, both made mechanical — 2026-10-23

> **A remedy that must be remembered is not a remedy.** Third confirmation —
> after the calendar marker and the dialect assertion, both of which only
> stopped recurring once a mechanism refused them.

### PART A — the reminders floor becomes an equality

**It was 7, then 9, then 10 inside two days.** Every `live` test added
re-opened the masking hole the floor existed to close, and the reminder to
raise it lived **in the registry** — which is where the previous two
remember-this remedies also lived.

**BOTH SIDES NOW COME FROM THE SELECTION ITSELF.** pytest reports how many
tests it SELECTED; `-v` prints one result line per test that produced an
outcome:

```
sel=$(grep -oE "[0-9]+ selected" logs/reminders.txt | tail -1 | …)
ran=$(grep -cE "^tests.*::.* (PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|XFAIL|XPASS)" …)
```

and the classifier requires `ran == sel`. **There is no number left to
maintain.** Driven end to end on the shipped step: `SELECTED=10 RAN=10
(SKIPPED=2, ERRORED=0)`.

**A reminder collected and not run is the defect the floor was
approximating**, and the equality catches it without a literal — an error at
setup, a crash between tests, a worker dying. The old floor could only catch
it if the shortfall happened to cross a number someone had remembered to
update.

#### Three states, kept apart

* **`SKIPPED` is not `DID_NOT_RUN`.** A `live` reminder skips when its input
  is absent, which is a legitimate outcome: it RAN. The count is reported
  separately so a run where *every* reminder skipped is visible rather than
  reading as a clean pass.
* **An `ERROR` line is not an outcome.** A test that errors at setup was
  attempted and produced no result, so it is deliberately absent from `ran` —
  the count then falls short of `sel` and the run reports NOT EVALUATED,
  which is what an errored reminder is.
* **An EMPTY selection is checked FIRST**, because `0 == 0` satisfies an
  equality. An empty selection is not an empty set of reminders: it means the
  markers or the `-m` expression changed and **nothing was asked**.

#### Both known-wrong controls, driven

| control | result |
|---|---|
| a reminder collected and not run (`ran < sel`, four shapes) | **exit 1**, `N of M SELECTED`, nothing to Telegram |
| a reminder legitimately skipped (`ran == sel`, all skips) | **exit 0**, `9 SKIPPED` reported, not NOT-EVALUATED |
| an errored reminder | **exit 1**, `1 errored`, NOT EVALUATED |
| an empty selection | **exit 1**, `SELECTED NO TESTS` |

**And no literal remains in that path**, with a test that one cannot be
reintroduced: `REMINDERS_EXPECTED_MIN` must be absent from the workflow, and
none of `== 7 / == 9 / == 10` (the three values it took in two days) may
reappear as a comparison. That test is itself comment-blind by construction,
because it asserts the ABSENCE of literals and its own comments name them —
the twelfth instance, avoided rather than discovered.

*The registry survives for a different job: it catches a reminder that LOSES
ITS MARKER, which is not the same defect. Renamed `REMINDERS_REGISTERED`, and
a blanket rename briefly made its own guard vacuous — it checked for the new
name, which the workflow has never contained, so it passed while saying
nothing. Caught and restored.*

### PART B — `code_of` is required, not remembered

#### The census, first, because the number decides the shape

`measured` 2026-10-23 over every `tests/test_*.py` that reads a `.py` source
and makes a **negative** assertion:

```
48  RAW text, no stripping at all
 8  HAND-ROLLED stripper (`l.split("#", 1)[0]`)
 5  uses conftest.code_of          (correct)
--
61  total
```

**The remedy exists in three forms and 5 of 61 use the right one.** The eight
hand-rolled ones handle the comment half and **not the docstring half** —
which is exactly the half that bit on 2026-10-22 (a quoted old code line in a
docstring) and 2026-10-23 (the record that `_ECHO_COLOUR` had been deleted).

**THE DEFECT SHAPE WAS NARROWED BY MEASUREMENT.** A first census of *all*
matching gave **132 sites in 57 files**; restricting to NEGATIVE assertions —
the form that false-fires on a comment — gave 61. A positive assertion cannot
break the same way: at worst a comment satisfies it, which is weaker and is
often where the thing is legitimately recorded.

#### So it is a RATCHET, and the reason is stated

Converting 56 sites blind would change what 56 tests assert, and **the
load-bearing question cannot be settled statically for 29 of them** — they
read through a helper or a fixture, so the target file is not resolvable from
the AST. That is said rather than papered over with a confident number: two
earlier cuts of this census produced 8 and then 6 "prose-only" sites, and
both were artefacts of loose target attribution. One of the six turned out to
be a site that *already* hand-rolls a stripper.

The ratchet refuses GROWTH — the shape `test_pnc_detector`'s backlog already
uses, and the only one this project has made work:

```
BASELINE = {"raw": 48, "hand": 8}      # may fall, never rise
```

**Driven**: adding a twelfth raw negative assertion fails it with
`grew from 48 to 49` and the three clearing actions (route through `code_of`,
declare an exemption with a reason, or lower the number).

#### The known-wrong control and the positive control, on one input

The **eleventh instance verbatim** — `assert "_ECHO_COLOUR" not in src`
against raw text, with the comment recording the deletion reproduced —
**raises** `AssertionError`; **the same assertion through `code_of` passes**,
and still sees the code it is meant to check. Both directions on one fixture,
which is what makes it a control rather than an illustration.

**Exemptions take the dialect/marker shape**: a site that must match raw text
declares itself with a reason. Two today, both of them controls, and a test
refuses the list growing past four — *an exemption list that absorbs the
backlog makes the mechanism vacuous.*

**And the rule is recorded where the instrument lives**, in `tests/conftest.py`
beside `code_of`, pointing at the mechanism that now requires it — so the next
reader is told it is required rather than offered.

### DISCIPLINE

Gating selection **2,512 passed, 10 deselected**; non-gating 8 passed, 2
skipped. Invariants pass, count not cited. Every workflow YAML parses.
Fingerprint **UNCHANGED at `s5.19 / cdec29`** — both parts are test and
notification machinery.

*Recorded 2026-10-23. `.github/workflows/reminders.yml`, `tests/conftest.py`,
`tests/test_reminders_are_evaluated.py`, `tests/test_code_of_is_enforced.py`.*

## Every matcher asserts its anchor — 2026-10-23

> **A matcher with zero hits has not verified anything. Passing is a claim
> about what was found, and nothing was found.**

### THE CENSUS, FIRST, because the number decides the shape

`measured` 2026-10-23 over every `tests/test_*.py` that derives a text
haystack (`read_text` / `inspect.getsource` / `fetch_log`, or a
`re.findall/search/finditer/match`) and then claims **absence or emptiness**:

```
116  matcher sites with an absence/emptiness claim
 77    GUARDED    -- the test establishes its haystack is the right one
 39    UNGUARDED  -- zero hits reads as a pass
```

**A FIRST, BROADER CUT GAVE 336 OF 535 AND IS NOT THE NUMBER TO RATCHET.** It
counted every anchor-keyed negative assertion, most of which are claims about
a **computed** value — `assert exposure == 0` after a real calculation — where
there is no anchor that can vanish and nothing for this mechanism to say. The
figure above is the matcher population only. Both numbers are reported
because the narrowing is the judgement, not an afterthought.

### FOUR INCIDENTS, ONE SHAPE, AND THREE DIFFERENT GUARDS

The shape is one: *a matcher that could no longer match passed silently.*

| incident | why it matched nothing | what guards it |
|---|---|---|
| `"\b870\b"` in a non-raw string | `\b` became **chr(8)**, a backspace byte | a scan that refuses zero hits |
| the ANSI colour filter | `fetch_log` strips ANSI **before** `extract` | a **measured effect on real input** |
| `pnc_scan`'s `KNOWN_INSTANCES` | its own table read as the evidence | a **planted finding** |
| `REMINDERS_REGISTERED` | a blanket rename; the name never existed | a **sentinel** in the same haystack |

**ONE HELPER DOES NOT COVER FOUR INCIDENTS, and that is stated rather than
papered over.** Two are mechanical and ship as `tests/conftest.py` helpers:

* **`anchored(hay, sentinel, what)`** — for a NEGATIVE assertion, where the
  needle cannot be its own anchor. `sentinel` is something known to be
  present; if it is absent the haystack is not the thing being checked, and
  the call raises **`UNEVALUATED, not clear`** rather than returning a flag. A
  guard that can be ignored is not a guard.
* **`must_match(pattern, hay, what)`** — for a POSITIVE scan, refusing an
  empty `findall`.

The other two cannot be: a filter's no-op and a scanner's self-suppression are
claims about **effect**, not about text. They need a PLANTED example, which is
what `ci_audit.PATTERN_EXAMPLES` and `calendar_marker_scan` already do.
`must_match` is explicitly **unusable** for a violation scan, where zero is
the goal.

### THE FOUR KNOWN-WRONG CONTROLS, EACH DRIVEN

**1 — the renamed constant.** The defect reproduced verbatim: `assert
"REMINDERS_REGISTERED" not in raw` **passes**, against a name the workflow has
never contained. `anchored(raw, "REMINDERS_REGISTERED", …)` reports
`UNEVALUATED`.

> **AND WRITING THIS CONTROL FOUND THE OTHER HALF.** Against **raw** YAML the
> *real* needle `REMINDERS_EXPECTED_MIN` is still present — in the comment
> that records its removal, at `reminders.yml:280`. **The thirteenth
> comment-blind instance**, found by the control rather than in production.
> So the real assertion needs **both**: `_code_of_yaml` to strip, *then*
> `anchored` on `reminders_selected=$sel` to prove the haystack. Two different
> failures, two different guards, and neither covers the other.

**2 — the backspace regex.** `chr(8) in broken` asserted, so the fixture
cannot silently lose the byte; `re.findall(broken, hay) == []` confirms the
pattern matches nothing; `must_match` refuses it. The corrected,
word-bounded pattern then finds the run id it should.

**3 — the stripped ANSI key.** Driven on the text `fetch_log` really returns:
`ANSI.sub` removes `\x1b[36;1m`, the colour-keyed filter is shown to be a
**no-op on that text**, and `must_match` on the key reports `UNEVALUATED`. The
shipped `strip_non_output`, keyed on the `##[group]Run` boundaries that
survive, is then shown to **remove lines from real input** and keep the output
line.

**4 — the scanner suppressed by its own table.** `anchored` **cannot** guard
this, and the control says so. The guard is a planted finding, and the
discriminator had to be measured: *"is it reported at all"* distinguishes
nothing, because the planted symbol lands in **some** bucket either way. What
the defect changed is **which**:

```
named only as a STRING in a KNOWN_INSTANCES-shaped table -> no_consumer     (correct)
called for real                                          -> orphan_cluster
```

so the control asserts the string-only plant stays in `no_consumer` **and**
that a real call moves it out — the second half being what makes the first
mean anything. A third plant with no table at all confirms the table is
inert.

**POSITIVE CONTROL** — a matcher whose anchor is present still asserts
normally: `anchored` returns the haystack **unchanged** (`hay is src`), the
real claim `"_ECHO_COLOUR" not in hay` holds, and `must_match` returns its one
hit.

### THE RATCHET, DRIVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

```
BASELINE_UNGUARDED = 39        # measured 2026-10-23; may fall, never rise
```

* **it bites**: a planted unguarded site fails it with `grew from 39 to 40`,
  the new site named, and the four clearing actions printed.
* **the clearing action clears** (CLR-2): wrapping that same site in
  `anchored` returns the count to 39 and the test passes. An alarm whose
  remedy does not change the predicate is not a remedy.

The population grew to 116 while the backlog stayed at **exactly 39** — the
four new tests are all guarded, which is the ratchet working rather than a
coincidence worth hiding.

### THE EXEMPTION LIST SHIPS EMPTY — 0 of 4

**The first draft's single entry was VACUOUS.** It named
`test_the_CENSUS_is_reproducible`, and the census only reaches the exemption
check for a site that reads a haystack **and** claims absence; that test does
neither (`>=` on two counts). It excused nothing and would have sat in the
list looking like a considered decision — **a vacuous check inside the
mechanism built to refuse vacuous checks.** Removed, not reworded.

So the cap test gained a third clause: an entry must name a site the census
would **otherwise have counted**. Driven in four directions:

| | result |
|---|---|
| a vacuous exemption | **REFUSED** |
| a real exemption with a real reason | accepted |
| five exemptions against a cap of four | **REFUSED** |
| a real site with a one-word reason | **REFUSED** |

*A list that absorbs the backlog makes the mechanism vacuous* — so the cap is
stated, at four, and nothing is in it.

### TWO THINGS FOUND BY BUILDING THIS, NOT BY LOOKING FOR THEM

* **`reminders.yml:280`** — the thirteenth comment-blind instance, above.
* **`must_match`'s own docstring was non-raw**, so the two characters it
  quotes had become `chr(8)`: **the record of the backspace bug was written
  in backspace**, and a grep for it would have found nothing. Marked `r"""`,
  with a test asserting the docstring contains backslash-`b` and **not**
  `chr(8)`.

### AND YESTERDAY'S RATCHET CAUGHT TODAY'S FILE

The `code_of` census went `raw 48 -> 49` on this file and **failed the gating
selection**. The site was
`test_the_RULE_is_RECORDED_beside_the_guards`, and it is an **attribution
artefact**: its only negative claim is `chr(8) not in doc`, against a
`__doc__` **object**, not file text — so `code_of` is inapplicable, and its
positive claims are deliberately against raw text because the thing being
checked *is* prose in comments.

**Split into its own test rather than exempted.** An exemption would have
spent one of four slots on an artefact. `raw` is back to **48**, and `code_of`
rose **5 -> 7** with this file's two correct sites.

### DISCIPLINE

Gating selection **2,522 passed, 10 deselected**; non-gating 8 passed, 2
skipped. Invariants 26 passed, count not cited. All seven workflow YAMLs
parse. No control characters in either touched file. `pnc_scan` **33 / 7,
byte-identical to HEAD** — verified by stashing. Fingerprint **UNCHANGED at
`s5.19 / cdec29`**; nothing under `src/` or `config/` is touched, so no
revision bump is due and `cohort_status`'s standing `BUMP` advisory does not

*Recorded 2026-10-23. `tests/conftest.py`,
`tests/test_matchers_assert_their_anchor.py`.*

## Decision paper for 2026-11-01 — measured 2026-10-23, not on the day

`docs/decision-2026-11-01.md`, with every figure reproducible from
`scripts/decision_paper_figures.py` (read-only, `assert db.is_postgres`
before anything). **No model built, no threshold fitted, no config changed.**
Fingerprint unmoved at `s5.19 / cdec29`.

### THE THREE ANSWERS

1. **What the models are worth:** nothing over the price. Five independent
   routes agree and the best-measured model in the repository **is** the
   price.
2. **How long to keep measuring:** more of the same changes nothing —
   **14.7 months** to reach the precision needed on a question already
   answered an order of magnitude away.
3. **Should the pick set change:** selectivity is **UNAVAILABLE**. There is
   no quantity to be selective on.

### THE STRUCTURAL FINDING THAT REFRAMES PART A

**`is_paper` is collinear with the ERA, not merely with `model_version`.**
Measured, not assumed:

* no `model_version` value takes both `is_paper` values — every stamped
  cohort is paper, every live pick carries `model_version = NULL`;
* **the last live pick is 2026-08-10 and the first paper pick is
  2026-08-11.** They share no day;
* **the experiment window contains ZERO live picks** (`n_settled = 1,359`,
  live = 0).

So the live ROI record and the experiment are two populations in two eras with
no overlap, and no change between them is treated as an effect anywhere in the
paper. Part D is therefore tabulated **twice**, once per population, rather
than pooled.

### AND ALL 172 CAPTURED CLOSES ARE PAPER

`measured` 2026-10-23: `late` 1,731 / `missing` 530 / **`captured` 172** /
`pending` 28. Of the 172, **171 are paper + valid evidence and one carries a
disposition**; the live population holds **zero**. So every CLV cell on the
live record is `UNEVALUATED`, and the first Part D run — on
`live + valid_evidence`, as the obvious population — came back `clv_n = 0` in
every bucket. That is what sent me to look.

**COVERAGE IS NO LONGER ZERO and the standing record said it was.**
172/1,325 = **13.0%** of the era in which capture was possible
(`pick_date >= 2026-08-14`); 7.0% of all saved picks. Memory corrected.

### THE DECISIVE NUMBER, AND IT IS A MULTIPLICITY FIGURE

Part D makes **1,000 pairwise 95%-interval comparisons** across 8 splits × 2
populations. **11 separate. 50 would separate by chance alone.**

> The number of apparently significant differences in the entire descriptive
> exercise is **five times below** what pure noise would generate.

Reported BEFORE the tables, so no table can be read as a signal. And the
answer to the only question Part D was permitted to settle:

* the **highest**-edge quartile is the **worst** on both ROI (−9.26% vs
  −5.07%) and CLV (−1.48% vs +0.24%);
* every ROI interval overlaps every other, so the ordering is not even
  reliably inverted — it is **absent**.

**Selectivity cannot help because there is nothing to be selective on**, and
that covers the model's edge, its confidence, the price, league, market, lead
time and the review's verdict.

*Also found: on the paper population `expected_value` has median **−0.0536**
and **1,034 of 1,359 picks are negative-EV by the model's own estimate**
(live: median +0.1126, 153 of 1,074). "Highest edge" means "least negative".*

### PART C DEMONSTRATES THE WIN-RATE QUESTION RATHER THAN ASSERTING IT

| band | n | win rate | break-even | gap | flat ROI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| short (<1.80) | 1,653 | 59.7% | 62.9% | **−3.2 pts** | −5.19% |
| medium | 614 | 46.9% | 48.9% | **−2.0 pts** | −4.73% |
| long (≥2.50) | 121 | 33.1% | 35.4% | **−2.3 pts** | −6.14% |

**The win rate is below break-even in every band**, by 2.0–3.2 points, while
the win rate itself nearly doubles across the range and **every ROI interval
overlaps**. The gap is the loss, and it is close to the **+1.85%** overround.

### PART B RE-MEASURED, NOT RESTATED

`baseline_revision = b2.884ee8`, 2026-10-23. **The sweep is still monotone to
w = 1.0**: +0.0430 (w=0) → +0.0163 (0.4) → +0.0079 (0.6) → +0.0024 (0.8) → 0
(w=1.0), and **at w = 0.8 the mixture is still detectably worse than the pure
price**. Every amount of model mixed in makes the forecast worse, in
proportion.

**A new reading of the same table:** the raw price *with the vig left in* is
statistically indistinguishable from the de-vigged price (+0.0022,
CI [−0.0003, +0.0046]). **De-vigging is worth about what the entire modelling
stack is worth.**

Both caveats carried: 3 effective folds of 5 on the PRICED subset, adjacent;
and the era's book mix was itself anomalous (4,836 1X2 books rejected).
**Three of the five routes carry no fold structure**, and the two weakest in
*generality* are the ones the conclusion mostly rests on.

### TWO FIGURES THE PAPER REFUSES TO QUOTE

* **Paired review-versus-model ROI is `UNEVALUATED`.** There is no
  `model_odds` column, so the model's leg has to borrow the FINAL pick's
  price — wrong **exactly on the 413 `CHANGE` picks the comparison is
  about**. Computed that way it gives +0.534% [−3.36%, +4.41%]; it is printed
  only to say it is not a figure.
* **The Claude review's monetary cost is zero, and that is the answer.** It
  runs on the Claude Code CLI on a **Pro subscription** — a shared usage pool
  at a fixed price, with the metered API only as fallback. There is no
  per-run dollar figure. The real units: **21.4 reviews/day** over 54 days,
  parallel bound 4 set by the pool, and a **pool share that is not recorded
  at all** — `UNEVALUATED`, not zero.

The measurable review figure, paired on CLV: n=132, **final − model =
+0.104%** CI [−0.2%, +0.5%]. **The sign has flipped** since the −0.101%
reading, on a larger n, and both sit well inside the interval. *The most
informative fact about this measurement is that its sign is unstable.*

### PART E — WHAT CAN STILL BE HIDING

| population | effective n | MDE (flat ROI) | vs +1.85% |
|---|---|---|---|
| all settled | 2,072 | +4.84% | 2.6× too coarse |
| live + valid evidence | 810 | +8.51% | 4.6× too coarse |
| paper + valid evidence | 1,281 | **+5.60%** | **3.0× too coarse** |
| captured-close subset | 170 | +15.94% | 8.6× too coarse |

So the honest claim is **not** "there is no edge" but **"no measurable edge,
and the measurement cannot exclude one three times larger than the one worth
having."** Part B is why the first remains the conclusion: the blend sweep is
a monotone result that does not depend on this power calculation.

At **23.4 picks/active day**: **+447 days = 14.7 months** to detect the
overround; **+164 days = 5.4 months** to halve the current bound.

### THREE RATCHETS CAUGHT THIS WORK, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THEM

The new script was refused three times before it could ship:

1. **`code_of` (yesterday's)** — `raw 48 → 49`, on an attribution artefact in
   the anchor test file. **Split, not exempted.**
2. **`pnc_scan`** — the script was committed half-built, with seven producers
   `main()` did not yet call. Finishing it cleared the backlog growth.
3. **the falsy-zero census** — **two real third-state conflations**:
   `if v.get("n_eff_needed_to_detect_overround"):` (0 is a measurement, not an
   absence) and `if not v.get("clv_n")`, which merged *"CLV was never looked
   at"* with *"looked at, no captured close"*. Both now counted apart, so no
   caller can read "0 buckets measured" as "CLV is zero".

**And the fifth `sys.path` entry-point instance**, hit writing this script —
with the finding that **the entry-point guard cannot catch it**: that test
runs each script with `--help`, which argparse answers before any work, so a
script whose `src.` imports live inside `main()` passes in **both** forms and
still fails in use.

**A printer bug also discarded a finished fifteen-minute computation** — a
`KeyError` in `_print` after every figure was computed, because the guard
asked `isinstance(dict)` and `pick_rate` is also a dict. The JSON is now
written **before** anything is printed: the expensive artefact is persisted
first and presentation cannot cost it.

### THREE STALE CLAIMS FOUND AND NOT FIXED

Hard rule 1 forbids changes in this stage, so they are recorded:

1. `src/evaluation/baseline.py` still prints **`CLV: UNAVAILABLE — no closing
   line is stored`** and sets `clv: None` with that note on every candidate.
   True on 2026-08-07, false now.
2. The sweep candidate is labelled **`market 80% + poisson/elo 19%`** —
   `int((1 - 0.8) * 100)` is 19. A label defect; the weight is correct.
3. The `sys.path` guard hole above.

### A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST DRAFT

The lead-time split measured `pick_date` (a DATE, so midnight) minus
`created_at` and came out **flat at −8 to −10 hours for every pick** — that is
the clock time of the daily run (`created_at` ≈ 10:52), not lead time. A
quantile split on it would have split the population by **nothing**, and four
near-identical buckets would have read as *"lead time does not matter"*. It
now joins `matches.match_date`; the real range is 4.2–8.8 h. The broken
version is kept as its own `run_hour` split, because that is a real question
— just not the one asked.

## `RESERVATION ENFORCED`, and the fourth card loss — 2026-10-28

### DECLARATION — `RESERVATION ENFORCED`, with the refusal that proves it

> **Enforcement is proved by a consumer being refused, never by reading a
> printed number.**

| direction | asked | granted | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **H1, before the fix** | 144 req = 288 cr | **144 = 288 cr** | overdrew its 168 reservation by **120**, and normal operation was left with `remaining() == 0` and a claim of 50 **refused** |
| **H1, after** | 144 req = 288 cr | **84 = 168 cr** | refused at exactly its allocation; a second claim of 10 → **0** |
| **normal, after** | 200 req = 400 cr | **116 = 232 cr** | refused at its remainder, reservation intact |

**The allocation was ONE-SIDED.** Stage 26 collapsed two constants into a
remainder; Stage 29 bound the **normal** side. H1's side was left to
`collection_stop` — which is a **pre-flight check**, read once before the run,
and therefore cannot bound what the run then claims. `remaining()` reported
the whole 400-credit pool to an instance allocated 168.

**One definition, two enforcement points.** `allocate()` now names
`h1_ceiling` — the *same* number at the point it is enforced, not a second
constant. `remaining()` caps H1 at the smaller of its allocation headroom and
what is physically left. `claim_requests` **clamps to `remaining()`** for both
consumers, so the reported ceiling is the enforced one on both sides, and a
test asserts the two ceilings sum to the pool.

#### And fixing it exposed a second defect, in the opposite direction

With H1's 168 spent, normal operation's `remaining()` read **64** instead of
its 232 ceiling — the reservation was withheld from the pool a **second time**
after H1 had already drawn it. `168 + 64 = 232` spendable of a **400** pool:
**168 credits unspendable by anyone.** That is Stage 26's "two independent
ceilings over one exhaustible pool" re-entering through the other door.
`reserved_from_me` now withholds the **unspent** reservation, and the
fail-closed direction is stated: when the attributed counter cannot be read,
withhold the **full** reservation — not knowing how much H1 drew must protect
its share, never release it.

**Driven against each other, both orderings:** each consumer run to refusal,
then the other asked for its full share. Each gets exactly its allocation,
the total is **400 of 400**, nothing stranded, and order does not matter.
Reverting the clamp fails four tests with *"asked for 288 credits against a
168-credit reservation and was granted 288"*.

#### `RESERVATION_EXHAUSTED` is reached from the WIRED path

Through `collection_state(session, since)` with real `odds_snapshots` rows —
not through `collection_stop` with a hand-supplied number. That is the
distinction Stage 29 named: *a parameter supplied only by the harness was
never wrong.* All five terminal states are driven and each gives a distinct
reason text.

The synthetic builder is **shared** with the analysis verification rather than
duplicated, and it builds the grain trap in on purpose: **60 qualifying SERIES
on 6 qualifying FIXTURES.**

#### The exact landing is now required rather than lucky

The claim grants whole requests, so H1's attributed spend only takes multiples
of `CREDITS_PER_REQUEST`, while the stop halts on `spent >= bound`. **A
reservation that is not such a multiple can never be reached** — nothing can
be claimed and nothing halts, so the state stays `COLLECTING` for ever. 168/2
divides; a test now requires it, and names the livelock.

#### One test encoded the blocker as a specification

`test_H1_sees_its_reservation_rather_than_having_it_withheld` asserted
`remaining() == 400`, reasoning *"its bound is `collection_stop`, not the
ledger"* — true about intent, false about effect. **Moved to the allocation
with the argument beside it, not relaxed.** Its fake quota also set `_store`
only, which is how a widened object raises `AttributeError` in a harness that
looked complete.

#### THE ENFORCEMENT IS INERT UNTIL THE WINDOW MOVES

`H1_RESERVATION_FROM/UNTIL` is still **2026-10-09 … 10-17**, so `h1_ceiling`
is **0 today and 0 on 2026-11-01**. H1 would be refused *entirely* — the safe
direction — but **the re-run cannot start until the window is moved**, and
moving it will fail the calendar-marked
`test_the_H1_RESERVATION_WINDOW_has_EXPIRED` by design. Stated here rather
than discovered on the day.

### THE FOURTH CAPTURE-GATE CARD LOSS — 2026-10-27, and it is mine

`tests/test_model_freshness.py::test_the_EXIT_CODE_is_0_FRESH_and_1_FINDING`
failed `assert 1 == 0`, which stopped `Run tests`, which **SKIPPED `update`,
`settle (pre-picks)` and `picks`**. The card was lost and recovered by a
dispatch at 10:25 the same morning.

**THE SHAPE.** The test built its fixture from a **frozen** module constant
(`NOW = dt.datetime(2026, 10, 22, 12, 0)`) and asserted on
`mf.main(["--quiet"])`, which computes `datetime.now(utc)` **itself** and takes
no `now` argument. One side frozen, one side live: as time passed the "fresh"
artefact aged past the staleness threshold and the exit code turned 1.

**WHY THE MARKER SCAN DID NOT REFUSE IT.** Its frozen-versus-moving logic is
right, but it learns which functions are clock-derived from **hand-maintained**
sets. `measured` 2026-10-28:

```
16  top-level functions in scripts/ that read the clock with NO `now` seam
 0  of the 16 registered in LIVE_NAMES / LIVE_QUALIFIED / SEAMLESS_READERS
```

*"A reader nobody registered is invisible"* is **already enumerated** in
`UNCOVERABLE`. This is that gap materialising, at a cost of one card.

#### No new detector is shipped, and the measurement is why

Registering the clock readers bluntly in `LIVE_QUALIFIED` took unmarked
findings **3 → 11**, and of the 8 new ones **1** was the real defect:

* `ci_alert.main` has **zero** clock reads — a bare-name false positive, killed
  by qualification;
* four `test_picks_bound_series` sites **stub the transport**;
* the `record_provenance` sites pass the frozen `NOW` **into** the
  `assess(now=…)` seam, so the clock never reaches the assert — the scan's own
  **"DOES NOT REACH"** ground.

Narrowing to the shape that actually cost the card — *a seamless clock
reader's result compared against a literal, with a frozen fixture feeding it*
— gives **zero instances today**, because `b9dd01e` made that fixture
clock-relative. **A guard with no findings is a regression guard, and saying
so is better than shipping one as a discovery.**

### Copilot's three commits, reviewed — all sound

| commit | verdict |
|---|---|
| `b9dd01e` | the correct repair above: the fixture becomes clock-**relative**, so both sides move together — the discrimination `test_BOTH_SIDES_MOVING_TOGETHER_is_NOT_refused` already calls legitimate |
| `2c537b1` | **a genuine repair of my own classifier.** `rc == 1` no longer means "a reminder is due", because `--continue-on-collection-errors` makes pytest exit 1 for an unimportable module too. It adds `UNEVALUATED` branches rather than guessing, and drives each one |
| `1a3b714` | replaces a literal deadline with `DEADLINE_MIN_BY_DAYTYPE["weekend"]`. **Not a tautology** — `SCHEDULE_DEADLINE_MIN = min(values)`, so it asserts **which day type binds**, and the two differ by 30 min |

### Two live repairs

#### `ci-audit` had been red for TEN consecutive runs

Every one alarming on the single 10-27 `daily-picks DID_NOT_RUN` — a resolved
past event that cannot be changed. Recorded in `RESOLVED_RUNS` against
`b9dd01e`.

> **The mechanism was not missing. It was not filled in.** For the second
> time, and the entry now says so.

#### A GREEN reminders run that decided nothing was invisible

`2c537b1`'s collection-error branch prints `::warning::` and **exits 0**.
`measured`: **none of the 35 registered patterns matched that line**, so the
run concluded SUCCESS, carried no marker, and was examined by nothing —
**PNC-1, a producer with no consumer.** A reminder module that cannot be
imported **never fires**, and firing on a date is this workflow's whole
purpose.

**It matters in four days:** `H1_RESERVATION_ACK_UNTIL` reddens on
**2026-11-01**, and a collection error that morning would have passed in
silence on a green run.

Pattern + example added (**36 of 36** self-test at load), matching the
**rendered** `##[warning]` form. The workflow's own source echo **cannot**
match it — there the count is an f-string placeholder, not a digit — which is
the lesson from the matcher that counted echoed script text. The finding fires
**unconditionally on the first occurrence**: unlike the producer-fell-silent
rules it needs no history, because **a missed date cannot be caught up**. It
is silent on 0 and on an absent key.

## H1 re-run readiness — 2026-10-28. Collection starts 2026-11-01.

Four commits: `49887a3` the window, `9c9c09f` the gate, `4316078` the
go/no-go, `29e1927` the FIFA check, the input guard and the analysis path.
Fingerprint **UNCHANGED at `s5.19 / cdec29`** throughout.

### `WINDOW MOVED` — 2026-11-01 … 2026-11-09 exclusive

Both dates **derived**: `FROM` is the TheOddsAPI monthly credit reset, because
a reservation carved out of a monthly pool must open when that pool does;
`UNTIL` is `FROM + 8 days`, preserving the pre-registered length exactly. Only
the position moves, so it is a reschedule and not an amendment to what is
collected. The 11-04 rate decision lands on **day 4 of 8**.

| date | `h1_ceiling` | `normal_ceiling` | sum |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-31 | 0 | 400 | 400 |
| **2026-11-01** | **168** | 232 | 400 |
| 2026-11-08 | 168 | 232 | 400 |
| 2026-11-09 | 0 | 400 | 400 |

The pin said *"Do NOT move the date"* and its own carve-out was *"a new
allocation with a fresh measurement"*. The first attempt is closed at n=4;
this is a new collection with its own pre-registration, so **the condition is
satisfied rather than overridden**. The docstring now refuses a *third* window.

**A name-keyed guard proved itself non-vacuous:** two sites assert that test's
name and **both failed** on the rename before being updated.

**Two seamless month reads given a seam.** `h1_credits_used` and
`credits_used` read `month_key()` off the **wall clock** while a claim writes
under the claim's date. In production both read the same clock and nothing was
wrong; the moment the window and the clock sat in different months the stop
reported `credits=0/168` **with 168 credits spent**, and the loop ran all
three rounds after its reservation was exhausted.

### `GATE INVERTED` — gating is opt-in

**Nine cards, four events**, and not one of the four tests says anything about
whether capture writes correct rows.

```
133 files    71 capture-critical, 62 not
2,547 gated  ->  1,671 gate, 911 moved out
gate wall clock  8m01s -> 3m05s
```

The criterion is **derived from the import graph**, not listed: a test is
capture-critical if it imports a module on the path that **writes a captured
row**. `src/models`, the features, reporting and evaluation are deliberately
out — a defect there produces a **wrong pick**, which is recoverable, where a
lost odds row **never backfills**.

**All four known-wrong controls pass.** Three of the four aren't
capture-critical; the fourth is (`test_empty_card_suppression.py` imports a
scraper inside one test, line 307) and the test that cost the card is
`calendar`-marked. **The inversion alone prevents 3 of 4; with the markers
kept, 4 of 4** — the two mechanisms do not cover each other.

**Both positive controls pass**, driven by planting the real defects: a
double-spending budget claim (6 failures inside the gate) and the two-way bet
admitted as a 1X2 authority (3 failures).

**Over-selection is accepted rather than gamed.** Any test that stands up a
synthetic database satisfies the criterion, so the gate carries 27 tests about
H1's own guards. The direction of the error is the safe one: over-selection
costs gate time, under-selection costs a card.

> **My first marker hook never ran.** Python keeps only the last
> `pytest_collection_modifyitems` and there were already two — one dead since
> the other absorbed its logic. `-m capture_critical` selected **nothing and
> reported no error**.

### `GO/NO-GO` — GO, from a labelled proxy

The forward fixture horizon is **zero days**, so 11-01→11-08 cannot be
measured. The proxy (2025-11-01…11-09, 291 matches, 23 leagues, 8 dates)
projects **n=70 against a floor of 33, on 8 of 8 dates**.

Ranked on `(dates, n)` **in that order** — spread is a constraint, not a
tie-break. T=09:00 reaches n=39 on only **four** dates and is the worse plan
despite clearing `TARGET_N`.

### `FIFA WINDOW CHECKED` — no overlap, one day of margin

The men's November 2026 window is **9–17 November**
(en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_International_Match_Calendar, fetched 2026-10-28;
corroborated by beinsports.com and the CONCACAF Nations League). The
collection window 11-01…11-08 is entirely outside it.

**The margin is one day, and that is luck recorded as luck** — the window came
from the credit reset plus eight days; nobody consulted the calendar.

**And it strengthens the proxy.** November 2025's window opened 11-10, so the
proxy week sits in the **same position relative to the break**: the eight club
days immediately before a November window. Aligned on this axis, not just on
the calendar. (The 2025 dates are search consensus only, labelled lower
confidence, used for comparability and never for a projection.)

### `INPUT GUARDED` — and the precondition was never wired

`h1_precondition.evaluate` existed, had four states and fifteen tests, and
**the collection loop did not call it**. The first attempt spent credits on
days whose card was 8, 4 and 1 fixtures and the reason was never recorded.
PNC-1 again — and its own passing tests are what made it look like a working
feature.

The reason is now captured **at the instant of the decision**, which is the
point: `is_fixture` is flipped later by the post-picks scrape, so a reason
re-derived afterwards is not recoverable.

**`OK` became `READY`**, and **"not pinned" had meant "none"**:
`league = ANY(:lg)` with an empty list matches nothing, so an unpinned run
reported `NO_FIXTURE_IN_BAND` on a card full of in-band fixtures while the
loop printed "ALL (not pinned)".

#### The start is a distribution, not a time

A `0 14` cron would have **started at 18:20–19:25** and missed the card
entirely. The nominal is the target minus the measured lateness.

`simulated` 2026-10-28, 20,000 trials, resampling the `measured` n=6 series
**independently per day**:

| cron | start window | p5 | median | P(n≥33) | P(n≥39) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0 9` | 13:20–14:25 | 27 | 46 | 0.891 | 0.867 |
| `20 9` | 13:40–14:45 | 29 | 46 | 0.809 | 0.735 |
| **`30 9`** | 13:50–14:55 | **45** | **69** | **0.999** | 0.995 |

**A thirty-minute shift moves floor-clearing from 89% to 99.9%**, because the
kickoff distribution is lumpy. Cron `30 9 1-8 11 *`, scoped to the window.

**The first cut was wrong in the pessimistic direction:** holding one start
time across all eight days gave a worst case of n=31 on 7 dates — below the
floor — for every candidate. That model is not the experiment.

#### The clearances, from both ends

* **LATE END** +358 min (weekday, mean+3sd); +389 at the observed max. The
  duration term is run **end** rather than time-to-picks, so conservative.
* **EARLY END** +60 min — the last round at 18:00 against the earliest in-band
  kickoff at 19:00.

**The early end binds at 60 minutes** and the late end has 358 to spare.
Moving T later buys nothing because the band moves with it.

#### "No overlap" is not achievable, so the cost is measured

`paper-trading-report` ran 14:02–16:49; `closing-lines` 00:31–23:50;
`reminders` 05:16–19:06. A **dispatched** daily-picks ended at 13:57 — three
minutes before T. With 3–5h cron lateness and nothing guarding the set, no T
guarantees non-overlap.

* **credit contention** — closed by the two-sided allocation.
* **observation contamination** — bounded, **and the grain is the whole
  answer.** At fixture-day grain the in-band data showed **67–103** distinct
  instants per fixture-day. At **series** grain — the unit
  `qualifying_triple` sees — all **1,939** in-band series-days carry **exactly
  one** and **zero** carry three. *I measured the wrong grain first and it
  said "serious contamination".* Residual: if H1 completes only 2 of 3 rounds
  a foreign instant could supply the third. Recorded, not closed.

### `ANALYSIS VERIFIED` — on a synthetic collection

The whole path now runs on a database with each step's output asserted. The
builder puts the `ρ=0.42` structure in on purpose: **60 qualifying series on 6
qualifying fixtures.**

**The clamp has its discrimination control:** 3 in-window and 4 post-window
fixtures; clamped gives 3, unclamped 7. Without it the clamp could exclude
nothing and the test would still pass.

**A third half-moved window found:** `h1_analysis.main`'s `--since` defaulted
to `datetime(2026, 10, 1)`. With the clamp at 11-09 the default population
would have been **10-01…11-09** — five weeks of normal-pricing snapshots
counted as H1 observations.

### Two pins, and a test that reached production

* **A selection returning zero is `UNEVALUATED`.** A gate that selects nothing
  **passes**, and that is indistinguishable from a clean tree unless the count
  is asserted. Pinned with a planted-two-hooks control.
* **Before optimising a duration term, establish that everything in it belongs
  there.** Both instances: 10-20 recovered 14.6 of 19.8 min with **no step
  getting faster**; 10-28 took the gate 8m01s→3m05s with **no test getting
  faster**.

> **A guard that fires in a later test names the wrong test.** The new wiring
> test drives `h1_collect.main()`, which calls `load_dotenv()` and put
> `DATABASE_URL` back after conftest stripped it. The test **passed** and
> poisoned the session — the failure surfaced as `assert not mgr.is_postgres`
> in a different file's fixture, six errors away. Nothing reached production
> because that guard held. An autouse fixture now fails the **offending** test
> and re-strips; driven both ways.
